name: LexiTrack English Core
description: General English vocabulary from A1 to C2, American spelling, with definitions sense by sense and example sentences: enough for IELTS 7.5, without rare words.

words.definition:
1. (indefinite article) used before a singular noun when you do not say which one, or when you mention it for the first time
2. (indefinite article) one
3. (indefinite article) each; per
4. (indefinite article) used to say what job someone has or what kind of thing something is
Note: Before a vowel sound, use “an” instead.
contexts: She has a dog and two cats.
There were about a hundred people at the party.
I go swimming twice a week.
She is a doctor.

words.definition:
1. (pronoun) a large amount or number
2. (adverb) very much
3. (adverb) often
contexts: She has a lot of friends.
Thanks a lot!
We go to the beach a lot in summer.

words.definition:
1. (preposition) on the subject of; connected with
2. (adverb) a little more or less than; not exactly
3. (preposition) used in “how ~…?” and “what ~…?” to suggest something or to ask someone's opinion
4. (adjective) (be ~ to) going to do something very soon
5. (adverb) in many directions or places; around
contexts: We talked about the film for hours.
The trip takes about three hours.
How about going to the cinema tonight?
The film is about to start.
The children were running about in the garden.

words.definition:
1. (preposition) in or to a higher place than something
2. (preposition) more than a number, an amount or a level
3. (preposition) higher in rank or importance
4. (adverb) earlier on the same page or in the same text
5. (adverb) (~ all) most importantly
contexts: There is a small window above the door.
Temperatures were above 30 degrees all week.
In the army, a captain is above a sergeant.
See the example above.
Above all, stay calm.

words.definition:
1. (preposition) from one side of something to the other
2. (preposition) on the other side of something
3. (preposition) in every part of a place
4. (adverb) from one side to the other, when you measure something
contexts: We swam across the river.
The bank is across the street from the park.
The news spread across the country.
The lake is two kilometers across.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the process of doing something to deal with a problem or to get a result
2. (noun) a thing that someone does
3. (noun) exciting events, especially in a film
4. (noun) fighting in a war
contexts: We need to take action before it is too late.
Her quick action saved the child's life.
I like films with lots of action.
Her grandfather was killed in action.

words.definition:
1. (noun) something that you do for fun or interest
2. (noun) a situation in which a lot of things are happening or people are busy
3. (noun) things that people do to get a result, often in a group
contexts: Swimming is my favorite activity on the weekend.
The kitchen was full of activity before the party.
The police are watching criminal activity in the area.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a person whose job is to perform in plays, films or television shows
contexts: He wants to be an actor in Hollywood films.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a woman whose job is to perform in plays, films or television shows
Note: Many women in this job prefer to be called “actor”.
contexts: The actress won an award for her role in the play.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to put something together with something else
2. (verb) to put numbers together to find the total
3. (verb) to say something more
4. (verb) to give a quality to something
contexts: Add some salt to the soup.
If you add five and three, you get eight.
“And don't be late,” she added.
The flowers add color to the room.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the details of where someone lives or works: the number of the building, the street and the town
2. (noun) the letters and symbols you use to send someone e-mail or to find a website
3. (verb) to start to deal with a problem
4. (verb) to speak to a person or a group, usually in a formal way
5. (verb) to write someone's name and where they live on an envelope or a package
6. (noun) a formal speech
contexts: Please write your address on the form.
What's your e-mail address?
The government must address the problem of housing.
She addressed the crowd from the stage.
The letter was addressed to my father.
The president gave an address to the nation.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a person who is fully grown, not a child
2. (adjective) fully grown
3. (noun) an animal that is fully grown
4. (adjective) behaving in a calm and sensible way, not like a child
5. (adjective) (of films, books, etc.) only for grown-ups, usually because they show sex
contexts: Tickets cost ten dollars for adults and five for children.
Most adult children live away from their parents.
Young birds look different from the adults.
Let's talk about this in an adult way.
This channel shows adult films late at night.

words.definition:
1. (noun) an opinion you give someone about what they should do
Note: You cannot say “two advices”; say “some advice” or “a piece of advice”.
contexts: My teacher gave me good advice about my studies.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) frightened; feeling fear
2. (adjective) worried that something bad might happen
3. (adjective) (I'm ~) used to say politely that you are sorry about something bad
contexts: My little sister is afraid of dogs.
He was afraid that he would fail the exam.
I'm afraid we might miss the train.

words.definition:
1. (preposition) later than something
2. (conjunction) at a later time than when something happens
3. (preposition) following or chasing someone or something
4. (preposition) next in order
5. (adverb) later
6. (preposition) (named ~) given the same name as someone
7. (preposition) (~ all) in spite of what you expected or planned
contexts: We went for a walk after lunch.
I'll call you after I finish work.
The dog ran after the ball.
Your name comes after mine on the list.
Soon after, it started to rain.
She was named after her grandmother.
It didn't rain after all.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the part of the day between twelve o'clock and the evening
contexts: I usually have a short sleep in the afternoon.

words.definition:
1. (adverb) one more time; another time
2. (adverb) back to the place or the state you were in before
contexts: Can you say that again, please?
It's good to be home again.

words.definition:
1. (noun) how old someone or something is
2. (noun) a period of history
3. (noun) the state of being old
4. (noun) (~s) a very long time
5. (verb) to become older, or to look older
contexts: What is your age?
We live in the age of the internet.
Her hair was gray with age.
I haven't seen you for ages!
Stress can make people age faster.

words.definition: 1. (adverb) before now; in the past (used after a length of time)
contexts: I moved to London two years ago.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to have the same opinion as someone
2. (verb) to say yes to something that someone asks or suggests
3. (verb) to decide something together with someone
4. (verb) to be the same as something; to match
5. (verb) (of food) to be good for you; usually with “not”
contexts: I agree with you about the plan.
She agreed to help me with my homework.
We agreed on a price for the car.
His story doesn't agree with the facts.
Spicy food doesn't agree with me.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the mix of gases around the earth that we breathe
2. (noun) the space above the ground
3. (noun) travel by plane
4. (noun) a feeling or a look that a person or a place has
5. (verb) to open the windows of a room so that it smells fresh, or to put clothes outside to dry
6. (verb) to show a program on television or radio
7. (verb) to tell people your opinions or complaints
contexts: Let's open the window and get some fresh air.
She threw the ball into the air.
We traveled by air.
There was an air of excitement in the room.
Open the windows to air the room.
The show will air next week.
Everyone had a chance to air their views.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a place where planes take off and land, with buildings for passengers
contexts: We arrived at the airport two hours before our flight.

words.definition:
1. (determiner) every one of
2. (determiner) the whole amount of
3. (determiner) during the whole of a period of time
4. (pronoun) everything; the only thing
5. (adverb) completely
contexts: All the students passed the test.
She spent all her money on clothes.
It rained all day.
All I want is some sleep.
He was all alone.

words.definition: 1. (adverb) in addition; too; as well
contexts: She speaks French and also a little German.

words.definition:
1. (adverb) at all times; every time
2. (adverb) forever; for all time
3. (adverb) again and again, often in an annoying way
contexts: He always drinks coffee in the morning.
I'll always remember that day.
She's always losing her keys.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) very surprising, especially in a good way; wonderful
contexts: The view from the top of the mountain was amazing.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) from or connected with the United States
2. (noun) a person from the United States
contexts: We watched an American film last night.
Many Americans visit Paris every summer.

words.definition:
1. (indefinite article) the form of “a” that is used before a vowel sound
2. (indefinite article) each; per
Note: Use it before a vowel sound, not a vowel letter: we say “an hour” but “a university”.
contexts: I ate an apple for breakfast.
The car was going at eighty miles an hour.

words.definition:
1. (conjunction) used to join words or parts of a sentence
2. (conjunction) used to show that one thing happens after another, or because of it
3. (conjunction) plus; used when adding numbers
4. (conjunction) used between two words that are the same, to show that something continues or grows
5. (conjunction) used after “come”, “go” and “try” instead of “to”
contexts: I bought bread and milk.
She opened the door and went in.
Two and two make four.
The music got louder and louder.
Come and see our new house.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) feeling very upset and wanting to shout because something is wrong or unfair
2. (adjective) (of a cut or a wound) red and painful
contexts: My father was angry because I came home late.
He had an angry red cut on his arm.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a living thing that can move and feel, such as a dog, a bird or a fish; often used for one that is not a person
2. (noun) a person who behaves in a cruel, rough or wild way
contexts: The lion is a wild animal.
He behaved like an animal at the party.

words.definition:
1. (determiner) one more of the same kind
2. (pronoun) a different one
3. (determiner) used before a number to mean “more”
contexts: Would you like another cup of tea?
This shirt is too small; can I try another?
We waited another ten minutes.

words.definition:
1. (noun) something you say or write back when someone asks you a question
2. (verb) to say or write something back when someone asks you a question or writes to you
3. (verb) to pick up the phone when it rings, or to open the door when someone knocks
4. (noun) a way of solving a problem, or the right result in a test
5. (noun) a reply when you phone someone or knock on a door
contexts: I didn't know the answer to his question.
She didn't answer my e-mail.
Please answer the phone.
There's no easy answer to this problem.
I knocked, but there was no answer.

words.definition:
1. (determiner) some; even a small amount or number; used in questions and after “not”
2. (determiner) one or some; it does not matter which
3. (adverb) at all; even a little; used in questions and after “not”
contexts: Do you have any questions?
You can take any seat you like.
I can't walk any faster.

words.definition:
1. (pronoun) any person at all; used in questions and after “not”
2. (pronoun) every person; it does not matter who
Note: Means the same as “anybody”, which is a little more informal.
contexts: Did anyone call while I was out?
Anyone can learn to swim.

words.definition:
1. (pronoun) any thing at all; used in questions and after “not”
2. (pronoun) a thing of any kind; it does not matter what
3. (pronoun) (~ but) not at all
contexts: Is there anything I can do to help?
I'm so hungry I could eat anything.
The test was anything but easy.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a set of rooms for living in, usually on one floor of a bigger building
Note: In British English this is usually called a “flat”.
contexts: They live in a small apartment downtown.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a round, hard fruit with red, green or yellow skin, white and juicy inside
contexts: She took an apple from the bowl.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the fourth month of the year, between March and May
contexts: My birthday is in April.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the language of the people of Arab countries, such as Egypt and Saudi Arabia
2. (adjective) written in this language or connected with it
contexts: He is learning Arabic.
She can read Arabic letters.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a part of a town, a country or the world
2. (noun) a part of a place that is used for a certain purpose
3. (noun) a subject or a type of activity
4. (noun) the size of a flat surface, found by multiplying its length by its width
contexts: This is a quiet area with lots of parks.
Please wait in the waiting area.
Medicine is her main area of research.
The area of the room is twenty square meters.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the part of the body between the shoulder and the hand
2. (noun) the side part of a chair that you rest this part of your body on, or the part of a coat or a shirt that covers it
3. (noun) (~s) weapons, especially guns
4. (verb) to give weapons to someone
contexts: He broke his arm playing football.
She sat on the arm of the sofa.
The country sells arms to its neighbors.
The soldiers were armed with rifles.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a soft, comfortable chair with parts at the sides to rest your arms on
contexts: He sat in the armchair and read the newspaper.

words.definition:
1. (preposition) in a circle, or on every side of something
2. (preposition) to or in many different parts of a place
3. (adverb) a little more or less than; about
4. (adverb) near; in the area
5. (adverb) so that you face the other way
6. (preposition) on the other side of something, by going along its edge
7. (adverb) present; available
contexts: The children danced around the tree.
We walked around the old town.
It costs around fifty dollars.
Is there a bank around here?
She turned around and smiled.
The shop is just around the corner.
Is your father around?

words.definition:
1. (verb) to get to a place, especially at the end of a journey
2. (verb) (of a thing) to be brought or sent to you
3. (verb) (of a time or an event) to come
4. (verb) (~ at) to reach a decision or an answer after thinking or talking
contexts: What time does the train arrive in Paris?
Your letter arrived this morning.
The big day finally arrived.
We arrived at a decision after a long discussion.

words.definition:
1. (noun) paintings, drawings and other things that people make to be beautiful or to show ideas
2. (noun) the activity or the skill of making paintings, drawings and other such things
3. (noun) (the ~s) subjects such as music, theater, painting and writing
4. (noun) a skill that you learn by practice
contexts: The museum has a large collection of modern art.
She studied art at university.
The government spends a lot of money on the arts.
Cooking is an art.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a piece of writing in a newspaper, a magazine or on a website
2. (noun) a single thing, especially one of a group of things
3. (noun) a part of a law or an official agreement
4. (noun) (in grammar) the words “a”, “an” and “the”
contexts: I read an interesting article in the newspaper.
Several articles of clothing were found on the beach.
This right is protected by Article 3 of the constitution.
“The” is called the definite article.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a person who paints or draws pictures, or makes other works of art
2. (noun) a person who sings, plays music or acts, especially as a job
contexts: The artist painted a picture of the sea.
More than fifty artists will play at the festival.

words.definition:
1. (preposition) in the job, the role or the form of
2. (conjunction) because
3. (conjunction) while; at the same time that
4. (adverb) (~ … ~) used to say that two things are equal in some way
5. (conjunction) in the way that
6. (conjunction) (~ if, ~ though) in a way that makes it seem that
contexts: She works as a nurse.
As it was raining, we stayed at home.
He sang as he cooked dinner.
She is as tall as her brother.
Do as I say.
He looked as if he hadn't slept.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to say or write a question to get information
2. (verb) to say that you want someone to do something
3. (verb) to say that you want something
4. (verb) to invite someone
5. (verb) to want a certain price for something you sell
contexts: Can I ask you a question?
She asked me to close the door.
If you need anything, just ask for help.
He asked her to the party.
How much are they asking for the house?

words.definition:
1. (preposition) used to show where someone or something is
2. (preposition) used to show a time
3. (preposition) in the direction of
4. (preposition) used to show a price, a speed, an age or a level
5. (preposition) used to say what someone is good or bad at doing
6. (preposition) used to say what causes a feeling
Note: The sign @ in e-mail addresses is read as “at”.
contexts: I'll meet you at the station at six o'clock.
The film starts at seven.
She smiled at me.
He drove at a hundred kilometers an hour.
She is very good at math.
We were surprised at the news.

words.definition: 1. (adverb) during the time when it is dark
contexts: I can't sleep at night.

words.definition:
1. (adverb) now, at the time when you are speaking
Note: A little less formal than “currently”.
contexts: I'm busy at the moment.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the eighth month of the year, between July and September
contexts: We always go on vacation in August.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the sister of your mother or father, or the wife of your uncle
contexts: My aunt lives in Scotland with her two children.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the country and continent between the Indian Ocean and the Pacific Ocean, whose capital is Canberra
contexts: Sydney is in Australia.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) from or connected with Australia
2. (noun) a person from Australia
contexts: She is Australian.
Many Australians live near the coast.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the season between summer and winter, when the leaves fall from the trees
Note: In American English it is usually called “fall”.
contexts: The leaves turn brown in autumn.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a wide street in a town, often with trees on both sides
2. (noun) a way of making progress or of getting a result
contexts: They have a shop on Fifth Avenue.
We have tried every avenue, but nothing has worked.

words.definition:
1. (adverb) to another place, further from someone or something
2. (adverb) at a certain distance from a place
3. (adverb) not at home or at work
4. (adverb) into a safe place or the place where something usually goes
5. (adverb) so that something disappears or is used up
6. (adverb) in the future; at a distance in time
7. (adverb) (of a sports game) played at the other team's ground
contexts: Go away and leave me alone!
The beach is two kilometers away.
She's away on vacation this week.
Put your toys away.
The music slowly faded away.
My birthday is only a week away.
Our team is playing away on Saturday.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a very young child, especially one who cannot walk or talk yet
2. (noun) a very young animal
3. (noun) the youngest person in a family
4. (noun) a person who cries or complains like a small child
5. (noun) (informal) a word for someone you love, such as your husband, wife or partner
contexts: The baby is sleeping in her room.
The cat had three babies last week.
She's the baby of the family.
Don't be such a baby!
I miss you, baby.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the part of your body between your neck and your bottom, on the other side from your chest
2. (noun) the part of something that is furthest from the front, or the other side of a page or a card
3. (adverb) to the place or the state that someone or something was in before
4. (adverb) in return; as a reply
5. (adverb) in or to a place behind you
6. (adverb) in or to the past
7. (adjective) furthest from the front
8. (verb) to support a person, a plan or an idea
9. (verb) to move backward, or to make a car move backward
contexts: I have a pain in my back.
We sat at the back of the bus.
She'll be back at five.
Can you call me back later?
Don't look back.
Back in 2010, I lived in Rome.
Use the back door.
Most people backed the new plan.
She backed the car out of the garage.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a bag that you carry on your back, with a strap over each shoulder
2. (verb) to travel cheaply, carrying your things in a bag on your back
contexts: He put his books in his backpack.
They backpacked around Europe after university.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) not good; not pleasant
2. (adjective) of low quality; not done well
3. (adjective) not able to do something well
4. (adjective) serious; severe
5. (adjective) harmful
6. (adjective) (of food) no longer fresh and not safe to eat
7. (adjective) (of a person or their actions) morally wrong; not behaving well
8. (adjective) (of a part of the body) injured or painful
9. (adjective) (feel ~) sorry or guilty about something
10. (adjective) not suitable or convenient
contexts: The weather was bad all week.
That was a really bad film.
I'm really bad at singing.
He has a bad cold.
Smoking is bad for your health.
This milk has gone bad.
He's not a bad person.
I've got a bad knee.
I feel bad about forgetting her birthday.
Is this a bad time to talk?

words.definition:
1. (noun) a container made of paper, plastic, cloth or leather, used for carrying things
2. (noun) the amount that a container like this holds
3. (noun) (~s) dark, loose skin under the eyes, often because you are tired
contexts: She put her books in her bag.
I bought a bag of apples.
He had bags under his eyes after the long night.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a shop where bread and cakes are made and sold
contexts: I bought bread at the bakery.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a small area with a wall or a rail around it on the outside of a building, above the ground, where you can sit or stand
2. (noun) the seats upstairs in a theater or a cinema
contexts: We had breakfast on the balcony.
We had seats in the balcony.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a round object that you throw, kick or hit in games
2. (noun) anything with a round shape
3. (noun) a large formal party where people dance
4. (noun) (have a ~) to enjoy yourself very much
contexts: The children are playing with a ball in the garden.
She rolled the clay into a ball.
Cinderella went to the ball.
We had a ball at the wedding.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a long, curved fruit with a thick yellow skin and a soft, sweet inside
contexts: He eats a banana every morning.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a group of musicians who play popular music together
2. (noun) a thin, flat strip of material that goes around something to hold it together
3. (noun) a strip of color or material that is different from what is around it
4. (noun) a group of people who do something together
5. (noun) a range of numbers, ages or prices
6. (noun) a plain ring, especially one worn by married people
contexts: My brother plays guitar in a band.
She tied her hair back with a rubber band.
The flag has a red band across the middle.
A small band of volunteers cleaned the beach.
Most of our customers are in the 25 to 35 age band.
He wore a gold wedding band.

words.definition:
1. (noun) an organization where people keep their money, and which lends money
2. (noun) the land along the side of a river
3. (noun) a place where something is stored to be used later
4. (verb) to keep your money in a particular organization of this kind
5. (verb) (~ on) to depend on something happening
contexts: I need to go to the bank to get some money.
We had a picnic on the bank of the river.
The hospital needs more blood for its blood bank.
Which company do you bank with?
You can't bank on good weather in April.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a large container that you fill with water and sit in to wash your body
2. (noun) the act of washing your body in this container
3. (verb) to wash someone in this container
4. (noun) (~s) a public building with pools for swimming or washing
Note: In American English the container is usually called a “bathtub”.
contexts: The bathroom has a bath and a shower.
She had a hot bath after work.
I'll bath the baby after dinner.
The Romans built public baths in the city.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a room with a bath or a shower, a washbasin and often a toilet
2. (noun) (American English) a toilet, especially in a public building
contexts: The bathroom is at the end of the hall.
Excuse me, where's the bathroom?

words.definition:
1. (verb) used to name or describe someone or something
2. (verb) used to say the place where someone or something stays
3. (verb) (there + ~) used to say that something exists somewhere
4. (verb) used to give someone's age, the time, a price and so on
5. (verb) to happen; to take place
6. (auxiliary verb) used with the -ing form of a verb to say that an action is going on
7. (auxiliary verb) used with a past participle to say what is done to someone or something
8. (auxiliary verb) (~ to) used to say what must happen or what is planned
Note: Its forms are am, is, are, was, were, been and being.
contexts: She is very tall.
Where are my keys?
There are many cafés in this street.
I am twenty years old.
The party is on Saturday.
She is reading a book.
The house was built in 1900.
You are to stay here until I return.

words.definition: 1. (noun) an area of sand or small stones next to the sea or a lake
contexts: We spent the day on the beach.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) very pleasant to look at
2. (adjective) very pleasant to hear or smell
3. (adjective) very good; done very well
contexts: What a beautiful garden!
She has a beautiful voice.
That was a beautiful goal.

words.definition:
1. (conjunction) for the reason that; used to say why something happens
2. (preposition) (~ of) as a result of
contexts: I stayed at home because I was ill.
The game was canceled because of the rain.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to start to be something
2. (verb) (what ~s of) used to ask what has happened to someone or something
contexts: She wants to become a teacher.
What became of your old friend from school?

words.definition:
1. (noun) a piece of furniture that you sleep on
2. (noun) the ground at the bottom of a river, a lake or the sea
3. (noun) an area of ground in a garden where flowers are grown
4. (noun) a layer of food that other food is put on
contexts: I usually go to bed at eleven.
The boat sank to the sea bed.
She planted roses in the flower bed.

words.definition:

words.definition:

1. (noun) knowledge of how or why something works or happens

words.definition: 1. (adverb) used to say that something is sad, bad or not what you hoped
contexts: Unfortunately, I can't come to your party.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) not kind or nice to other people
contexts: The staff were unfriendly.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) sad
2. (adjective) not pleased with something
contexts: She looks unhappy.
I'm unhappy with my exam results.

words.definition:
1. (noun) special clothes that all members of a group wear, for example at school or at work

words.definition:
1. (noun) a fixed amount used for measuring
2. (noun) one part of a course book or a course

The book has twelve units.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) joined together with the same goals

words.definition:
1. (adjective) (of a place) with things not in their right place

contexts: His room is very untidy.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) different from what is normal or common
contexts: It's unusual for him to be late.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to send pictures, files, etc. from your device to the internet

contexts: Upload the photos.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the address of a web page
contexts: Type the URL into the browser.

words.definition:
1. (modal verb) used to say that something happened often in the past, or was true in the past, but not now
Note: Questions and negatives: Did you use to …? / I didn't use to …. Different from be used to (= be familiar with).
contexts: I used to play tennis every week.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a person who uses a product, a machine or a service
2. (noun) a person who takes drugs
3. (noun) (informal) a person who uses other people to get what they want
contexts: The app has a million users.
He was a drug user for many years.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) normal; happening most often
2. (noun) (the ~) the drink or the food that someone always orders
contexts: I'll meet you at the usual time.

words.definition: 1. (noun) low land between hills or mountains, often with a river

words.definition: 1. (noun) a vehicle like a big car with a covered back, for carrying goods or people
contexts: They moved their furniture in a van.

words.definition:
1. (noun) (a ~ of) many different kinds of things

3. (noun) a type of something, for example a plant or an animal

words.definition:
1. (noun) a machine that carries people or things on roads, such as a car, a bus or a truck
2. (noun) a way of showing ideas or reaching a goal
contexts: No vehicles are allowed in the city center.

words.definition:
1. (noun) an opinion or a belief

5. (verb) to look at something carefully
6. (verb) to watch something on a screen

She views the job as a chance to learn.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a very small living thing that causes illness
2. (noun) an illness caused by this

contexts: She caught a virus.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the sounds you make when you speak or sing

words.definition:

words.definition:
1. (noun) fighting with weapons between countries or groups

3. (noun) strong competition between companies or groups

words.definition:
1. (noun) (British) a tall cupboard where you hang clothes
2. (noun) all the clothes that a person has

contexts: Hang your clothes in the wardrobe.
She needs a new summer wardrobe.

words.definition:
1. (noun) (British) clothes that need cleaning or have just been cleaned
2. (noun) the act of cleaning something with water
3. (idiom) (do the ~) to clean the dirty clothes
Note: In US English, sense 1 is laundry.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) used to tell someone to be careful because of danger

words.definition:
1. (noun) a line of higher water that moves across the sea

words.definition:
1. (adjective) not physically strong

words.definition: 1. (noun) a report that says if it will be sunny, rainy, etc.

words.definition:
1. (noun) (the ~) the internet, the place where you look at pages of information

words.definition: 1. (noun) a ceremony where two people get married, and the party after it

words.definition:
1. (noun) how heavy someone or something is

words.definition:

words.definition:
1. (noun) a round object that turns to move a car, a bike, etc.

words.definition:

words.definition:

words.definition: 1. (noun) a way of connecting computers and phones to the internet without wires

words.definition:

words.definition:
1. (noun) a careful study of something to understand it
2. (noun) a test on a substance to find what it is made of
Note: Plural: analyses.
contexts: The analysis showed a rise in sales.
The blood sample was sent for analysis.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to study something carefully to understand it
2. (verb) to test a substance to find what it is made of
Note: British spelling: analyse.
contexts: We need to analyze the data.
The lab analyzed the water samples.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a safe place where animals that were in danger or badly treated are kept and protected
contexts: She works at an animal sanctuary.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a place that looks after lost or unwanted pets until they find a new home
contexts: We got our dog from an animal shelter.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to tell people something officially
2. (verb) to say something in a loud or confident way
3. (verb) to tell people over a speaker in a public place, for example at a station
contexts: They announced the winner of the competition.
She announced that she was leaving.
They announced that the train was late.

words.definition: 1. (noun) an official statement that tells people about something
contexts: The pilot made an announcement.

words.definition: 1. (verb) to make someone a little angry, often by doing something again and again
contexts: His loud music annoys me.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) a little angry
contexts: I was annoyed that he was late.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) making you feel a little angry
contexts: That noise is very annoying.

words.definition:
1. (adverb) with a space or a time between two people or things
2. (adverb) not together; separated
3. (adverb) into pieces
4. (idiom) (~ from) except for
5. (idiom) (~ from) as well as; in addition to
contexts: The two houses are ten meters apart.
My parents live apart.
The old car fell apart.
Apart from Tom, everyone came.
Apart from English, she speaks French and German.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a large building with many separate homes in it
Note: British English usually says block of flats.
contexts: They live on the tenth floor of an apartment building.

words.definition: 1. (noun) (US) a group of buildings with many homes, and shared areas such as a pool or a garden
contexts: They live in an apartment complex with a pool.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to say that you are sorry for something
Note: British spelling: apologise.
contexts: You should apologize for being rude.

words.definition:
1. (noun) (US) a small amount of food that you eat before the main part of a meal
Note: British English usually says starter.
contexts: We ordered garlic bread as an appetizer.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a written request for something, such as a job or a place at a university
2. (noun) a computer program that does a particular job
3. (noun) the practical use of something
4. (noun) the act of putting a cream, paint, etc. on a surface
contexts: I sent my job application.
She downloaded a new application.
The application of new technology has changed farming.
The cream needs three applications a day.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a meeting that you have arranged for a particular time
2. (noun) the act of choosing someone for a job
contexts: I have a dentist's appointment at three.
We welcome the appointment of a new director.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to be thankful for something
2. (verb) to understand how important or serious something is
3. (verb) to see how good or valuable someone or something is
4. (verb) to go up in value
contexts: I appreciate your help.
You don't appreciate how hard it is.
You don't appreciate good music until you're older.
The house has appreciated by 20%.

words.definition: 1. (adverb) close to a number or an amount, but not exactly
contexts: The journey takes approximately two hours.

words.definition:
1. (verb) (of the police) to take someone away because they may have done something against the law
2. (noun) the act of taking someone away to the police station
3. (verb) (formal) to stop something from getting worse
contexts: The police arrested two men.
There were three arrests.
The drug can arrest the disease.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the act of reaching a place
2. (noun) the time when something new starts to exist or is used
3. (noun) a person or a thing that has just come to a place
contexts: We were met on arrival at the airport.
The arrival of the internet changed everything.
The hotel welcomed the new arrivals.

words.definition:
1. (noun) computer systems that can do things that usually need a human mind, such as learning or answering questions
Note: Often shortened to AI.
contexts: Artificial intelligence is changing medicine.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a piece of work that a teacher gives to a student
2. (noun) a job that someone is given to do
contexts: The teacher gave us a writing assignment.
The reporter is on assignment in Africa.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to help someone do something
2. (noun) (in sport) a pass that helps another player to score
contexts: The nurse assisted the doctor.
He had two goals and an assist.

words.definition:
1. (idiom) not more than
Note: Opposite: at least.
contexts: It will cost fifty dollars at most.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a machine, often in a wall outside a bank, that gives out money when you put in your card
Note: British English also says cash machine.
contexts: I took money out of the ATM.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the mood or feeling in a place
2. (noun) (the ~) the gases around the earth or another planet
3. (noun) the air in a room or a place
contexts: The restaurant has a friendly atmosphere.
The atmosphere protects the earth.
The atmosphere in the room was hot and smoky.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to fix or join one thing to another
2. (verb) to add a file to an email
3. (verb) (~ importance to) to think that something is important
4. (verb) (be ~ed to) to love or like someone or something very much
contexts: Attach the label to the bag.
I attached the photos to the email.
She attaches great importance to family.
She's very attached to her dog.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the way that you think and feel about something
2. (noun) (informal) a way of behaving that seems rude or too confident
contexts: She has a positive attitude to life.
Don't give me attitude!

words.definition:
1. (verb) to make people want to come to a place or do something
2. (verb) to make someone like or love you
3. (verb) to cause a particular reaction, such as interest
4. (verb) to pull something toward itself without touching it
contexts: The festival attracts thousands of visitors.
What attracted you to him?
The case attracted a lot of attention.
Magnets attract iron.

words.definition:
1. (noun) an interesting place or thing that people go to see
2. (noun) a feeling of liking someone, especially in a romantic way
3. (noun) a quality that makes something interesting or good
4. (noun) a force that pulls things toward each other
contexts: The castle is the main tourist attraction.
There was a strong attraction between them.
The main attraction of the job is the travel.
The earth's attraction pulls things toward the ground.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the power to give orders and make decisions
2. (noun) an official group that controls an area or an activity
3. (noun) (the ~ies) the people or the groups with official power, such as the police
4. (noun) an expert on a subject
contexts: Teachers have authority in the classroom.
The local authority built new houses.
He reported the crime to the authorities.
She is an authority on Chinese art.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a person who loves reading and reads a lot
contexts: She's an avid reader of crime novels.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a fruit with a hard green or dark skin, soft green inside and a large seed
contexts: I had avocado on toast.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) having won a prize
contexts: It's an award-winning book.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) knowing that something exists or is happening
2. (adjective) knowing a lot about a subject, and interested in it
contexts: Are you aware of the risks?
Young people are very politically aware.

words.definition: 1. (adverb) moving in one direction and then the other, many times
contexts: He walked back and forth.

words.definition: 1. (phrasal verb) to stop asking for something or saying that you are right, because people are against you
contexts: The government refused to back down.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to support someone or say that they are right
2. (phrasal verb) to make a copy of computer files so you do not lose them
3. (phrasal verb) to show that something is true
4. (phrasal verb) to make a car move backward
contexts: Don't worry, I'll back you up.
Back up your files.
Can you back up your story with facts?
Back up a little so I can get out.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a pain in your back
contexts: I have a backache from sitting all day.

words.definition: 1. (noun) traveling cheaply with your things in a bag on your back
contexts: She went backpacking in Asia.

words.definition:
1. (adverb) toward the place behind you
2. (adverb) in the opposite order from usual, from the end to the start
3. (adverb) with the back part at the front
4. (adverb) toward a worse state
Note: US English often says backward.
contexts: He took a step backwards.
Say the alphabet backwards.
You've got your shirt on backwards.
This plan is a step backwards.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a round bread roll with a hole in the middle
contexts: I had a bagel with cream cheese.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the place at an airport where you collect your bags after a flight
contexts: Collect your bags at baggage claim.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to cook food such as bread or cakes in an oven
2. (verb) (informal) to be very hot
contexts: She baked a cake for the party.
We're baking in this heat!

words.definition:
1. (noun) the ability to stay steady and not fall
2. (noun) the right amount of different things, so that one is not too strong
3. (noun) the amount of money in your bank account
4. (noun) an amount of money that you still have to pay
5. (verb) to keep something steady so that it does not fall
6. (verb) to give the right amount of time or attention to different things
7. (idiom) (on ~) after thinking about all the facts
contexts: I lost my balance and fell.
Find a balance between work and rest.
I checked my balance online.
Pay the balance by Friday.
She balanced the book on her head.
It's hard to balance work and family.
On balance, I think we made the right choice.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to say officially that people must not do or use something
2. (verb) to officially stop someone from doing something or going somewhere
3. (noun) an official rule that says people must not do something
contexts: Smoking is banned in restaurants.
He was banned from driving for a year.
There is a ban on hunting.

words.definition: 1. (noun) an arrangement with a bank where you keep your money and take it out when you need it
contexts: I opened a bank account.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a large farm building for keeping animals, food for animals or crops
contexts: The cows are in the barn.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the lowest part of something, which it stands on
2. (noun) the main place where a person or a company lives or works
3. (noun) a place where soldiers live and work
4. (noun) the main idea or part from which something can grow
5. (noun) the main part of a food or a drink, to which other things are added
6. (verb) (be ~d on) to be made using something as a starting point
7. (verb) (be ~d in) to have your main home or office in a place
contexts: The lamp has a heavy base.
The company's base is in London.
He works at an army base.
The town has a strong economic base.
This soup has a tomato base.
The film is based on a novel.
The company is based in Paris.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) simple, at the first and easiest level
2. (adjective) most important and necessary
3. (adjective) without anything extra; very simple
4. (noun) (the ~s) the most important facts or skills of something
contexts: I have a basic knowledge of French.
Food is a basic need.
The hotel room was very basic.
She taught me the basics of cooking.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the main facts or ideas from which something can grow
2. (noun) (on a … ~) the way that something is done or arranged
3. (noun) the reason for doing something
Note: Plural: bases.
contexts: The report forms the basis of our plan.
We meet on a weekly basis.
On what basis did you choose him?

words.definition:
1. (noun) an object that stores power for things like phones and toys
2. (noun) a group of large guns used together
3. (noun) (a ~ of) a large number of things of the same kind
contexts: My phone battery is low.
The army set up a battery of guns on the hill.
He had to do a battery of tests.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a fight between armies in a war
2. (noun) a long, hard effort to do something difficult
3. (noun) a competition or an argument between people or groups
4. (verb) to try very hard to do something difficult
contexts: Many soldiers died in the battle.
Her battle against cancer lasted years.
There's a battle for control of the company.
She battled the illness for years.

words.definition:
1. (adverb) in a very nice way that is pleasant to see or hear
2. (adverb) very well
contexts: She sings beautifully.
It's a beautifully written novel.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the quality of being very nice to look at or listen to
2. (noun) a very good-looking woman
3. (noun) (informal) an excellent example of something
4. (noun) (the ~ of) the good thing about something
contexts: The beauty of the lake took my breath away.
She was a famous beauty.
That car's a real beauty.
The beauty of this plan is that it's cheap.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a small hotel or a private house where you pay for a room and a morning meal
Note: Often written B&B.
contexts: We stayed in a bed and breakfast.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the time when you usually go to sleep at night
contexts: Nine o'clock is bedtime for the kids.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a flying insect that makes honey and can sting
contexts: A bee stung me on the arm.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a strong feeling that something is true or exists
2. (noun) an idea that a person thinks is true, especially about religion or right and wrong
3. (noun) trust that someone or something is good or will succeed
contexts: She has a strong belief in God.
He has strong religious beliefs.
I have great belief in her.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a metal object shaped like a cup that rings when you hit it
2. (noun) a thing that makes a ringing sound to get attention, for example on a door
3. (noun) the sound of a ringing that tells people something, for example at school
contexts: The church bells rang.
I rang the bell, but no one answered.
The bell rang and the students left.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a long seat for two or more people
2. (noun) (the ~) the place where players who are not playing sit during a game
3. (noun) a long table for working on
contexts: We sat on a park bench.
He spent the whole match on the bench.
The tools are on the work bench.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to make something become curved
2. (verb) to move the top part of your body down
3. (verb) (of a road or a river) to change direction
4. (noun) a curved part of a road or a river
5. (idiom) (~ the rules) to do something that is not quite allowed
Note: Past tense: bent.
contexts: Bend your knees.
Bend down and pick it up.
The road bends to the left.
There is a sharp bend in the road.
Can't you bend the rules just this once?

words.definition:
1. (noun) a part of a road that only bicycles may use
Note: British English usually says cycle lane.
contexts: Ride in the bike lane.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to cut into something with your teeth
2. (verb) (of an insect or a snake) to hurt you by making a small hole in your skin
3. (verb) (of a fish) to take the food on a hook
4. (noun) a small piece of food that you take with your teeth
5. (noun) a small amount of food; a small meal
6. (noun) a wound made by teeth or an insect
Note: Past tense: bit; past participle: bitten.
contexts: The dog bit the postman.
I was bitten by mosquitoes.
The fish aren't biting today.
Can I have a bite of your apple?
Let's grab a bite before the film.
I have mosquito bites all over my legs.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) (of a film, a photo or a TV) showing pictures in grey, without colors
2. (adjective) very clear and simple, with only right or wrong
3. (idiom) (in ~) written down
contexts: We watched a black and white film.
The problem isn't black and white.
I want the agreement in black and white.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) (of food) without a strong taste
2. (adjective) not interesting or exciting
contexts: The soup was bland.
The building is bland and ugly.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a jacket that is not part of a suit, often with the sign of a school or a club
contexts: He wore a blue blazer.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a romantic meeting between two people who have never met before, arranged by friends
contexts: They met on a blind date.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a small swelling on the skin with liquid inside, caused by rubbing or burning
2. (verb) to get small swellings, or to make something get them
contexts: I have a blister on my foot.
My feet blistered after the long walk.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a snowstorm with very strong winds
2. (noun) a very large number of things that come at the same time
contexts: We got lost in a blizzard.
I got a blizzard of emails after the holiday.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a large, solid piece of something with flat sides
2. (noun) (British) a large building with many flats or offices
3. (noun) (US) a group of buildings with streets on all four sides, or the distance along one side
4. (noun) something that stops movement or progress
5. (verb) to stop something from moving through or along
6. (verb) to stop something from happening or making progress
7. (verb) to stop someone from seeing something
8. (verb) to stop someone from contacting you online
contexts: The statue is made from a block of ice.
They live in a tall block of flats.
We live in the next block.
There's a block in the pipe.
A fallen tree blocked the road.
The government blocked the plan.
You're blocking my view.
I blocked him on social media.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) (of a pipe, a road, etc.) closed, so that things cannot go through
2. (adjective) (of your nose) full, so that you cannot breathe easily
contexts: The sink is blocked.
I have a cold and my nose is blocked.

words.definition: 1. (noun) one piece of writing put on a personal website
contexts: She wrote a blog post about her trip.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to explode, or to destroy something with an explosion
2. (phrasal verb) to fill something with air
3. (phrasal verb) (informal) to suddenly become very angry
4. (phrasal verb) to make a photo bigger
contexts: The bomb blew up.
Can you help me blow up the balloons?
He blew up at me.
We blew up the photo and put it on the wall.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a small, round, dark blue fruit that grows on bushes
contexts: She added blueberries to her yogurt.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the door at an airport where you get on the plane
contexts: Go to boarding gate 12.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a card that you must show to get on a plane
contexts: Show your boarding pass.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a weapon that explodes
2. (verb) to attack a place with weapons that explode
3. (verb) (informal) to fail badly
4. (noun) (a ~) (British, informal) a lot of money
contexts: A bomb exploded in the city.
The city was bombed during the war.
The film bombed at the box office.
That car must have cost a bomb.

words.definition: 1. (noun) (informal) a person who spends a lot of time reading books
contexts: She's a bookworm.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the line between two countries
2. (noun) a strip around the edge of something
3. (verb) to be next to another country or area
4. (verb) (~ on) to be almost a certain thing
contexts: We crossed the border into France.
The plate has a gold border.
Spain borders Portugal.
His behavior borders on rude.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) always telling other people what to do
contexts: My sister is bossy.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to annoy or interrupt someone
2. (verb) to make someone worried
3. (verb) (often with not) to make the effort to do something
4. (noun) trouble or extra work
contexts: Sorry to bother you.
What's bothering you?
Don't bother to cook; we'll eat out.
It's no bother at all.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a part of a tree that grows out from the main stem
2. (noun) a local office or shop of a large company
3. (noun) a part of a large subject or a large group
4. (verb) (~ off) (of a road or a river) to divide into a smaller part
contexts: A bird sat on the branch.
The bank has a branch in every town.
Biology is a branch of science.
A small path branches off to the left.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the name of a product made by a particular company
2. (noun) a particular type of something
3. (verb) to give a product a name and an image
4. (verb) to say that someone is a bad kind of person
5. (verb) to mark an animal with a hot iron to show who owns it
contexts: Which brand of coffee do you buy?
He has his own brand of humor.
The company branded the product as healthy.
The newspapers branded him a liar.
The farmer branded his cattle.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) not afraid of danger or pain
2. (verb) to go into a bad or dangerous situation without fear
contexts: The brave firefighter saved the child.
We braved the cold to watch the fireworks.

words.definition:
1. (idiom) the main way that a person or a business earns money
2. (idiom) (~ issues) basic and very important to most people
contexts: Teaching is my bread and butter.
Voters care about bread and butter issues like jobs and prices.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the air that you take into your body and let out
2. (noun) one act of taking air in and letting it out
3. (idiom) (out of ~) needing more air, after running or hard exercise
4. (idiom) (hold your ~) to stop taking in air for a short time
Note: The verb is breathe.
contexts: Take a deep breath.
She took a breath and jumped into the water.
I was out of breath after climbing the stairs.
Can you hold your breath under water?

words.definition:
1. (verb) to take air into your body and let it out
2. (verb) (~ in/out) to take air into your body, or let it out
3. (verb) to say something very quietly
Note: The noun is breath.
contexts: Breathe in through your nose.
Breathe out slowly.
“I love you,” she breathed.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the act of taking air into your body and letting it out
contexts: His breathing was slow and deep.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a woman on her wedding day, or a woman who has just got married
Note: The man is the groom.
contexts: The bride wore a white dress.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a green vegetable with a thick stem and many small green heads
contexts: Eat your broccoli.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a small, square, soft chocolate cake
contexts: She baked brownies for the party.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to look at things in a shop without a clear plan to buy something
2. (verb) to look through pages on the internet, or a book or a magazine
3. (verb) (of an animal) to eat leaves and plants
contexts: I browsed the shops.
She browsed the website.
The deer were browsing on the bushes.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a computer program for looking at websites
2. (noun) a person who looks at things in a shop without buying
contexts: Open the page in your browser.
The shop was full of browsers, but nobody bought anything.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a dark mark on the skin after you are hit or fall
2. (noun) a dark, soft mark on a fruit where it has been hit
3. (verb) to get a dark mark on the skin, or to cause one
contexts: I have a bruise on my leg.
This apple has a bruise.
She fell and bruised her knee.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a meal that you eat in the late morning, instead of breakfast and lunch
contexts: Let's meet for brunch on Sunday.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a woman with dark brown hair
2. (adjective) (of hair) dark brown
contexts: She's a tall brunette.
She has long brunette hair.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a ball of air or gas in a liquid or floating in the air
2. (noun) a small, closed world where people only meet others like them
3. (verb) (of a liquid) to make many small balls of air or gas, for example when it boils
contexts: The children blew bubbles.
He lives in a bubble and doesn't know how ordinary people live.
The soup was bubbling on the stove.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a round, open container with a handle, for carrying water and other things
2. (noun) (~s) (informal) a large amount
Note: US English also says pail.
contexts: He carried a bucket of water.
It's raining buckets.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to meet someone you know by chance
2. (phrasal verb) to hit something or someone by accident while moving
contexts: I bumped into my old teacher at the mall.
I bumped into the table in the dark.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to put a dead body in the ground
2. (verb) to put something in a hole in the ground and cover it
3. (verb) to cover or hide something so it cannot be seen
4. (verb) to try to forget a bad feeling or memory
contexts: He was buried next to his wife.
The dog buried a bone in the garden.
She buried her face in her hands.
She tried to bury her feelings.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a journey that you make for your work
contexts: He's on a business trip.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a large, round vegetable with thick green, white or purple leaves
contexts: Mum made cabbage soup.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the people who look after passengers on a plane
contexts: The cabin crew served drinks.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a young cow
2. (noun) the young of some other large animals, such as elephants and whales
3. (noun) the back part of your leg between the knee and the foot
Note: Plural: calves.
contexts: The cow had a calf.
The elephant stayed close to her calf.
I pulled a muscle in my calf.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) not worried, angry or excited
2. (adjective) (of the sea) without big waves
3. (adjective) (of weather) without wind
4. (adjective) (of a place) quiet and peaceful
5. (verb) to make someone less worried, angry or excited
6. (verb) (~ down) to become less worried, angry or excited
7. (noun) a quiet and peaceful state
contexts: Stay calm!
The sea was calm this morning.
It was a calm, sunny day.
The village is calm at night.
She tried to calm the child.
Calm down and tell me what happened.
It was the calm before the storm.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a planned set of actions to reach a goal, for example to change something in society
2. (noun) the work that people do to get votes before an election
3. (noun) planned activities to sell a product
4. (noun) a planned set of military attacks in a war
