Note: British spelling: globalisation.
contexts: Globalization has changed the way we shop.

words.definition:
1. (noun) (the ~) the world
2. (noun) a round model of the world that can turn
3. (noun) an object shaped like a ball
contexts: She has travelled all over the globe.
He spun the globe and pointed to Brazil.
The room was lit by glass globes.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) dark in a way that makes you feel sad
2. (adjective) sad and without hope
contexts: It was a cold, gloomy day.
Why are you looking so gloomy?

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to follow or chase someone to catch or stop them
2. (phrasal verb) to try to get or win something
contexts: The police went after the thief.
Are you going to go after the job?

words.definition: 1. (idiom) to have known each other for a long time
contexts: Tom and I go back years – we were at school together.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to go dancing at night in places where there is loud music and drinks
Note: Informal.
contexts: We went clubbing on Saturday night.

words.definition: 1. (idiom) to share the cost of a meal or an evening out equally
contexts: On our first date, we decided to go Dutch.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) (of a bomb or gun) to explode or fire
2. (phrasal verb) (of an alarm) to start ringing
3. (phrasal verb) (of food) to become bad and not good to eat
4. (phrasal verb) (of lights or machines) to stop working
5. (phrasal verb) to leave a place
6. (phrasal verb) to stop liking someone or something
7. (phrasal verb) to happen in a particular way
Note: The meanings about food and stopping liking something are mainly British.
contexts: The bomb went off in the street.
My alarm went off at six.
The milk has gone off.
Suddenly all the lights went off.
He went off without saying goodbye.
I've gone off coffee lately.
The party went off well.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to look at or think about something carefully, often again
2. (phrasal verb) to walk or move towards someone or something
3. (phrasal verb) (~ well/badly) to be liked or not liked by people
contexts: Let's go over the plan one more time.
She went over to say hello.
His joke didn't go over well.

words.definition: 1. (idiom) (of a video, picture or story) to spread very quickly on the internet and be seen by many people
contexts: Her video went viral overnight.

words.definition: 1. (phrasal verb) to live or manage although you do not have something you need or want
contexts: They had to go without food for two days.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) made of gold
2. (adjective) bright yellow, like gold
3. (adjective) very good or successful
4. (adjective) (of a celebration) marking 50 years
contexts: She wore a golden crown.
She has golden hair.
This is a golden opportunity.
My grandparents had their golden wedding last year.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the quality of being kind and doing the right thing
2. (noun) the part of food that is good for your health
3. (exclamation) (my ~!) used to show surprise
4. (idiom) (thank ~) used to show you are happy that a problem has ended
contexts: I believe in the goodness of people.
Don't overcook vegetables or you'll lose the goodness.
My goodness, you've grown!
Thank goodness you're safe!

words.definition:
1. (adjective) very beautiful or attractive
2. (adjective) very pleasant
Note: Informal.
contexts: You look gorgeous in that dress.
It's a gorgeous day.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to officially control a country or area and make decisions about it
2. (verb) to control or have an effect on something
contexts: The country is governed by an elected president.
Strict rules govern the use of the land.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the person who is in charge of a state or area, especially in the US
2. (noun) a person who leads a large organization, such as a bank or prison
3. (noun) a member of the group of people who control a school or hospital
contexts: He was elected governor of California.
She is the governor of the central bank.
The school governors meet every month.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to take hold of something or someone suddenly and roughly
2. (verb) to get or take something quickly because you are busy
3. (verb) to take a chance quickly
4. (verb) to get someone's attention
5. (noun) (make a ~ for) a sudden movement to take hold of something
6. (idiom) (up for ~s) available for anyone to take or win
contexts: He grabbed my arm.
Let's grab something to eat.
Grab the chance while you can!
The story grabbed the headlines.
He made a grab for the gun.
There are prizes up for grabs.

words.definition: 1. (adverb) slowly, over a period of time
contexts: The weather gradually improved.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) big and very impressive
2. (adjective) very important or ambitious
3. (adjective) very good or enjoyable
4. (noun) a thousand dollars or pounds
5. (adjective) (~ total) the final total after everything has been added
Note: The meaning "a thousand dollars or pounds" is informal; plural: grand.
contexts: They live in a grand old house.
He has grand plans for the business.
We had a grand time.
The car cost ten grand.
The grand total was 500 euros.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to officially give or allow someone something that they have asked for
2. (verb) to agree that something is true
3. (noun) money that a government or organization gives for a particular purpose, such as study
4. (idiom) (take something for ~ed) to expect something always to be there and not see how lucky you are
5. (idiom) (take someone for ~ed) to not show thanks to someone who helps you a lot
contexts: They granted him a visa.
I grant that it's not easy, but we must try.
She got a grant to study in Paris.
We take clean water for granted.
He takes his wife for granted.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) connected with drawing, design or pictures
2. (adjective) showing or describing something unpleasant, especially violence, in a very clear way
3. (noun) a picture or diagram, especially on a computer
contexts: She works as a graphic designer.
The film contains graphic violence.
The article includes a graphic showing the results.

words.definition:
1. (noun) pictures and images, especially ones made on a computer
2. (noun) the activity of making designs and pictures
contexts: The game has amazing graphics.
She studied graphics at college.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the feeling of being thankful
contexts: I'd like to express my gratitude for your help.

words.definition:
1. (verb) (of animals) to eat grass in a field
2. (verb) to hurt your skin a little by rubbing it against something rough
3. (verb) to touch something lightly while passing it
4. (verb) to eat small amounts of food often during the day
5. (noun) a small injury where your skin has been rubbed against something rough
contexts: Cows were grazing in the field.
I fell and grazed my knee.
The ball grazed the post.
I tend to graze instead of having proper meals.
It's only a graze.

words.definition: 1. (adverb) very much
contexts: Your help is greatly appreciated.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a building made of glass for growing plants in
contexts: We grow tomatoes in the greenhouse.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the warming of the earth because gases in the air trap heat from the sun
contexts: Carbon dioxide adds to the greenhouse effect.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a gas in the air, such as carbon dioxide, that traps heat around the earth and makes it warmer
contexts: Cars produce greenhouse gases.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) so exciting that you want to keep watching or reading
contexts: It's a gripping story.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to make a long, low sound because you are in pain, unhappy or annoyed
2. (verb) to make a long, low sound like something heavy pressing on it
3. (noun) a long, low sound of pain, unhappiness or annoyance
contexts: He groaned with pain.
The old floor groaned under our feet.
She let out a groan.

words.definition:
1. (noun) (~ies) food and other things for the home that you buy in a shop
2. (noun) a shop that sells food and other things for the home
Note: In American English, a grocery store is a supermarket.
contexts: I need to buy some groceries.
She runs a small grocery.

words.definition: 1. (phrasal verb) to slowly become less close to someone, for example because your interests change
contexts: We were best friends at school, but we've grown apart.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to become too big to wear clothes or shoes
2. (phrasal verb) to stop doing something as you get older
3. (phrasal verb) to develop from something
contexts: He's already grown out of his new shoes.
She used to bite her nails, but she grew out of it.
The business grew out of a small hobby.

words.definition:
1. (verb) (of an animal) to make a low, angry sound in the throat
2. (verb) to say something in a low, angry voice
3. (noun) a low, angry sound
contexts: The dog growled at the stranger.
“Go away,” he growled.
The bear gave a loud growl.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to complain about something in an unhappy way, often quietly
2. (verb) to make a low, deep sound
3. (noun) a complaint
contexts: He's always grumbling about his job.
My stomach was grumbling.
I've heard a few grumbles about the food.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to promise that something will happen or is true
2. (verb) to make something certain to happen
3. (verb) to promise in writing to repair or replace something if it breaks
4. (noun) a written promise that a company will repair or replace a product if it breaks
5. (noun) a promise or something that makes another thing certain
contexts: I can't guarantee that he'll come.
Money doesn't guarantee happiness.
The watch is guaranteed for two years.
The TV comes with a two-year guarantee.
There's no guarantee that it will work.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a rule or piece of advice about how to do something
contexts: Follow these guidelines when you write your essay.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the natural place where a particular animal or plant lives
contexts: Pandas are losing their natural habitat.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a person who secretly gets into other people's computer systems to steal information or cause damage
2. (noun) a person who is very good at writing computer programs
contexts: Hackers stole the details of thousands of customers.
He's a talented hacker who loves solving problems.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the activity of secretly getting into other people's computer systems to steal information or cause damage
contexts: He was arrested for hacking.

words.definition: 1. (verb) to argue with a seller to make the price lower
contexts: We haggled over the price of the carpet.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a hotel stay where breakfast and dinner are included in the price
Note: Mainly British.
contexts: We booked a room with half board.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to give something to someone, often because they ask or order you to
2. (phrasal verb) to give power or responsibility to someone else
3. (phrasal verb) to give a person to the police or another authority
contexts: The robber told him to hand over his wallet.
The old manager will hand over to his deputy next month.
They handed the thief over to the police.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to deal with a situation, problem or person
2. (verb) to touch, hold or move something with your hands
3. (verb) to be responsible for something
4. (noun) the part of a door, window or drawer that you use to open it
5. (noun) the part of an object that you hold
6. (idiom) (fly off the ~) to suddenly become very angry
7. (idiom) (get a ~ on) to start to understand or control something
contexts: She handled the situation very well.
Please handle the glasses with care.
Our office handles all the bookings.
The door handle is broken.
He picked up the knife by the handle.
He flies off the handle at the smallest thing.
I'm still trying to get a handle on the new system.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) useful and easy to use
2. (adjective) near and easy to reach
3. (adjective) good at using your hands to make or fix things
4. (idiom) (come in ~) to be useful at some time
contexts: This is a handy little tool.
Keep your phone handy.
He's very handy around the house.
Keep the box – it might come in handy.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to stay in a place without doing much
2. (phrasal verb) (~ with) to spend time with someone
3. (phrasal verb) to wait for something
Note: Informal. British English also: hang about.
contexts: They hang around the shopping centre all day.
Who does she hang around with?
We hung around for an hour, but he never came.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to wait for a short time
2. (phrasal verb) to hold something tightly
3. (phrasal verb) (~ to) to keep something
4. (phrasal verb) to keep trying in a difficult situation
Note: Informal.
contexts: Hang on a minute – I'm coming.
Hang on tight!
Hang on to your ticket.
The team hung on to win 1–0.

words.definition:
1. (noun) an area of water near the coast that is protected from the sea, where ships can stay safely
2. (verb) to keep a feeling or thought in your mind for a long time
3. (verb) to hide and protect someone who is wanted by the police
Note: British spelling: harbour.
contexts: The boats were tied up in the harbor.
She harbored a secret wish to be an actor.
They were accused of harboring criminals.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a situation that is very difficult to live in, especially because you do not have enough money or food
contexts: The war brought great hardship.

words.definition:
1. (noun) damage or injury
2. (verb) to hurt or damage someone or something
3. (idiom) (there's no ~ in) used to say that something is a good idea and will not cause problems
4. (idiom) (out of ~'s way) in a safe place
contexts: Too much sun can do harm to your skin.
The chemicals may harm the environment.
There's no harm in asking.
We moved the children out of harm's way.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) causing damage or injury
contexts: Smoking is harmful to your health.

words.definition: 1. (idiom) to share many interests, opinions or qualities with someone
contexts: We have a lot in common – we both love music and travel.

words.definition: 1. (idiom) to love eating sugary food
contexts: I have a sweet tooth, so I always order dessert.

words.definition: 1. (idiom) to go to bed earlier than usual
contexts: I'm tired – I think I'll have an early night.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) (of the air) not clear because of a light mist, heat or smoke
2. (adjective) not clear in your memory or mind
contexts: It was a hot, hazy day.
My memories of that night are a bit hazy.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to go towards a place
2. (phrasal verb) to be likely to have something soon, especially something bad
contexts: We headed for the beach.
The company is heading for trouble.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the main office of a company or organization
2. (noun) the place from which an army or the police are controlled
Note: Plural: headquarters. Short form: HQ.
contexts: The company has its headquarters in New York.
The police took him to their headquarters.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the person who is in charge of a school
Note: British. In American English: principal.
contexts: The headteacher wants to see you in her office.

words.definition:
1. (verb) (of a cut, broken bone or other injury) to become well again
2. (verb) to make a person who is ill or hurt well again
3. (verb) to make a bad situation or painful feelings better
contexts: The wound healed quickly.
She believes music can heal people.
Time heals all wounds.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a worrying time when you think you might be seriously ill
2. (noun) a time when many people worry that something is dangerous to eat or use
contexts: After a health scare last year, he stopped smoking.
There was a health scare about the meat.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) careful about what you eat and do so that you stay well
contexts: More people are becoming health-conscious and eating less sugar.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the service of looking after people's medical needs
Note: Also written: health care.
contexts: Everyone should have access to good healthcare.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the ability to notice sounds with your ears
2. (noun) an official meeting where people listen to facts about a case, especially in a court
3. (idiom) (give someone a fair ~) to listen to someone's opinion fairly
4. (idiom) (in/within ~) near enough to be heard
contexts: My grandfather's hearing is getting worse.
The court hearing is next week.
Please give me a fair hearing.
Don't talk about it within her hearing.

words.definition:
1. (noun) (in some religions) the place where God lives and where good people go after they die
2. (noun) a very pleasant place or situation
3. (exclamation) (good ~s! / ~s!) used to show surprise
4. (idiom) (for ~'s sake) used to show you are annoyed
5. (idiom) (thank ~) used to show you are happy that a problem has ended
Note: When it means the place where God lives, it often starts with a capital letter.
contexts: She believes her mother is in heaven.
This beach is heaven.
Good heavens! What happened here?
For heaven's sake, be quiet!
Thank heaven you're home!

words.definition: 1. (noun) a small brown animal covered in sharp spikes, that can roll into a ball
contexts: A hedgehog came into our garden at night.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the back part of your foot
2. (noun) the part of a shoe or sock under or around the back of your foot
3. (noun) the raised part on the bottom of a shoe at the back
4. (noun) (~s) shoes with high raised parts at the back
5. (idiom) (on the ~s of) very soon after something
contexts: I've got a blister on my heel.
There's a hole in the heel of my sock.
She can't walk in high heels.
She wore heels to the party.
The news came on the heels of another disaster.

words.definition:
1. (noun) (in some religions) the place where bad people are believed to go after they die and suffer
2. (noun) a very bad or unpleasant situation
3. (exclamation) used to show anger or to make words stronger
4. (idiom) (a ~ of a) used to make a noun stronger, in a good or bad way
Note: The meanings as an exclamation and "a hell of a" are rude to some people.
contexts: He believes that bad people go to hell.
The journey was hell.
What the hell are you doing?
We had a hell of a time.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a hard hat that protects your head
contexts: Always wear a helmet when you ride a bike.

words.definition:
1. (adverb) for this reason
2. (adverb) from now
Note: Formal.
contexts: The town is near the sea, hence its name, Seaview.
The new rules come into force two weeks hence.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a plant whose leaves are used in cooking to add taste
2. (noun) a plant used to make medicine
Note: In American English, the "h" is not pronounced.
contexts: Add some fresh herbs, like basil and parsley.
She uses herbs to treat colds.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to stop for a moment before you do or say something, because you are not sure or are nervous
2. (verb) (not ~ to) used to say that someone should feel free to do something
contexts: She hesitated before answering.
Don't hesitate to call me if you need help.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) in a place where it cannot be seen or found easily
2. (adjective) secret or not easy to notice
contexts: There's a hidden door behind the bookcase.
Watch out for hidden costs.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a large main road that connects cities
2. (noun) any public road
Note: Mainly American. In British English, a large fast road is a motorway.
contexts: We drove along the highway for hours.
Drivers must follow the rules of the highway.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a path for long walks in the countryside or mountains
contexts: We followed a hiking trail through the forest.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) extremely funny
contexts: The film was hilarious.

words.definition:
1. (noun) one of the two parts at the sides of your body between the top of your legs and your waist
2. (adjective) fashionable and modern
Note: The adjective is informal.
contexts: She stood with her hands on her hips.
It's a hip new bar in the city centre.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to make a long "s" sound, like a snake
2. (verb) to say something in a quiet, angry voice
3. (verb) to make a long "s" sound to show you do not like someone, for example a speaker
4. (noun) a long "s" sound
contexts: The snake hissed.
“Be quiet!” she hissed.
The crowd hissed at the referee.
I heard the hiss of gas.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a person who studies or writes about the past
contexts: Historians disagree about the causes of the war.

words.definition:
1. (noun) an accident in which a driver hurts someone and then drives away without stopping
Note: Also written: hit-and-run.
contexts: He was killed in a hit and run.

words.definition:
1. (idiom) to like each other as soon as you meet
Note: Informal.
contexts: We hit it off immediately.

words.definition:
1. (idiom) to go shopping
Note: Informal.
contexts: Let's hit the shops this weekend.

words.definition:
1. (idiom) to go out in a city to have fun, for example at bars, restaurants and clubs
Note: Informal.
contexts: After the exams, we hit the town to celebrate.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to stop yourself from showing a feeling
2. (phrasal verb) to stop someone or something from moving forward or making progress
3. (phrasal verb) to not tell someone everything you know
4. (phrasal verb) to not do something because you are not sure or afraid
contexts: She tried to hold back her tears.
The police held back the crowd.
I think he's holding something back.
Don't hold back – tell me what you really think.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to make someone or something late
2. (phrasal verb) to raise something in the air
3. (phrasal verb) to support something so that it does not fall
4. (phrasal verb) to steal from a bank, shop or person using a gun or other weapon
5. (phrasal verb) to stay strong or in good condition
6. (phrasal verb) (~ as) to show someone or something as a good example
contexts: Sorry I'm late – I was held up in traffic.
Hold up your hand if you know the answer.
The roof is held up by four columns.
Two men held up a bank this morning.
How are you holding up?
She is often held up as a role model.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) having an empty space inside
2. (adjective) (of a promise, words or feelings) not sincere or without real value
3. (adjective) (of cheeks or eyes) sinking into the face
4. (noun) a small area lower than the land around it
5. (phrasal verb) (~ out) to make an empty space inside something
contexts: The tree trunk was hollow.
His promises sound hollow.
He had hollow cheeks after his illness.
The house is in a hollow between two hills.
They hollowed out a log to make a boat.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) connected with God or religion
2. (adjective) very good in a religious way
contexts: The Bible and the Koran are holy books.
He was a holy man who helped the poor.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a person who is buying a house or flat
Note: Also written: home buyer.
contexts: Prices are too high for first-time homebuyers.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) having nowhere to live
2. (noun) (the ~) people who have nowhere to live
contexts: The fire left fifty people homeless.
She volunteers at a shelter for the homeless.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the problem of people having nowhere to live
contexts: The city is trying to reduce homelessness.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a person who owns the house or flat they live in
contexts: Homeowners will pay more tax next year.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the quality of telling the truth and not cheating or stealing
contexts: I admire her honesty.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to make the loud noise of a car horn
2. (verb) (of a goose) to make a loud noise
3. (noun) the loud noise of a car horn or a goose
contexts: The driver behind me honked his horn.
Geese were honking above us.
I heard a honk outside.

words.definition:
1. (noun) great respect that people have for someone
2. (noun) something that makes you feel proud and happy
3. (noun) the quality of doing what is right and having good values
4. (noun) a prize or title that someone gets for doing something great
5. (verb) to show great respect for someone, often with a prize or ceremony
6. (verb) to do what you have promised or agreed to do
7. (noun) (Your/His/Her ~) a polite way to speak to or about a judge
Note: British spelling: honour.
contexts: A party was held in honor of the president.
It's an honor to meet you.
He's a man of honor.
She received the highest honor in her country.
The soldiers were honored for their courage.
The company honored its promise.
Yes, Your Honor.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the hard part of the foot of a horse, cow and some other animals
Note: Plural: hoofs or hooves.
contexts: The horse hurt its hoof.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a curved piece of metal or plastic for hanging things on
2. (noun) a curved piece of metal with a sharp end, used for catching fish
3. (verb) to hang or fasten something with a curved piece of metal
4. (verb) to catch a fish with a curved piece of metal
5. (phrasal verb) (~ up) to connect a machine to something, such as power or another machine
6. (idiom) (off the ~) out of a difficult situation or free from blame
7. (idiom) (ring off the ~) (of a phone) to ring again and again because many people are calling
contexts: Hang your coat on the hook.
He put a worm on the hook.
She hooked the bag on the back of the chair.
He hooked a big fish.
Have you hooked up the printer to the computer?
You're off the hook this time.
The phone was ringing off the hook all day.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) (~ on) enjoying something so much that you want to do it all the time
2. (adjective) (~ on) not able to stop taking a drug
3. (adjective) curved like the letter J
Note: The first two meanings are informal.
contexts: She's hooked on that TV series.
He got hooked on painkillers.
The old woman had a hooked nose.

words.definition:
1. (adverb) used to say what you hope will happen
2. (adverb) in a way that shows you hope something will happen
contexts: Hopefully, it won't rain tomorrow.
The dog looked at me hopefully.

words.definition:
1. (noun) all the people who live together in a house or flat
2. (adjective) connected with a home and looking after it
3. (idiom) (~ name) a person or thing that everyone knows
contexts: The whole household was asleep.
Cleaning is just one of many household jobs.
She became a household name after the show.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a party for friends that you give when you move into a new home
contexts: We're having a housewarming party on Saturday.

words.definition:
1. (noun) buildings for people to live in, such as houses and flats
2. (noun) the job of providing homes for people
3. (noun) a hard cover that protects part of a machine
contexts: There isn't enough cheap housing in the city.
The government plans to spend more on housing.
The engine is inside a metal housing.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to sing a tune with your lips closed
2. (verb) to make a low, steady sound
3. (verb) to be full of activity
4. (noun) a low, steady sound
contexts: She hummed a song while she cooked.
The fridge was humming.
The city was humming with life.
I could hear the hum of traffic.

words.definition:

contexts: They are fighting for justice.
The criminal justice system needs to change.
The killers must be brought to justice.
The photo doesn't do her justice.
She is a Supreme Court Justice.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to give a good reason for something that other people think is wrong
2. (verb) to be a good reason for something
contexts: How can you justify spending so much money?
The results justify the cost.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) wanting to do something very much
2. (adjective) (~ on) liking someone or something very much
3. (adjective) very interested and enthusiastic
4. (adjective) (of the senses) very good
Note: Mainly British.
contexts: She's keen to start her new job.
He's keen on football.
She's a keen gardener.
Dogs have a keen sense of smell.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to not tell someone something
2. (phrasal verb) to stop someone or something from doing something
3. (phrasal verb) to stop yourself from doing something
contexts: I don't want to keep anything from you.
The noise kept me from sleeping.
I could hardly keep from laughing.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to move at the same speed as someone or something
2. (phrasal verb) to stay at the same level as someone or something
3. (phrasal verb) to learn about the newest news or changes
4. (phrasal verb) to stay in contact with someone
5. (phrasal verb) to keep paying or doing something regularly
contexts: Slow down! I can't keep up with you.
Wages are not keeping up with prices.
She likes to keep up with the latest fashions.
Do you keep up with your old school friends?
He couldn't keep up with the payments on his car.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a small hut for a dog to sleep in
2. (noun) (~s) a place where people pay to have their dogs looked after while they are away
Note: In American English, a small dog hut is usually called a doghouse.
contexts: The dog was asleep in its kennel.
We left the dog at the kennels when we went on holiday.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) (of a football match) to start
2. (phrasal verb) to start an event or activity
3. (phrasal verb) to take your shoes off by shaking your feet
4. (phrasal verb) to suddenly become angry or start fighting
Note: The last meaning is informal and British.
contexts: The match kicks off at three o'clock.
The festival kicks off on Friday.
She kicked off her shoes and sat down.
He kicked off when they told him to leave.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to take a person away by force and keep them as a prisoner, often to get money for returning them
2. (noun) the crime of taking a person away by force
Note: kidnap – kidnapped – kidnapped (US also: kidnaped).
contexts: The businessman was kidnapped and held for a week.
The police are treating it as a kidnap.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the crime of taking a person away by force and keeping them as a prisoner
contexts: There has been a rise in kidnappings in the area.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a set of tools or equipment for a particular purpose
2. (noun) a set of parts that you put together to make something
3. (noun) the clothes and things you need for a sport or activity
4. (phrasal verb) (~ out) to give someone the clothes or equipment they need
Note: The meanings about clothes are mainly British.
contexts: Every car should have a first-aid kit.
He built the model plane from a kit.
Don't forget your football kit.
They were kitted out with new uniforms.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to destroy a building or wall
2. (phrasal verb) to hit someone with a car so that they fall to the ground
3. (phrasal verb) to hit someone so that they fall to the ground
4. (phrasal verb) to make a seller lower the price of something
contexts: They're going to knock down the old school.
She was knocked down by a bus.
He knocked his attacker down.
I knocked him down to $50.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to hit someone so that they become unconscious
2. (phrasal verb) to make someone sleep or become unconscious
3. (phrasal verb) to beat a team or player so that they must leave a competition
4. (phrasal verb) to make someone admire you very much
5. (phrasal verb) to stop something from working
contexts: The boxer knocked out his opponent in the third round.
The pills knocked me out.
England were knocked out in the semi-final.
Her performance knocked me out.
The storm knocked out the power.

words.definition:
1. (noun) work, especially hard work with your body
2. (noun) the workers in a country or company
3. (noun) the process of giving birth to a baby
4. (verb) to work hard, especially with your body
Note: British spelling: labour.
contexts: The job involves a lot of manual labor.
There's a shortage of skilled labor.
She was in labor for ten hours.
They labored all day in the fields.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a piece of equipment with two long sides and short steps between them, used for climbing up and down
2. (noun) a series of levels in a job or organization that you move up
3. (noun) a long hole in a pair of tights
Note: The meaning about tights is British. In American English: a run.
contexts: He climbed the ladder to fix the roof.
She's moving up the career ladder.
I've got a ladder in my tights.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the act of a plane or spacecraft arriving on the ground or water
2. (noun) the flat area at the top of a set of stairs
3. (noun) the act of arriving on land after a jump or fall
contexts: The plane made a safe landing.
Her bedroom is on the landing.
The gymnast made a perfect landing.

words.definition:
1. (noun) everything you can see when you look across a large area of land
2. (noun) a painting of a view of the countryside
3. (noun) the general situation in a particular area of activity
4. (adjective) (of a page or picture) wider than it is tall
contexts: The landscape here is beautiful.
She paints landscapes.
The political landscape has changed.
Print the document in landscape format.

words.definition: 1. (adverb) mostly, mainly
contexts: The success was largely due to her hard work.

words.definition: 1. (adverb) recently, in the last few days or weeks
contexts: Have you seen him lately?

words.definition:
1. (verb) to start an important activity or plan
2. (verb) to make a new product available to buy for the first time
3. (verb) to send a rocket or spacecraft into the sky
4. (verb) to put a boat or ship into the water
5. (verb) to start a computer program
6. (noun) the act of starting something or making a new product available
7. (noun) the act of sending a rocket into the sky
8. (noun) a large boat with an engine
contexts: The police have launched an investigation.
The company launched a new phone last month.
The rocket was launched from Florida.
The new ship will be launched next week.
Click the icon to launch the app.
The launch of the new website is in June.
Thousands watched the launch.
We took a launch across the bay.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to stop employing someone because there is not enough work
2. (phrasal verb) to stop using or doing something that is bad for you
3. (phrasal verb) to stop annoying or criticizing someone
Note: The last two meanings are informal.
contexts: The factory laid off 200 workers.
You should lay off the chocolate for a while.
Lay off him – he's had a hard day.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the position of being in charge of a group or country
2. (noun) the ability to guide and control people well
3. (noun) the people who are in charge of a group or country
contexts: The party has a new leadership.
He has strong leadership skills.
The leadership has rejected the plan.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the main part in a film or play
2. (noun) the most important part in an activity
contexts: She plays the leading role in the new film.
The company played a leading role in the project.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a printed sheet of paper, or a few pages, with information or advertising, usually given free
contexts: They were handing out leaflets in the street.

words.definition: 1. (noun) vegetables with green leaves that you eat, such as spinach, cabbage and lettuce
contexts: Eat plenty of leafy greens.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a group of sports teams or players who play against each other to see who is best
2. (noun) a level of quality or ability
3. (noun) a group of people or countries who join together for a shared purpose
4. (idiom) (in ~ with) working together secretly, often to do something wrong
contexts: They won the league last season.
As a cook, she's not in my league.
The League of Nations was formed in 1920.
The police officer was in league with the criminals.

words.definition:
1. (verb) (of liquid or gas) to come out through a hole or crack
2. (verb) (of a container) to let liquid or gas out through a hole or crack
3. (verb) to give secret information to newspapers or the public
4. (noun) a small hole or crack that lets liquid or gas out
5. (noun) liquid or gas that comes out through a hole or crack
6. (noun) the act of giving secret information to the public
contexts: Water was leaking from the pipe.
The roof leaks when it rains.
Someone leaked the report to the press.
There's a leak in the roof.
There was a gas leak in the building.
The government is trying to find the source of the leak.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to bend your body forwards, backwards or to the side
2. (verb) to rest against something for support, or to put something against something else
3. (verb) (~ on) to need help and support from someone
4. (adjective) thin and healthy
5. (adjective) (of meat) with little or no fat
6. (adjective) (of a time) difficult because there is not much money or success
Note: lean – leaned or leant – leaned or leant. "Leant" is British.
contexts: She leaned forward to hear better.
He was leaning against the wall.
You can always lean on me.
He's tall and lean.
Buy lean meat.
The company went through some lean years.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a person who teaches at a university or college
2. (noun) a person who gives talks on a subject to groups of people
contexts: She's a lecturer in history.
He's a popular guest lecturer.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a very old story that may or may not be true
2. (noun) a very famous person who is admired for their skill
3. (noun) the words that explain the signs on a map or chart
contexts: The legend of King Arthur is famous.
He's a football legend.
Check the legend to see what the symbols mean.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a curved piece of glass or plastic that makes things look bigger, smaller or clearer, used in glasses, cameras and other tools
2. (noun) (contact ~) a small, thin piece of plastic that you put on your eye to help you see
3. (noun) the clear part of your eye behind the dark centre
Note: Plural: lenses.
contexts: I need new lenses for my glasses.
She wears contact lenses.
The lens of the eye helps you focus.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to make someone disappointed because you did not do what they expected
2. (phrasal verb) to let the air out of something
3. (phrasal verb) to make a piece of clothing longer
4. (phrasal verb) to move something lower
contexts: I won't let you down.
Someone let down my tyres.
Can you let down these trousers?
They let the bucket down into the well.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to not punish someone, or to punish them less than they expected
2. (phrasal verb) to make a bomb or firework explode
3. (phrasal verb) to allow someone not to do a job or duty
4. (idiom) (~ steam) to do something to get rid of your strong feelings or energy
contexts: The police let him off with a warning.
They let off fireworks at midnight.
The teacher let us off homework today.
He goes running to let off steam.

words.definition: 1. (idiom) to relax and enjoy yourself, especially after working hard
contexts: It's the weekend – time to let your hair down.

words.definition:
1. (noun) an official document that shows you are allowed to do, own or use something
2. (verb) to give someone official permission to do or own something
3. (noun) (~ to) the freedom to do what you want
Note: In British English, the noun is spelled licence and the verb license.
contexts: Do you have a driving license?
The shop is licensed to sell alcohol.
The success gave him license to experiment.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the number of years that a person is likely to live
contexts: Life expectancy in Japan is very high.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a person who is lively and funny and makes a party or social event fun
Note: British English also: the life and soul of the party.
contexts: She's always the life of the party.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) able to cause someone's death
contexts: He has a life-threatening illness.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) lasting or continuing for the whole of your life
contexts: They became lifelong friends.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the time during which someone is alive
2. (noun) the time during which something exists or works
3. (idiom) (the chance/trip of a ~) a very special chance or trip that you will probably only have once
contexts: He saw many changes during his lifetime.
The battery has a lifetime of five years.
It was the trip of a lifetime.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the lamps in a room, building or street, or on a stage, and the kind of brightness they give
contexts: The lighting in the restaurant was soft.

words.definition:
1. (adverb) in the same way
2. (adverb) also
3. (exclamation) used to say that you feel the same as the other person
contexts: She left early, and I did likewise.
The food was excellent, and likewise the service.
“Nice to meet you.” “Likewise.”

words.definition:
1. (noun) a rule or fact that controls how much of something there can be
2. (noun) a weakness, or something you cannot do well
contexts: There are limitations on how much you can take on the plane.
Everyone has their limitations.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) small in amount or number
2. (adjective) kept within a certain size or amount
3. (adjective) not very great or good
4. (adjective) (with a capital L) used after the name of a company in Britain
Note: The short form of the company meaning is Ltd.
contexts: We have limited time.
The offer is for a limited period only.
My knowledge of French is limited.
He works for Brown and Sons Limited.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to walk with difficulty because one of your legs or feet is hurt
2. (noun) a way of walking with difficulty because one leg or foot is hurt
3. (adjective) soft and not firm
contexts: He limped off the field.
She walks with a limp.
The salad was limp.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the people who are performing at an event, or the players in a team for a particular game
2. (noun) a group of people standing in a row, so that a person who saw a crime can choose the criminal
3. (noun) a set of TV programmes or products
Note: Also written: line-up.
contexts: The festival has a great lineup this year.
She picked him out of a police lineup.
The new lineup of shows starts in September.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a unit for measuring liquid; there are 1,000 millilitres in it
Note: British spelling: litre.
contexts: The bottle holds two liters of water.

words.definition:
1. (adverb) really and exactly, in the true meaning of the words
2. (adverb) used to make a statement stronger, even when it is not exactly true
3. (adverb) (translate ~) word for word
4. (idiom) (take something ~) to understand words in their most basic meaning, when this is not what the speaker meant
Note: Some people think the second meaning is wrong.
contexts: The word "breakfast" literally means "to break a fast".
I literally died of shame.
The phrase doesn't translate literally into English.
Don't take it literally – he was joking.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) connected with books, poems and plays and the study of them
2. (adjective) (of language) used in books and poems and not in everyday speech
contexts: She's a literary critic.
The word "steed" is literary.

words.definition:
1. (noun) pieces of paper, empty bottles and other rubbish that people leave in public places
2. (noun) a group of baby animals born to the same mother at the same time
3. (noun) a material such as small stones that you put in a box for a pet cat to use as a toilet
4. (verb) to make a place untidy by leaving rubbish there
5. (verb) (be ~ed with) to have a lot of something, especially something bad
contexts: Please don't drop litter.
Our dog had a litter of six puppies.
I need to change the cat litter.
Paper cups littered the street.
The essay was littered with mistakes.

words.definition: 1. (phrasal verb) to get the money or food you need from someone or something
contexts: He's 30 and still lives off his parents.

words.definition: 1. (phrasal verb) to be as good as someone expected
contexts: The film didn't live up to my expectations.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) full of energy and enthusiasm
2. (adjective) (of a place or event) busy and exciting
3. (adjective) (of colours) bright and strong
contexts: She's a lively young girl.
The city has a lively nightlife.
The room was painted in lively colours.

words.definition:
1. (noun) (~s) how much money and comfort people have
Note: Usually used in the plural. Also: standard of living.
contexts: Living standards have improved a lot in the last 50 years.

words.definition:
1. (noun) something heavy that is carried by a person, vehicle or animal
2. (noun) the amount of work that a person or machine has to do
3. (noun) (a ~ of / ~s of) a lot of something
4. (noun) an amount of clothes that you wash at one time
5. (verb) to put a lot of things into or onto something, such as a vehicle
6. (verb) to put something into a machine, such as film in a camera or bullets in a gun
7. (verb) to put a program or information into a computer, or to open on a screen
Note: The meaning "a lot of" is informal.
contexts: The truck was carrying a heavy load.
Teachers have a heavy load of work.
There were loads of people at the party.
I've done three loads of washing today.
We loaded the car with our bags.
He loaded the gun.
The page is taking ages to load.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) carrying a lot of things
2. (adjective) (of a gun) with bullets in it
3. (adjective) very rich
4. (adjective) (of a question or word) having a hidden meaning, or meant to make you answer in a particular way
5. (adjective) (~ with) full of something
Note: The meaning "very rich" is informal.
contexts: The truck was fully loaded.
Be careful – the gun is loaded.
Her parents are loaded.
That's a loaded question.
The cake is loaded with sugar.

words.definition:
1. (noun) money that you borrow, usually from a bank, and pay back with extra money over time
2. (noun) the act of lending something
3. (idiom) (on ~) borrowed from someone
4. (verb) to lend something to someone
contexts: They took out a loan to buy a car.
Thanks for the loan of your bike.
The painting is on loan from a museum in Paris.
She loaned me her car.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a sea animal with a hard shell, eight legs and two large claws
2. (noun) the meat of this sea animal, eaten as food
contexts: The fisherman caught a lobster.
We had lobster for dinner.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to close all the doors and windows of a building with a key before you leave
2. (phrasal verb) to put someone in prison or another place they cannot leave
3. (phrasal verb) to put something valuable in a safe place with a key
contexts: Don't forget to lock up when you go.
He was locked up for ten years.
She locked up her jewellery.

words.definition: 1. (idiom) to be unable to get into your home or car because you have left your keys inside
contexts: Take your keys, or you might lock yourself out of the house.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a small house in the country, used by people on holiday or for hunting
2. (noun) a small house at the gate of a large building or park
3. (verb) to make an official complaint or request
4. (verb) to live in a room in someone's house and pay them
5. (verb) to become stuck somewhere
contexts: We stayed in a ski lodge.
The gardener lives in the lodge.
She lodged a complaint with the manager.
He lodges with a family in town.
A fish bone lodged in his throat.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a room or space under the roof of a house, often used for storing things
2. (noun) a large flat in an old factory or warehouse
Note: In American English, the space under a roof is usually called an attic.
contexts: Our old toys are in the loft.
They live in a loft in New York.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) sensible and reasonable
2. (adjective) following the rules of clear thinking
contexts: It's the logical thing to do.
She has a very logical mind.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a picture or design that a company or organization uses as its sign
contexts: The company's logo is on all their products.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) lasting or having an effect for a long time into the future
2. (adverb) for a long time into the future
contexts: Smoking can cause long-term health problems.
Long-term, this will save us money.

words.definition: 1. (phrasal verb) to think that you are better or more important than someone
contexts: She looks down on people who didn't go to university.

words.definition: 1. (phrasal verb) to try to find out the facts about a problem or situation
contexts: The police are looking into the case.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to read or check something quickly
2. (phrasal verb) to look at a place or thing to see what it is like
contexts: Can you look over my essay before I hand it in?
We looked over the house before buying it.

words.definition: 1. (phrasal verb) to admire and respect someone
contexts: He's always looked up to his older brother.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) not firmly fixed in place
2. (adjective) (of clothes) not fitting your body tightly
3. (adjective) free and not tied up or kept in a place
4. (adjective) not packed together or in a container
5. (adjective) not exact
6. (idiom) (at a ~ end) with nothing to do
Note: Don't confuse it with the verb "lose".
contexts: One of my teeth is loose.
She wore a loose dress.
The dog got loose.
The tea is sold loose.
It's a loose translation.
Call me if you're at a loose end this weekend.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a man of high social rank, for example in old times, who owned land and had power
2. (noun) (with a capital L) a title for a man of high rank in Britain
3. (noun) (with a capital L) a name for God or Christ
4. (exclamation) (oh ~! / good ~!) used to show surprise or worry
contexts: The lord lived in a big castle.
Lord Smith spoke in the debate.
Praise the Lord!
Oh Lord! I forgot her birthday!

words.definition: 1. (idiom) to suddenly become too afraid to do something
contexts: Don't lose your nerve now – you can do it!

words.definition: 1. (idiom) to suddenly become very angry
contexts: Try not to lose your temper with the children.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a game in which people buy tickets with numbers on them and win money if their numbers are chosen
2. (noun) a situation in which success depends on luck
contexts: He won a million dollars on the lottery.
Finding a good flat is a bit of a lottery.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to move something down
2. (verb) to make something less in amount, level or strength
3. (adjective) below something else, or at the bottom of something
4. (idiom) (~ yourself) to do something that makes people respect you less
contexts: They lowered the boat into the water.
The shop has lowered its prices.
My lower back hurts.
I wouldn't lower myself to answer him.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) always supporting your friends, family, country or ideas
2. (adjective) (of a customer) always buying from the same company
contexts: He's a loyal friend.
The shop has many loyal customers.

words.definition: 1. (noun) an amount of money that is paid all at once, not in smaller amounts over time
contexts: She received a lump sum when she retired.

words.definition: 1. (noun) one of the two organs in your chest that you use to breathe
contexts: Smoking causes lung cancer.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the words of a song
Note: Singular (rare): lyric.
contexts: I love the lyrics of this song.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) very beautiful and impressive
2. (adjective) very good
contexts: The palace is magnificent.
She gave a magnificent performance.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to keep something at the same level or in the same state
2. (verb) to keep a building, machine or road in good condition by checking and repairing it
3. (verb) to say firmly that something is true
4. (verb) to pay for someone to have what they need to live
contexts: We need to maintain the quality of our products.
The car has been well maintained.
He maintains that he's innocent.
He has a family to maintain.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to study something as the main subject at university
Note: Mainly American.
contexts: She majored in history.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the larger part of a group, more than half
2. (noun) the difference in the number of votes between the winner and the loser in an election
3. (noun) the age at which you become an adult by law
contexts: The majority of people agree.
She won by a majority of 500 votes.
He'll reach his majority next year.

words.definition:
1. (idiom) to earn money quickly and easily, often in a dishonest way
Note: Informal. Also: make a quick buck.
contexts: He's only interested in making a fast buck.

words.definition: 1. (idiom) to have just enough money to pay for the things you need
contexts: They both work long hours to make ends meet.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to invent a story, excuse or lie
2. (phrasal verb) to become friends again after an argument
3. (phrasal verb) to form the whole of something
4. (phrasal verb) (~ for) to do something good to fix a bad thing you did, or to replace something lost
5. (phrasal verb) to put powder, colour and other products on your face
6. (phrasal verb) to prepare something by putting different things together
7. (idiom) (~ your mind) to decide
contexts: He made up an excuse for being late.
They argued, but they made up the next day.
Women make up 60% of the workers.
I'll make up for missing your birthday.
She made herself up before the party.
The chemist made up the medicine.
I can't make up my mind.

words.definition:
1. (noun) coloured creams and powders that people put on their faces to look more attractive
2. (noun) the different parts or people that form something
3. (noun) a person's character
Note: Also written: make-up.
contexts: She doesn't wear much makeup.
The ethnic makeup of the city has changed.
Jealousy isn't part of his makeup.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the process of producing or creating something
2. (idiom) (in the ~) becoming something, or being created
3. (idiom) (of your own ~) caused by you
4. (idiom) (have the ~s of) to have the qualities needed to become something
contexts: The making of the film took three years.
He's a star in the making.
The problem is of his own making.
She has the makings of a great teacher.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) done with your hands
2. (adjective) worked by hand, not automatically
3. (noun) a book that tells you how to use a machine or do something
contexts: He does manual work on a farm.
The car has a manual gearbox.
Read the instruction manual first.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to make goods in large numbers in a factory
2. (noun) the process of making goods in large numbers
contexts: The company manufactures cars.
The factory is used for the manufacture of cars.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the business of making goods in large numbers in factories
contexts: Many jobs in manufacturing have been lost.

words.definition:
