4. (adjective) (~ school) a school for children aged about 3 to 5
5. (noun) (~ rhyme) a short traditional poem or song for young children
contexts: Their son goes to a nursery three days a week.
They painted the nursery yellow.
We bought some roses at the nursery.
My daughter starts nursery school in September.
She knows lots of nursery rhymes.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the job of looking after people who are ill, injured or old
2. (adjective) connected with caring for people who are ill or old
3. (noun) (~ home) a place where old people who need care live
contexts: She's studying nursing.
She has nursing experience.
My grandmother lives in a nursing home.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the food that you eat and the way it affects your health
2. (noun) the science of food and its effect on health
contexts: Good nutrition is important for children.
She's an expert in nutrition.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the condition of being so fat that it is dangerous for your health
contexts: Obesity is a growing problem among children.

words.definition: 1. (verb) to do what a person, law or rule tells you to do
contexts: You must obey the law.

words.definition:
1. (noun) something that you are trying to achieve
2. (adjective) based on facts and not influenced by personal feelings or opinions
contexts: Our main objective is to increase sales.
Try to be objective.

words.definition: 1. (noun) something that you must do because it is your duty, a law or a promise
contexts: Parents have an obligation to send their children to school.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the act of watching someone or something carefully for a period of time
2. (noun) a comment about something you have noticed
contexts: The patient is under observation in hospital.
She made an interesting observation about the film.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to watch someone or something carefully
2. (verb) to notice or see something
3. (verb) to say something that you have noticed
4. (verb) to obey a law or follow a custom
Note: Formal.
contexts: Scientists observed the birds for a year.
Did you observe anything unusual?
“It's getting late,” he observed.
All drivers must observe the speed limit.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a person who watches or notices something
2. (noun) a person whose job is to watch an event, such as an election, to check that it is fair
3. (noun) a person who studies events and says what they think
contexts: To a casual observer, nothing looked wrong.
UN observers watched the election.
Political observers expect him to win.

words.definition: 1. (noun) something that blocks your way or makes it difficult to make progress
contexts: Lack of money is the biggest obstacle.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to get something, especially by making an effort
Note: Formal.
contexts: You need to obtain a visa.

words.definition: 1. (adverb) from time to time, but not very often
contexts: I occasionally go to the cinema.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a job or profession
2. (noun) the act of an army taking control of a country or area
3. (noun) something you do in your free time
4. (noun) the act of living in a building
contexts: Please write your name and occupation.
The country was under foreign occupation for ten years.
Reading is her favourite occupation.
The house is ready for occupation.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to fill or use a space, area or amount of time
2. (verb) to keep someone busy
3. (verb) (of an army) to take control of a country or area
4. (verb) to live or work in a building
5. (verb) to have a particular job or position
contexts: The table occupies most of the room.
The game kept the children occupied for hours.
The army occupied the city.
The building is occupied by a bank.
She occupies an important position in the company.

words.definition:
1. (idiom) small objects of different kinds that are not valuable
2. (idiom) small jobs of different kinds
Note: Informal.
contexts: The drawer was full of odds and ends.
I have a few odds and ends to finish at work.

words.definition:
1. (idiom) far away from places where many people go
Note: American English also: off the beaten path.
contexts: We stayed in a little village off the beaten track.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to make someone upset or angry because of something rude or unkind you say or do
2. (verb) to seem very unpleasant to someone
3. (verb) to do something illegal
contexts: I'm sorry, I didn't mean to offend you.
The smell offended my nose.
Many young people who offend do it again.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) upset or angry because someone has been rude or unkind to you
contexts: She was offended by his comments.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a person who has done something illegal
2. (noun) a person or thing that causes a problem
contexts: The prison is for young offenders.
Plastic bags are the worst offenders.

words.definition:
1. (noun) an illegal act, a crime
2. (noun) a feeling of being upset or angry because of rude or unkind behaviour
3. (noun) the players in a sports team who try to score points
Note: British spelling: offence. The last meaning is American.
contexts: Drink driving is a serious offense.
I hope you won't take offense.
Their offense is very strong.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) rude in a way that makes people upset or angry
2. (adjective) very unpleasant
3. (noun) a military attack
4. (adjective) connected with attacking
contexts: His jokes were offensive to women.
There was an offensive smell.
The army began a major offensive.
They used offensive weapons.

words.definition: 1. (noun) an accident in which a lot of oil comes out of a ship or pipe into the sea or land
contexts: The oil spill killed thousands of birds.

words.definition:
1. (idiom) getting better after an illness or injury
2. (idiom) (of a situation) improving
Note: Informal.
contexts: She was very ill, but she's on the mend now.
The economy is on the mend.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) coming towards you
contexts: He drove into the path of an oncoming car.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) continuing to happen or exist
contexts: The investigation is ongoing.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to talk about your feelings honestly
2. (phrasal verb) to make something possible or available
3. (phrasal verb) to unlock the door of a building
4. (phrasal verb) to start a new business
5. (phrasal verb) to make a hole or space in something
contexts: He finally opened up about his problems.
Learning English opens up many opportunities.
The shop opens up at nine.
A new café has opened up on our street.
The earthquake opened up a huge crack in the road.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) happy to listen to new ideas and other people's opinions
contexts: My parents are very open-minded.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a hole or space that something can pass through
2. (noun) the beginning of something
3. (noun) a ceremony or event for the start of something new, such as a shop or exhibition
4. (noun) a job that is available
5. (noun) a good chance to do something
6. (adjective) first, or happening at the beginning
contexts: We got in through an opening in the fence.
The opening of the film is very exciting.
We went to the opening of the new art gallery.
There's an opening for a sales manager.
The other team's mistake gave us an opening.
She made the opening speech.

words.definition: 1. (adverb) honestly and without hiding anything
contexts: They talked openly about their problems.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a play in which all or most of the words are sung, with music played by an orchestra
contexts: We went to the opera last night.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to use or control a machine, or to make it work
2. (verb) (of a machine or system) to work in a particular way
3. (verb) to cut open someone's body to repair, remove or replace a part
4. (verb) (of a business or organization) to work or do business in a particular way or place
5. (verb) to run a business or service
contexts: Can you operate this machine?
The heating operates automatically.
The doctors operated on her leg.
The company operates in 30 countries.
The airline operates flights to Spain.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a person whose job is to use a machine or piece of equipment
2. (noun) a person who works for a phone company and helps people make calls
3. (noun) a company that runs a particular business or service
contexts: He's a computer operator.
Ask the operator for the number.
The tour operator cancelled our holiday.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a person or team that you play or compete against
2. (noun) a person who disagrees with an idea or plan and wants to stop it
contexts: She beat her opponent easily.
He was a strong opponent of the war.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to disagree with a plan, idea or action and try to stop it
2. (verb) to compete with someone, for example in an election
contexts: Many people oppose the new law.
She will oppose him in the next election.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) (~ to) disagreeing strongly with something
2. (adjective) very different
3. (idiom) (as ~ to) used to show a difference between two things
contexts: I'm opposed to the death penalty.
They have opposed views on most things.
I prefer tea as opposed to coffee.

words.definition:
1. (noun) strong disagreement with a plan or idea
2. (noun) (the ~) the main political parties that are not in the government
3. (noun) (the ~) the team or person you are playing against
contexts: There was strong opposition to the new airport.
The leader of the opposition spoke after the prime minister.
The opposition scored in the first minute.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) believing that good things will happen
contexts: I'm optimistic about the future.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a large group of musicians who play different instruments together, especially classical music
contexts: She plays violin in the orchestra.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a part of the body that has a particular job, such as the heart or liver
2. (noun) a large musical instrument with pipes and keys, often played in churches
contexts: The heart is a vital organ.
She plays the organ at church.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) (of food or farming) grown or produced without artificial chemicals
2. (adjective) coming from or connected with living things
3. (adjective) developing naturally over time
contexts: We only buy organic vegetables.
Organic material rots quickly.
The company has had organic growth.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the beginning or cause of something
2. (noun) the country, family or culture that a person comes from
3. (noun) the place where something comes from
contexts: What is the origin of the word "hello"?
She's of Turkish origin.
The origin of the river is in the mountains.

words.definition:
1. (adverb) if not, or if something does not happen
2. (adverb) apart from what has just been mentioned
3. (adverb) in a different way
contexts: Hurry up, otherwise we'll be late.
The soup was cold, but otherwise the meal was good.
He says he's ill, but I think otherwise.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) old and not useful or fashionable any more
2. (adjective) (of a document) no longer able to be used officially
Note: Written "out-of-date" before a noun.
contexts: The map is out of date.
My passport is out of date.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) not fit or healthy
2. (adjective) (of an object) not in its usual form, for example after being bent or stretched
contexts: I'm really out of shape – I can't run anymore.
My sweater has been pulled out of shape.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) without a job
Note: Written "out-of-work" before a noun.
contexts: He's been out of work for six months.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the result or effect of an action, event or process
contexts: We're waiting for the outcome of the election.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) on the outside of something
2. (adjective) far from the centre
3. (noun) (~ space) the area beyond the earth's air, where the planets and stars are
contexts: Remove the outer leaves of the cabbage.
They live in the outer suburbs of the city.
The film is about aliens from outer space.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a set of clothes that you wear together, especially for a particular event
2. (noun) a group of people who work together, such as a company or band
Note: The second meaning is informal.
contexts: She bought a new outfit for the wedding.
He works for a small publishing outfit.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a short description of the main facts or points of something
2. (noun) a line that shows the shape of something
3. (verb) to describe the main facts or points of something
4. (verb) to show the shape of something
contexts: Here is an outline of the plan.
We could see the outline of the mountains.
She outlined her ideas for the project.
The trees were outlined against the sky.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the amount of something that a person, machine or factory produces
2. (noun) information that a computer produces
3. (noun) the power or energy produced by a machine
contexts: The factory has increased its output.
Check the output on the screen.
The engine has an output of 200 horsepower.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) extremely good
2. (adjective) not yet paid, done or solved
3. (adjective) very clear and easy to notice
contexts: She's an outstanding student.
You have an outstanding bill.
It's an outstanding example of modern art.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) including everything
2. (adverb) in general, when you think about everything
3. (noun) a piece of clothing like a loose coat that you wear over your clothes to keep them clean
4. (noun) (~s) a piece of clothing with trousers and a top part, worn over clothes for dirty work
contexts: The overall cost will be $500.
Overall, it was a good year.
The painter wore a white overall.
The mechanic was wearing blue overalls.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) (of the sky or weather) covered with grey clouds
contexts: It was an overcast day.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to succeed in dealing with a problem or difficulty
2. (verb) to defeat someone
3. (verb) (be ~ by/with) to be so strongly affected by a feeling, smoke or heat that you cannot act normally
Note: overcome – overcame – overcome.
contexts: She overcame her fear of flying.
They overcame the other team in the final.
He was overcome with emotion.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the catching of so many fish that there are not enough left in the sea
contexts: Overfishing has destroyed many fish populations.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to become too hot, or to make something too hot
2. (verb) (of an economy) to grow too fast, so that prices rise a lot
contexts: The engine overheated.
The economy is starting to overheat.

words.definition:
1. (adverb) during or for the whole night
2. (adverb) very quickly and suddenly
3. (adjective) happening during or for the night
4. (adjective) happening very quickly and suddenly
contexts: We stayed overnight in a hotel.
She became famous overnight.
We took the overnight train.
The book was an overnight success.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) too expensive for what it is
contexts: The food here is overpriced.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) thought to be better or more important than it really is
contexts: I think the film is overrated.

words.definition:
1. (adverb) in or to a foreign country, especially across the sea
2. (adjective) from, in or to a foreign country
contexts: She's working overseas.
There are many overseas students at the university.

words.definition: 1. (idiom) to stay somewhere as a guest longer than people want you to
contexts: Don't stay too long – you don't want to overstay your welcome.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to go past a car or person that is going in the same direction
2. (verb) to become greater, better or more successful than someone or something
3. (verb) (of a feeling or event) to suddenly affect someone
Note: overtake – overtook – overtaken. In American English, people usually say "pass" for cars.
contexts: Never overtake on a bend.
China has overtaken the US as the biggest market.
They were overtaken by the storm.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to remove a leader or government from power by force
2. (noun) the act of removing a leader or government by force
Note: overthrow – overthrew – overthrown.
contexts: The army overthrew the president.
They planned the overthrow of the government.

words.definition:
1. (noun) extra hours that you work after your normal working day
2. (noun) money that you are paid for working extra hours
3. (noun) extra time added to a game when the score is equal
Note: The meaning about extra time in a game is American. In British English: extra time.
contexts: I worked ten hours of overtime last week.
They don't pay overtime.
The game went into overtime.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) (of a word or idea) used so often that it is no longer interesting or effective
2. (adjective) used too much, so that it is damaged
contexts: “Amazing” is an overused word.
The old machines are overused.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) having too much work or too many problems to deal with
2. (adjective) feeling a very strong emotion, so that you do not know how to react
contexts: I'm overwhelmed with work this week.
She was overwhelmed by everyone's kindness.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to have to pay money back to someone who lent it to you
2. (verb) to feel that you should do something for someone because they helped you
3. (verb) (~ to) to have something because of someone or something
contexts: I owe my brother $50.
I owe you a favour.
She owes her success to hard work.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the fact of having something as your legal property
contexts: Home ownership is rising.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a gas in the air that has no colour or smell, and that people, animals and plants need to live
contexts: Fish take in oxygen through their gills.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a flat sea animal with a rough shell that you can eat raw or cooked; some produce pearls
2. (idiom) (the world is your ~) you can go anywhere and do anything you want
contexts: We ate oysters at the seaside.
You're young and clever – the world is your oyster.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the speed at which someone walks or runs, or at which something happens
2. (noun) a single step, or the distance of one step
3. (verb) to walk up and down a room or space, often because you are worried
4. (idiom) (keep ~ with) to move or change as fast as someone or something
5. (idiom) (at your own ~) as fast or slowly as you want
contexts: She walked at a fast pace.
He took two paces forward.
He paced up and down the hospital corridor.
It's hard to keep pace with new technology.
You can study at your own pace.

words.definition:
1. (idiom) to prepare to leave a place, often because you have to or are unhappy
Note: Informal.
contexts: If you don't like it here, pack your bags and go.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a small paper or plastic container that food or other things are sold in
2. (noun) a small parcel
3. (noun) a large amount of money
Note: Mainly British. In American English: pack or package. "Cost a packet" is informal.
contexts: He bought a packet of crisps.
A packet arrived for you this morning.
That car must have cost a packet.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a book that is so exciting that you want to read it quickly
Note: Informal.
contexts: Her new thriller is a real page-turner.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the inside part of your hand between your fingers and your wrist
2. (noun) a tall tree with no branches and a lot of large leaves at the top, that grows in hot countries
3. (phrasal verb) (~ off) to sell or give something unwanted to someone by tricking them
contexts: She held the coin in the palm of her hand.
There were palm trees along the beach.
He tried to palm off his old car on me.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a flat piece of wood, glass or metal that forms part of a door, wall or other surface
2. (noun) a group of experts who discuss something or make decisions
3. (noun) a flat board with switches and controls on it
4. (noun) (solar ~) a flat board that changes sunlight into electricity
contexts: The door has a glass panel.
A panel of judges chose the winner.
The pilot checked the control panel.
We put solar panels on the roof.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a sudden strong feeling of fear or worry that stops you from thinking clearly
2. (verb) to suddenly feel so afraid or worried that you cannot think clearly
3. (noun) (~ attack) a sudden feeling of great fear that makes your heart beat fast and makes it difficult to breathe
Note: panic – panicked – panicked.
contexts: There was panic when the fire started.
Don't panic! Everything will be fine.
She had a panic attack on the plane.

words.definition: 1. (verb) to breathe quickly and loudly with your mouth open, for example after running
contexts: He was panting after climbing the stairs.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a small room or cupboard in a house for keeping food
contexts: There's some rice in the pantry.

words.definition:
1. (noun) photographers who follow famous people everywhere to take pictures of them to sell
Note: Singular: paparazzo.
contexts: The singer was chased by the paparazzi.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a public event in which people walk or ride through the streets, often with music, to celebrate something
2. (noun) a formal event in which soldiers march together
3. (noun) a series of people or things that come one after another
4. (verb) to walk through the streets as part of a public celebration
5. (verb) to walk around to show yourself or something to other people
contexts: We watched the carnival parade.
The soldiers were on parade.
There was an endless parade of visitors.
The team paraded the trophy through the city.
She paraded around in her new dress.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) (of two lines) side by side and always the same distance apart
2. (adjective) similar and happening at the same time
3. (noun) a way in which two things are similar
4. (idiom) (in ~) happening at the same time
contexts: The road is parallel to the river.
There are parallel investigations in two countries.
There are many parallels between the two stories.
The two projects are running in parallel.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the group of people who are elected to make the laws of a country
Note: Often starts with a capital letter, as in "the British Parliament".
contexts: She was elected to parliament in 2015.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) working or studying for only some of the normal hours in a week
2. (adverb) for only some of the normal hours in a week
contexts: She has a part-time job in a café.
He works part-time.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a person who takes part in an activity or event
contexts: All participants will receive a certificate.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the act of taking part in an activity or event
contexts: Thank you for your participation.

words.definition: 1. (adverb) to some degree, but not completely
contexts: The accident was partly my fault.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a situation in which two or more people or organizations work together
2. (noun) a business owned by two or more people
3. (noun) the relationship between two people who are married or live together
contexts: The two companies are working in partnership.
He went into partnership with his brother.
They have a strong partnership.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a person who loves going to parties and has a lot of fun at them
Note: Informal.
contexts: She was a real party animal at university.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a person who spoils other people's fun
Note: Informal.
contexts: Don't be a party pooper – stay a bit longer!

words.definition: 1. (phrasal verb) to die (a polite way of saying it)
contexts: Her grandmother passed away last year.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to give something to another person, after you have received or used it
2. (phrasal verb) to give a disease to another person
3. (phrasal verb) to give a quality to your children through your genes
4. (phrasal verb) to make customers pay for an increase in your costs
5. (phrasal verb) (~ to) to start talking about something new
6. (phrasal verb) to die (a polite way of saying it)
contexts: Please read this and pass it on.
She passed on her cold to the whole family.
Parents can pass on the gene to their children.
The company passed on the higher costs to customers.
Let's pass on to the next point.
He passed on peacefully in his sleep.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a long, narrow space with walls on both sides that connects two places
2. (noun) a short part of a book, speech or piece of music
3. (noun) the movement of time
4. (noun) a journey by ship
5. (noun) the act of a new law being accepted by a parliament
contexts: A dark passage led to the kitchen.
Read the passage and answer the questions.
The building has changed with the passage of time.
They booked a passage to New York.
The bill had an easy passage through parliament.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) showing very strong feelings or beliefs
2. (adjective) showing strong romantic or sexual love
contexts: She's passionate about music.
They had a passionate relationship.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a secret group of letters or numbers that you must type to use a computer, website or phone
2. (noun) a secret word that you must say to be allowed into a place
contexts: Enter your password to log in.
The guard asked for the password.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the ability to stay calm and not get annoyed when you have to wait or deal with problems
2. (noun) a card game for one player
Note: The card game is called solitaire in American English.
contexts: Teaching young children requires a lot of patience.
She played patience on her computer.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a flat area with a hard stone floor next to a house, where people sit outside
Note: Plural: patios.
contexts: We had breakfast on the patio.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) decorated with shapes, lines or colours that repeat
contexts: She wore a patterned dress.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to stop speaking or doing something for a short time before you start again
2. (verb) to stop a video or song for a short time by pressing a button
3. (noun) a short time when you stop speaking or doing something
4. (idiom) (give someone ~ for thought) to make someone stop and think carefully about something
contexts: She paused for a moment, then continued.

There was a long pause before he answered.
Her words gave me pause for thought.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the foot of an animal such as a cat, dog or bear, that has claws
2. (verb) (of an animal) to touch or scratch something with a foot
3. (verb) to touch someone in a rough or unpleasant way
contexts: The dog hurt its paw.
The dog was pawing at the door.
Stop pawing me!

words.definition: 1. (noun) a formal agreement between countries to end a war
contexts: The two countries signed a peace treaty.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a person who tries to help people or countries stop fighting and agree
contexts: She's the peacemaker in our family.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a large male bird with a long, beautiful blue and green tail that it can spread out like a fan
Note: The female is called a peahen.
contexts: The peacock spread its tail.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the muscles of the chest
Note: Informal. Short for pectorals.
contexts: He works out to build up his pecs.

words.definition:

2. (verb) (of skin or paint) to come off in thin pieces
3. (verb) to remove a thin cover from something
4. (noun) the skin of fruit or vegetables
5. (idiom) (keep your eyes ~ed) to watch carefully for something
contexts: Peel the potatoes and cut them into pieces.
My back is peeling after the sunburn.
Peel the plastic off the screen.
Add some orange peel to the cake.
Keep your eyes peeled for a parking space.

words.definition:

3. (noun) (~ pressure) the feeling that you must do what people of your age do
4. (noun) (in Britain) a person of high social rank, such as a lord
contexts: Teenagers want to be accepted by their peers.
She peered through the window.
He started smoking because of peer pressure.
He became a peer in 2010.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a punishment for breaking a law or rule

3. (noun) a bad result of an action or situation
contexts: The penalty for parking here is $100.
He scored from a penalty.
You'll pay the penalty for not studying.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) having no money at all
contexts: He died penniless.

words.definition:
1. (noun) money that a person gets regularly after they stop working because of their age
2. (phrasal verb) (~ off) to make someone stop working and give them money regularly
3. (noun) a small, cheap hotel, especially in Europe
contexts: My grandfather lives on his pension.
He was pensioned off at 60.
We stayed in a little pension in Paris.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a person who has stopped working because of their age and gets money regularly from the state
Note: Mainly British. Also: old-age pensioner.
contexts: Pensioners get free bus travel.

words.definition: 1. (noun) an expensive flat on the top floor of a tall building
contexts: They live in a penthouse with a view of the whole city.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to see, hear or notice something
2. (verb) to understand or think of someone or something in a particular way
Note: Formal.
contexts: Some animals can perceive sounds that humans can't hear.
She is perceived as a strong leader.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the way you think about or understand someone or something
2. (noun) the ability to see, hear or notice things
3. (noun) the ability to understand things quickly and well
contexts: The public perception of the police has changed.
The drug can affect your perception of colour.
She showed great perception in her report.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) lasting for a very long time or for ever
2. (adjective) (of a job) that you can keep for as long as you want, not only for a short time
contexts: The injury caused permanent damage.
She's looking for a permanent job.

words.definition: 1. (adverb) for ever, or for a very long time
contexts: He moved to Spain permanently.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to allow someone to do something, or to allow something to happen, especially officially
2. (verb) to make something possible
3. (noun) an official document that gives you the right to do something

contexts: Smoking is not permitted in the building.
We'll go for a walk, if the weather permits.
You need a work permit.

words.definition: 1. (verb) to continue trying to do something, even though it is difficult
contexts: If you persevere, you'll succeed.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a particular way of thinking about something
2. (noun) the ability to think about a problem sensibly and see how important it really is
3. (noun) a way of drawing things so that they look far away or close
contexts: Try to see it from my perspective.
The accident helped me put my problems into perspective.
The artist had a good understanding of perspective.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) believing that bad things will happen
contexts: He's pessimistic about the future.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) (of a woman or girl) small and thin in an attractive way
contexts: She's very petite.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) extremely frightened
2. (adjective) (of wood or a plant) changed into stone over a very long time
contexts: I'm petrified of spiders.
They found a petrified tree.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a stage in a process or in the development of something
2. (phrasal verb) (~ out) to slowly stop using something
3. (phrasal verb) (~ in) to slowly start using something
contexts: The project is in its final phase.
Old phones are being phased out.
The new rules will be phased in over two years.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the highest university degree, which you get for doing research in a subject
Note: Short for Doctor of Philosophy.
contexts: She has a PhD in chemistry.

words.definition:
1. (noun) something that exists or happens, especially something unusual or difficult to understand
2. (noun) a person or thing that is very successful or unusual
Note: Plural: phenomena.
contexts: Rainbows are a natural phenomenon.
The band became a global phenomenon.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the study of ideas about life, knowledge, truth and what is right and wrong
2. (noun) a set of beliefs or ideas about how to live or do something
contexts: She's studying philosophy at university.
My philosophy is to enjoy every day.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a very strong fear of something that is not reasonable
contexts: She has a phobia of spiders.

words.definition: 1. (phrasal verb) to treat someone badly or unfairly again and again, for example by criticizing or hurting them
contexts: The older boys always pick on him.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to choose one person or thing from a group
2. (phrasal verb) to recognize someone or something in a group
3. (phrasal verb) to be able to see or hear something with difficulty
contexts: She picked out a dress for the party.
Can you pick out my dad in this photo?
I could just pick out the tune.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) (of a place) pretty and charming, like a painting
contexts: We stayed in a picturesque village by the sea.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a number of things lying on top of each other
2. (noun) (a ~ of / ~s of) a lot of something
3. (verb) to put things on top of each other
4. (verb) (~ into/out of) to move quickly as a group into or out of a place
Note: "Piles of" is informal.
contexts: There's a pile of books on the table.
I've got piles of work to do.
She piled the plates on the table.
We all piled into the car.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to increase in amount, often so that it becomes difficult to deal with
2. (phrasal verb) to put things on top of each other
contexts: The work is piling up.
He piled up the boxes in the corner.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a small hard piece of medicine that you swallow
2. (noun) (the ~) a medicine that women take to stop them getting pregnant
3. (idiom) (a bitter ~ to swallow) something unpleasant that you must accept
contexts: Take two pills with water.
She's on the pill.
Losing the final was a bitter pill to swallow.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a field for playing football, cricket and some other sports
2. (noun) how high or low a sound or voice is
3. (noun) the things a person says to try to sell something or persuade people
4. (noun) a level or degree
5. (verb) to throw a ball, especially in baseball
6. (verb) to try to persuade someone to buy or accept something
7. (verb) to put up a tent
8. (phrasal verb) (~ in) to start helping with work that a group is doing
Note: The meaning "field" is British. In American English: field.
contexts: The players ran onto the pitch.
Her voice has a high pitch.
He made a sales pitch to the customers.
The excitement reached a high pitch.
He pitched the ball to the batter.
She pitched her idea to the boss.
We pitched our tent by the lake.
Everyone pitched in to clean up.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a container with a handle and a lip, for pouring liquids
2. (noun) the player in baseball who throws the ball to the batter
Note: The container is called a jug in British English.
contexts: She brought a pitcher of water.
He's the best pitcher on the team.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a feeling of sadness for someone who is suffering or in a bad situation
2. (noun) (a ~) a situation that makes you sad or disappointed

4. (idiom) (take ~ on) to help someone because you feel sorry for them
contexts: I felt pity for the homeless man.
It's a pity you can't come.
I pity anyone who has to work with him.
She took pity on the cat and gave it some food.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a period of time when a student works somewhere to get experience
2. (noun) the act of finding a suitable job, school or home for someone
3. (noun) the act of putting something in a particular position
Note: The first meaning is mainly British. In American English: internship.
contexts: She did a six-month placement at a bank.
The agency helps with job placement.
The placement of the furniture makes the room look bigger.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) simple, without decoration or extra details
2. (adjective) all one colour, without a pattern
3. (adjective) easy to see or understand
4. (adjective) honest and direct
5. (adjective) (of a person) not beautiful
6. (noun) a large area of flat land
7. (idiom) (~ sailing) easy, without problems
contexts: She wore a plain black dress.
The walls are plain white.
It's plain that he's unhappy.
Let me be plain with you.
She was a plain child.
The plains of North America stretch for hundreds of miles.
After the first week, it was plain sailing.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) not containing or using the light, strong material made from oil that bags and bottles are often made of
contexts: The shop is completely plastic-free.

words.definition:
1. (idiom) to stay away from school without permission
Note: British. In American English: play hooky or skip school.
contexts: He was caught playing truant.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) having a sharp end
2. (adjective) (of a remark) clearly aimed at a particular person and showing criticism
contexts: The witch wore a pointed hat.
She made some pointed comments about his clothes.

words.definition:
1. (adverb) badly, not well
2. (adjective) ill
Note: The adjective is British and informal.
contexts: The room was poorly lit.
She's feeling poorly today.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to appear suddenly or when you do not expect it
2. (phrasal verb) (of a window on a computer screen) to appear suddenly
Note: Informal.
contexts: New cafés are popping up all over town.
An advert popped up on my screen.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the fact of being liked or used by many people
contexts: The popularity of online shopping is growing.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a part of something
2. (noun) the amount of food for one person
3. (phrasal verb) (~ out) to share something between people
contexts: A large portion of the money went on rent.
The portions in this restaurant are huge.
She portioned out the cake.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to cause a problem or danger
2. (verb) to ask a question
3. (verb) to sit or stand in a particular position for a photo or painting

contexts: The heat poses a risk to old people.

They posed for photographs.
He posed as a police officer.
She struck a pose for the camera.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to have or own something
2. (verb) (of a feeling) to have a strong effect on someone and control what they do
Note: Formal.
contexts: He possesses two houses.
What possessed you to do that?

words.definition:
1. (noun) a student who is studying at university after getting their first degree
2. (adjective) connected with study after a first degree
Note: In American English: graduate student.
contexts: The course is open to postgraduates.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) possible, or able to become something in the future

words.definition: 1. (adverb) possibly, in a way that could happen in the future

words.definition:

words.definition:

words.definition: 1. (noun) something you do to stop something bad or dangerous from happening

words.definition:
1. (verb) to happen or come before something else

words.definition:

words.definition:

words.definition:
1. (adverb) exactly

words.definition:
1. (adjective) easy to know in advance what will happen
2. (adjective) boring because it happens or behaves as you expected
contexts: The weather here is very predictable.

words.definition:

1. (verb) to drink alcohol, for example at home, before going out to a party or club

words.definition: 1. (adjective) (of a woman or female animal) having a baby growing inside her body

words.definition:
1. (noun) the first public showing of a film or play

words.definition:

words.definition:

words.definition:
