1. (verb) to limit the size, amount or range of something
2. (verb) to stop someone from doing what they want
contexts: Speed is restricted to 30 km/h in the town.
The new rules restrict our freedom.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a rule or law that limits what people can do
2. (noun) the act of limiting something
contexts: There are restrictions on how much money you can take out of the country.
The restriction of free speech is dangerous.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the business of selling goods to the public in shops or online
2. (verb) to be sold at a particular price
contexts: She works in retail.
The book retails at $15.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to keep something or continue to have it
2. (verb) to remember information
3. (verb) to hold liquid or heat
Note: Formal.
contexts: She retained her title as world champion.
I can't retain so many facts.
The soil retains water well.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the time when a person stops working because of their age
2. (noun) the period of your life after you stop working
contexts: He took early retirement at 55.
They're enjoying their retirement by the sea.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a meeting of people who have not seen each other for a long time
contexts: We're having a school reunion next month.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to tell people something that was secret or not known
2. (verb) to show something that was hidden
contexts: She revealed that she was pregnant.
He opened the box to reveal a beautiful ring.

words.definition:
1. (noun) money that a business or organization gets, especially from selling things
2. (noun) money that a government gets from taxes
contexts: The company's revenue rose by 10%.
Tax revenue has fallen this year.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the act of studying things you have learned again before an exam
2. (noun) a change made to something to improve it or correct it
Note: The meaning about exams is British. In American English: review.
contexts: I need to do some revision for my history exam.
The plan needs some revision.

words.definition:
1. (noun) an attempt by many people to change the government of a country, often using force
2. (noun) a very great change in the way people do things or think
3. (noun) one complete turn around a central point
contexts: The French Revolution began in 1789.
The internet caused a revolution in communication.
The wheel makes 50 revolutions a minute.

words.definition:
1. (noun) something good that you get because you have worked hard, behaved well or helped someone
2. (noun) money that is offered for information about a crime or for finding something lost
3. (verb) to give someone something because they have worked hard, behaved well or helped
contexts: As a reward for passing her exams, she got a new phone.
They offered a $500 reward for finding their dog.
She was rewarded for her honesty.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a regular repeated pattern of sounds or beats in music
2. (noun) a regular pattern of movements or events
contexts: I love the rhythm of this song.
The rhythm of her breathing slowed.

words.definition:
1. (noun) one of the curved bones around your chest
2. (noun) a piece of meat with one of these bones in it
3. (verb) to make jokes about someone in a friendly way
Note: The verb is informal.
contexts: He broke two ribs in the accident.
We had pork ribs for dinner.
His friends ribbed him about his new haircut.

words.definition:
1. (verb) (get ~ of) to throw away or remove something you do not want
2. (verb) (get ~ of) to make someone go away
3. (verb) (~ of) to remove something bad from a place
4. (adjective) (be ~ of) free from someone or something you did not want
Note: rid – rid – rid.
contexts: I need to get rid of these old clothes.
We couldn't get rid of him – he stayed all evening.
They tried to rid the city of crime.
I'm glad to be rid of that old car.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) very silly or unreasonable, so that people laugh at it
contexts: Don't be ridiculous!

words.definition:
1. (noun) the right to drive before other vehicles at a particular place on a road
2. (noun) the legal right to walk across someone else's land
Note: Plural: rights of way.
contexts: Cars on the main road have the right of way.
There's a public right of way through the farm.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to make someone pay too much money for something
2. (phrasal verb) to steal something or copy someone's idea
3. (phrasal verb) to remove something quickly by pulling it
Note: The first two meanings are informal.
contexts: The taxi driver ripped us off.
They ripped off our design.
He ripped off his shirt and jumped into the water.

words.definition:
1. (noun) something that costs much more than it should
2. (noun) a cheap copy of something
Note: Informal.
contexts: Ten dollars for a coffee? That's a rip-off!
The film is a rip-off of a famous French movie.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) (of fruit or crops) fully grown and ready to eat or be picked
2. (adjective) (~ for) ready for something to happen
3. (adjective) (of cheese) with a strong taste because it is old
4. (idiom) (a ~ old age) a very old age
contexts: These bananas aren't ripe yet.
The time is ripe for change.
This cheese is very ripe.
She lived to the ripe old age of 98.

words.definition: 1. (verb) to become ready to eat, or to make fruit become ready to eat
contexts: The tomatoes are ripening in the sun.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) involving the possibility of danger, loss or failure
contexts: Starting a business is risky.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a person, team or company that competes with another
2. (adjective) competing with another person, team or company
3. (verb) to be as good or as important as someone or something else
Note: rival – rivalled – rivalled (US: rivaled).
contexts: The two teams are old rivals.
He works for a rival company.
Few cities can rival Paris for beauty.

words.definition: 1. (noun) violent anger between drivers, often caused by the stress of driving
contexts: He was attacked in a road rage incident.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the crime of stealing money or things from a person or place, often using force or threats
contexts: There was a bank robbery yesterday.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a large vehicle shaped like a tube that is sent into space
2. (noun) a weapon that flies through the air and explodes
3. (noun) a firework that goes high into the sky and explodes
4. (verb) to increase very quickly
5. (noun) a plant with long green leaves that you eat in salads
Note: The plant is called arugula in American English.
contexts: The rocket was launched into space.
They fired rockets at the city.
We watched the rockets on New Year's Eve.
House prices have rocketed.
Add some rocket to the salad.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a small animal with long, sharp front teeth, such as a mouse, rat or squirrel
contexts: Rodents can damage crops.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a love relationship between two people, especially a short one
2. (noun) the exciting feeling connected with love
3. (noun) a story about love
4. (noun) a feeling of excitement and mystery about something
contexts: They had a holiday romance.
There's not much romance in their marriage.
She likes reading romances.
I love the romance of travelling by train.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the part of a plant that grows under the ground and takes in water
2. (noun) the part of a hair or tooth that is under the skin
3. (noun) the main cause or origin of something
4. (noun) (~s) the place, family or culture that a person comes from
5. (phrasal verb) (~ out) to find and remove something bad
6. (verb) to search for something by moving things around
7. (idiom) (take ~) to become established
contexts: The tree has very deep roots.
The dentist removed the tooth and its root.
Money is the root of the problem.
She went back to her roots in Ireland.
We must root out crime.
She rooted through her bag for her keys.
The idea took root quickly.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a flower with a sweet smell that grows on a bush with sharp points on its stems
2. (adjective) pink in colour
3. (verb) (the past form of "rise")
4. (idiom) (a bed of ~s) an easy and pleasant situation
contexts: He gave her a red rose.
The sky turned rose at sunset.
The sun rose at six o'clock.
Life isn't always a bed of roses.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) (of food, wood or plants) gone bad and not able to be used
2. (adjective) very bad or unpleasant
3. (adjective) ill or unhappy
4. (adverb) (spoil someone ~) to give a child everything they want
Note: The meanings "very bad" and "ill" are informal.
contexts: The apples were rotten.
What rotten weather!
I feel rotten today.
Her grandparents spoil her rotten.

words.definition:
1. (adverb) about, not exactly
2. (adverb) in a violent or careless way
3. (idiom) (~ speaking) used to show that what you say is not exact
contexts: It takes roughly two hours.
He pushed her roughly out of the way.
Roughly speaking, the trip will cost $1,000.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to press your hand or a cloth on a surface and move it backwards and forwards
2. (verb) to put cream or oil on a surface by pressing and moving your hand over it
3. (verb) (of two surfaces) to press and move against each other, often causing pain
4. (phrasal verb) (~ out) to remove pencil marks by pressing and moving something over them
5. (idiom) (~ it in) to keep talking about someone's mistake to make them feel bad
contexts: He rubbed his eyes.
Rub some sun cream on your back.
My new shoes rub.
Rub out the wrong answers.
Okay, I was wrong – don't rub it in.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a strong material that stretches, made from the liquid of a tree or from chemicals
2. (noun) a small piece of this material used to remove pencil marks
3. (adjective) made of this material
Note: The meaning "a piece used to remove pencil marks" is British. In American English: eraser.
contexts: Car tyres are made of rubber.
Can I borrow your rubber?
She wore rubber gloves to wash the dishes.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to spoil or damage something so badly that it loses all its value or pleasure
2. (verb) to make someone lose all their money or position
3. (noun) (~s) the parts of a building that are left after it has been destroyed
4. (noun) the state of being destroyed or badly damaged
5. (noun) the state of having lost all your money
contexts: The rain ruined our holiday.
The scandal ruined his career.
We visited the ruins of an old castle.
The house was in ruins after the war.
The business is facing ruin.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to meet someone by chance
2. (phrasal verb) to start having problems or difficulties
3. (phrasal verb) to hit something with a vehicle
4. (phrasal verb) to reach a particular amount
contexts: I ran into an old friend at the station.
The project ran into money problems.
The car ran into a tree.
The cost could run into millions.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to hit someone or something with a vehicle and drive over them
2. (phrasal verb) to take longer than planned
3. (phrasal verb) (of a liquid) to come over the top of a container
4. (phrasal verb) to quickly explain or practise something
contexts: Our cat was run over by a car.
The meeting ran over by half an hour.
The bath ran over.
Let's run over the plan again.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to practise something, such as a speech or play, from start to finish
2. (phrasal verb) to quickly explain or read something
3. (phrasal verb) (of a feeling or quality) to be present in all parts of something
contexts: Let's run through the song one more time.
She ran through the list of names.
A feeling of fear ran through the crowd.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) connected with the countryside, not towns and cities
contexts: They live in a rural area.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to move or do something very quickly
2. (verb) to make someone do something too quickly
3. (verb) to take someone or something somewhere very quickly
4. (noun) a situation in which you need to hurry
5. (noun) a sudden fast movement of people or things
6. (noun) a sudden strong feeling
contexts: She rushed to the hospital.
Don't rush me – I'm thinking.
He was rushed to hospital.
I'm in a rush.
There was a rush for the exit.
I felt a rush of excitement.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the busy time of day when many people are travelling to or from work
contexts: The trains are always crowded during rush hour.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to make someone leave their job, often because they did something wrong
2. (noun) (the ~) the act of losing your job
3. (noun) a large, strong bag for carrying or storing things
4. (idiom) (hit the ~) to go to bed
Note: The meanings about losing a job are informal and British. In American English: fire. "Hit the sack" is informal.
contexts: He was sacked for being late every day.
She got the sack last week.
They carried sacks of potatoes.
I'm tired – I'm going to hit the sack.

words.definition: 1. (idiom) not hurt or damaged, after being in danger
contexts: The missing children were found safe and sound.

words.definition:
1. (noun) (~s) official orders that stop trade or other contact with a country, to make it obey international law
2. (noun) official permission or approval
3. (noun) a punishment for breaking a rule
4. (verb) to officially allow or approve something
5. (verb) to officially punish someone or something
Note: Formal.
contexts: The UN put sanctions on the country.
The plan was given official sanction.
There are tough sanctions for cheating.
The government sanctioned the use of force.
The club was sanctioned for breaking the rules.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a machine sent into space that moves around the earth and sends back information or TV signals
2. (noun) a natural object, such as a moon, that moves around a planet
3. (adjective) (of a town or office) connected to a bigger one that controls it
contexts: The match was shown live by satellite.
The moon is the earth's only natural satellite.
The company has a satellite office in Leeds.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a pleasant feeling you get when you achieve something or when you get what you want
2. (idiom) (to someone's ~) in a way that pleases someone
contexts: She gets a lot of satisfaction from her job.
The problem was solved to everyone's satisfaction.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) pleased because you got what you wanted or expected
2. (adjective) certain that something is true
contexts: Are you satisfied with the result?
The police are satisfied that it was an accident.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to make someone pleased by giving them what they want or need
2. (verb) to give someone what they need or have all the qualities that are needed
3. (verb) to make someone believe that something is true
Note: satisfy – satisfied – satisfied.
contexts: Nothing I do satisfies her.
The food was enough to satisfy our hunger.
The police were satisfied by his story.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to fry food quickly in a little hot oil or butter
Note: Also written: saute. sauté – sautéed – sautéed.
contexts: Sauté the onions until they are soft.

words.definition: 1. (phrasal verb) to keep money over a period of time so that you can buy something
contexts: I'm saving up for a new bike.

words.definition:
1. (noun) an amount of money or time that you do not have to spend
2. (noun) (~s) money that you have kept, usually in a bank
contexts: You can make a big saving by buying online.
She spent all her savings on a car.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) (of food) salty or spicy, not sweet
2. (adjective) pleasant or morally good
Note: British spelling: savoury. The second meaning is usually used with "not".
contexts: Do you prefer sweet or savory snacks?
He's not a very savory character.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the size or level of something, especially when it is very large
2. (noun) a set of numbers or marks used for measuring or comparing
3. (noun) (~s) a machine for weighing people or things
4. (noun) the relationship between the size of something on a map or model and its real size
5. (noun) one of the small hard pieces that cover the skin of fish and snakes
6. (noun) a series of musical notes that go up or down
7. (verb) to climb up something high and steep
8. (phrasal verb) (~ down/back) to make something smaller in size or amount
Note: In American English, "scale" is used for a weighing machine.
contexts: We didn't realize the scale of the problem.
On a scale of 1 to 10, how happy are you?
She stood on the bathroom scales.
The map has a scale of 1:50,000.
Remove the scales before you cook the fish.
She practised her scales on the piano.
They scaled the wall.
The company has scaled back its plans.

words.definition:
1. (noun) an event or situation that shocks people because someone has behaved in an immoral or dishonest way
2. (noun) talk about the bad or shocking things that people have done
3. (noun) (a ~) something that is very wrong and makes you angry
contexts: The minister resigned after a financial scandal.
She loves a bit of scandal.
It's a scandal that so many children are hungry.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) available only in small amounts and not enough
2. (idiom) (make yourself ~) to go away or stay away, so you are not in the way
contexts: Water is scarce in the desert.
When her parents arrived, I made myself scarce.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to make someone feel frightened
2. (verb) to become frightened
3. (noun) a sudden feeling of fear
4. (noun) a situation in which many people worry about something dangerous
contexts: You scared me!
He doesn't scare easily.
You gave me a scare!
There was a bomb scare at the airport.

words.definition: 1. (idiom) extremely frightened
contexts: I was scared to death when the plane started shaking.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a description of a possible situation or of what might happen
Note: Plural: scenarios.
contexts: The worst scenario would be losing all our money.

words.definition:
1. (noun) an official plan or system for doing something
2. (noun) a clever plan, often a dishonest one
3. (verb) to make secret plans, especially to do something bad
4. (noun) (colour ~) a set of colours that are used together
Note: The meaning "official plan" is mainly British. In American English: plan or program.
contexts: The government has started a new scheme to help young people find jobs.
He came up with a scheme to steal the money.
They were scheming against the president.
I like the colour scheme in your kitchen.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a person who studies a subject in great detail, especially at a university
2. (noun) a student who has been given money to pay for their studies
contexts: She's a well-known history scholar.
He's a Rhodes scholar at Oxford.

words.definition:
1. (noun) money that a school or university gives a student to pay for their studies
2. (noun) serious study of a subject
contexts: She won a scholarship to study in the US.
The book is a fine piece of scholarship.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) extremely hot
contexts: It was a scorching day.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to rub your skin with your nails, usually because it itches
2. (verb) to cut or damage a surface with something sharp
3. (noun) a thin cut or mark on skin or a surface
4. (idiom) (from ~) from the very beginning, without help
5. (idiom) (up to ~) as good as it should be
contexts: Stop scratching your arm!
The cat scratched me.
There's a scratch on the table.
She built the company from scratch.
His work isn't up to scratch.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to shout very loudly in a high voice because you are frightened, hurt, angry or excited
2. (noun) a loud, high cry
3. (noun) (a ~) a very funny person or thing
Note: "A scream" meaning very funny is informal.
contexts: She screamed when she saw the spider.
We heard a scream from upstairs.
The party was a scream.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the showing of a film or TV programme
2. (noun) a medical test that checks people for a disease before they have signs of it
3. (noun) the process of checking people to find out if they are suitable or safe
contexts: There will be a screening of the film at 8 p.m.
Women over 50 should have regular screening for breast cancer.
All passengers go through security screening.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the average height of the sea, used as a base for measuring the height of land
contexts: The town is 500 metres above sea level.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the part of a town that is next to the sea, often with a path or road along it
Note: Mainly British.
contexts: We walked along the seafront.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a part of a country's economy or businesses
2. (noun) a part of an area or city
contexts: She works in the public sector.
The city was divided into four sectors.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) safe and protected from danger, harm or loss
2. (adjective) confident and not worried
3. (adjective) certain to stay the same and not likely to be lost
4. (adjective) firmly fixed and not likely to fall or move
5. (verb) to get something, often with difficulty
6. (verb) to fix or close something firmly
7. (verb) to make something safe
contexts: Keep your passport in a secure place.
Children need to feel secure.
She has a secure job.
Make sure the ladder is secure.
She secured a place at university.
Secure the boat to the pier.
The police secured the building.

words.definition: 1. (idiom) to agree with someone
contexts: My father and I don't always see eye to eye.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to go to an airport, station or other place to say goodbye to someone who is leaving
2. (phrasal verb) to make someone go away
3. (phrasal verb) to defeat someone in a game or competition
contexts: We went to the airport to see her off.
The dog saw off the burglars.
They saw off their rivals easily.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to look for something or someone
2. (verb) to try to get something, such as help or advice
3. (verb) to try to do something
Note: Formal. seek – sought – sought.
contexts: They're seeking a solution to the problem.
You should seek medical advice.
They sought to calm the crowd.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a person who is looking for or trying to get something
contexts: The town is popular with sun seekers.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to choose someone or something from a group, carefully
2. (adjective) of very high quality, and used by or available to only a few people
contexts: She was selected for the national team.
It's a very select club.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the act of choosing someone or something from a group
2. (noun) a range of things that you can choose from
3. (noun) a person or thing that has been chosen
contexts: The selection of the team will take place next week.
The shop has a wide selection of shoes.
Here's a selection of her best photos.

words.definition:
1. (noun) your own nature and personality
2. (noun) your own interests and wishes, more than other people's
Note: Plural: selves. Often used as part of words like "self-confident" and "myself".
contexts: She's back to her old self again.
He thinks only of self.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) sure of your own abilities and value
contexts: She's a very self-confident young woman.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) able to produce or provide everything you need without help from others
contexts: The farm is completely self-sufficient.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a house that is joined to one other house on one side by a wall they share
Note: British. Informal short form: semi.
contexts: They live in a semi-detached house in the suburbs.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a class at a university where a small group of students discusses a subject with a teacher
2. (noun) a meeting where people discuss or learn about a particular subject
contexts: We have a history seminar on Thursday.
She went to a seminar on marketing.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) having a higher position or rank than others
2. (adjective) older
3. (noun) a person who is older than someone else
4. (noun) a student in the last year of high school or university
5. (noun) an old person, especially someone who has stopped working
6. (noun) (with a capital S) used after a father's name when his son has the same name
Note: Some meanings are mainly American. Short form of the name: Sr.
contexts: She's a senior manager.
Senior members of the family were treated with respect.
She's five years my senior.
He's a senior in high school.
The centre offers activities for seniors.
John Smith Senior is the founder of the company.

words.definition: 1. (noun) an old person, especially one who has stopped working (a polite way of saying it)
contexts: Senior citizens can travel for free on buses.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) easily upset by what people say or do
2. (adjective) understanding other people's feelings and problems
3. (adjective) (of a subject) that needs to be dealt with carefully because it may upset people
4. (adjective) easily hurt or damaged
5. (adjective) (of equipment) able to measure very small changes
6. (adjective) (of information) secret
contexts: She's very sensitive about her weight.
He's a kind and sensitive man.
Religion is a sensitive subject.
I have sensitive skin.
It's a very sensitive camera.
The files contain sensitive information.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a book or film that continues the story of an earlier one
2. (noun) something that happens after an earlier event
contexts: The sequel is even better than the first film.
As a sequel to the meeting, we signed the deal.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a series of events or things that follow each other in a particular order
2. (noun) the order in which things happen or are arranged
contexts: Put the pictures in the right sequence.
The numbers are in sequence.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a period of time used for a particular activity
2. (noun) a formal meeting of a court, parliament or other official group
3. (noun) a period of time when you are using a website or app
contexts: We have a training session every Monday.
Parliament is now in session.
Your session has ended – please log in again.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to keep money or time for a particular use
2. (phrasal verb) to not think about something for a time because something else is more important
3. (phrasal verb) (of a court) to say that an earlier decision has no legal force
contexts: She sets aside an hour every day for reading.
Let's set aside our differences for now.
The judge set aside the verdict.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to start a journey
2. (phrasal verb) to start doing something with a clear aim
3. (phrasal verb) to explain or describe something clearly, often in writing
4. (phrasal verb) to arrange things so they can be seen or used
contexts: We set out early in the morning.
She set out to become a doctor.
The rules are set out in the handbook.
She set out the cups on the table.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a problem that delays progress or makes a situation worse
contexts: The team suffered a setback when their best player was injured.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to go and live in a place and stay there for a long time
2. (verb) to end an argument or disagreement by agreeing on something
3. (verb) to decide or arrange something finally
4. (verb) to pay money that you owe
5. (verb) to sit or lie in a comfortable position
6. (verb) to come down and rest on something
7. (verb) to become calm, or to make someone calm
8. (phrasal verb) (~ for) to accept something that is not exactly what you wanted
contexts: They settled in Canada after the war.
The two sides settled their differences.
It's settled – we're going to Rome.
Please settle your bill before you leave.
She settled into her chair with a book.
Dust had settled on the furniture.
This medicine will settle your stomach.
We wanted a big house, but we had to settle for a small flat.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to start living a quiet life in one place, often with a partner
2. (phrasal verb) to become calm and quiet, or to make someone do this
3. (phrasal verb) to sit or lie in a comfortable position
4. (phrasal verb) (~ to) to start giving your attention to something
contexts: He wants to settle down and have children.
Settle down, children!
She settled down on the sofa to watch TV.
I couldn't settle down to work.

words.definition: 1. (phrasal verb) to start to feel comfortable and happy in a new home, job or school
contexts: It took her a few weeks to settle in at her new school.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a person who goes to live in a new country or area where few people live
contexts: The first European settlers arrived in the 17th century.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) very bad or serious
2. (adjective) very strict or hard
3. (adjective) not friendly or kind in the way you look or behave
4. (adjective) very plain and without decoration
contexts: He has severe back pain.
The punishment was too severe.
She gave him a severe look.
The building has a severe design.

words.definition:
1. (adverb) very badly or seriously
2. (adverb) in a very strict or hard way
contexts: He was severely injured in the crash.
She was severely punished.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) sexually attractive or exciting
2. (adjective) exciting and interesting
Note: Informal.
contexts: She looked very sexy in that dress.
The new phone has a sexy design.

words.definition:
1. (noun) an area that is cooler and darker because the sun cannot reach it
2. (noun) a type of a particular colour, a little darker or lighter
3. (noun) a cover that keeps out light, for example on a lamp or window
4. (noun) (~s) sunglasses
5. (noun) a small difference in meaning
6. (verb) to protect something from direct light
7. (idiom) (put someone in the ~) to be much better than someone
Note: "Shades" meaning sunglasses is informal.
contexts: Let's sit in the shade.
The walls are painted a pale shade of green.
Pull down the shade.
She put on her shades.
The word has many shades of meaning.
He shaded his eyes from the sun.
Her performance put everyone else in the shade.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a dark shape that appears on a surface when something is between it and a light
2. (noun) an area of darkness
3. (noun) a dark area under your eyes because you are tired
4. (noun) a sad or bad feeling or influence
5. (verb) to follow someone secretly to watch what they do
6. (idiom) (beyond/without a ~ of a doubt) completely certain
contexts: The tree cast a long shadow across the grass.
Someone was standing in the shadows.
She had dark shadows under her eyes.
The news cast a shadow over the celebrations.
The police shadowed him for weeks.
She is, without a shadow of a doubt, the best player.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) not deep
2. (adjective) not showing serious thought, feelings or knowledge
3. (adjective) (of breathing) taking in only a little air
4. (noun) (the ~s) an area of water that is not deep
contexts: The children played in the shallow water.
He's very shallow – he only cares about looks.
Her breathing was shallow.
Fish swam in the shallows.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the bad feeling you have when you know you have done something wrong or embarrassing
2. (noun) (a ~) a situation that makes you sad or disappointed
3. (noun) loss of respect because of bad behaviour
4. (verb) to make someone feel bad about something they did wrong
5. (exclamation) (~ on you!) used to tell someone they should feel bad about what they did
contexts: He felt deep shame for what he had done.
It's a shame you can't come.
He brought shame on his family.
They shamed him into apologizing.
Shame on you for lying!

words.definition:
1. (adjective) having a particular form
Note: Often used in words like "heart-shaped" and "L-shaped".
contexts: The cake was shaped like a heart.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a place or building that protects people from bad weather or danger
2. (noun) a building where people with no home can stay
3. (noun) protection from bad weather or danger
4. (verb) to protect someone or something from bad weather or danger
5. (verb) to stay in a place that protects you
contexts: They built a shelter from branches.
She volunteers at a shelter for the homeless.
Everyone needs food and shelter.
The trees shelter the house from the wind.
We sheltered in a doorway until the rain stopped.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a sudden, unpleasant surprise that upsets you
2. (noun) a serious medical condition in which the blood does not flow normally, often after an injury
3. (noun) a sudden pain caused by electricity passing through your body
4. (noun) a strong shaking movement caused by a crash or explosion
5. (verb) to surprise and upset someone very much
6. (verb) to make someone feel offended, because of something rude or immoral
contexts: Her death was a terrible shock.
She was taken to hospital in shock.
I got a shock from the light switch.
The shock of the explosion was felt miles away.
The news shocked everyone.
The film shocked many viewers.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) very surprised and upset by something bad
contexts: We were shocked to hear about the accident.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) very bad or morally wrong in a way that makes people surprised and angry
2. (adjective) very bad or of very low quality
3. (adjective) (of a colour) very bright
Note: The second meaning is informal and mainly British.
contexts: The way they treat animals is shocking.
The food was shocking.
She wore shocking pink.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a situation in which someone is hurt or killed by a gun
2. (noun) the sport or activity of killing animals or birds with a gun
3. (noun) the process of making a film
contexts: There was a shooting in the city last night.
He goes shooting at weekends.
Shooting starts next month.

words.definition: 1. (phrasal verb) to compare the prices of something in different shops before you buy it
contexts: It's worth shopping around for a good deal.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the crime of taking things from a shop without paying
contexts: She was arrested for shoplifting.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the land along the edge of the sea or a lake
2. (phrasal verb) (~ up) to support or strengthen something that is weak
contexts: We walked along the shore.
The government took steps to shore up the economy.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) lasting or having an effect for only a short time
contexts: She found a short-term job for the summer.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a situation in which there is not enough of something that people need
contexts: There's a shortage of nurses.

words.definition:
1. (adverb) soon
2. (adverb) in an angry or unfriendly way, using few words
contexts: I'll be with you shortly.
“I'm busy,” she said shortly.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the act of firing a gun, or the sound of this
2. (noun) the act of kicking, hitting or throwing a ball to score a goal or point
3. (noun) an attempt to do something
4. (noun) a photograph or part of a film
5. (noun) an injection of a drug
6. (noun) a small amount of a strong alcoholic drink
7. (verb) (the past form of "shoot")
8. (idiom) (a long ~) something that is not likely to succeed
contexts: We heard two shots.
Good shot!
I'll have a shot at fixing it.
I got some great shots of the mountains.
Have you had your flu shot?
He drank a shot of vodka.
He shot the ball into the net.
It's a long shot, but it might work.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to behave in a way that tries to make people admire you, which is often annoying
2. (phrasal verb) to show people something you are proud of
3. (phrasal verb) to make something look attractive
contexts: Stop showing off!
She wanted to show off her new car.
The white dress shows off her tan.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) (of a business or factory) to close, or to make it close, and stop working
2. (phrasal verb) (of a computer or machine) to stop working, or to make it stop working
contexts: The factory shut down last year.
Shut down your computer before you leave.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a brother or sister
Note: Formal.
contexts: I have three siblings.

words.definition: 1. (noun) time away from work because you are ill
contexts: She's been on sick leave for two weeks.

words.definition:
1. (noun) your name written by you in your own special way, for example at the bottom of a letter or document
2. (noun) a quality or thing that makes someone or something easy to recognize
contexts: Please put your signature at the bottom of the form.
Spicy sauce is the restaurant's signature dish.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the importance or meaning of something
contexts: The discovery is of great significance.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) large or important enough to have an effect or be noticed
2. (adjective) having a special or hidden meaning
3. (idiom) (~ other) your husband, wife or partner
contexts: There has been a significant increase in crime.
She gave him a significant look.
You can bring your significant other to the party.

words.definition: 1. (adverb) in a way that is large or important enough to be noticed
contexts: Prices have risen significantly.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a time or state when there is no sound at all
2. (noun) a time when nobody speaks
3. (noun) a situation in which someone refuses to talk about something
4. (verb) to make someone or something stop speaking or making a noise
contexts: There was complete silence in the room.
There was a long silence before he answered.
The government has kept its silence on the matter.
She silenced him with a look.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a smooth, soft, shiny cloth made from the thin threads that a type of insect produces
contexts: She wore a silk scarf.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) (of feelings or words) honest and real
2. (adjective) (of a person) saying only what they really feel or believe
contexts: Please accept my sincere apologies.
He seems very sincere.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to sit comfortably and relax
2. (phrasal verb) to do nothing while something happens, often when you should act
contexts: Sit back and enjoy the show.
We can't just sit back and watch them destroy the forest.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) having the knowledge and ability to do a job or activity well
2. (adjective) (of work) needing special training and experience
contexts: She's a skilled pianist.
There's a shortage of skilled workers.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) having no money
Note: British, informal.
contexts: I can't come out tonight – I'm skint.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the bones of the head, which protect the brain
contexts: He fractured his skull in the fall.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a person who is owned by another person and has to work for them without pay
2. (noun) a person who is completely controlled by something
3. (verb) to work very hard
contexts: Millions of Africans were sold as slaves.
He's a slave to fashion.
I've been slaving away in the kitchen all day.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to move smoothly over a surface, or to make something do this
2. (verb) to move quietly and quickly
3. (verb) to slowly become lower or worse
4. (noun) a structure in a playground with steps and a smooth surface that children go down
5. (noun) one page of a computer presentation
6. (noun) a small piece of film in a frame that you show on a screen
7. (noun) a fall in the price, value or level of something
8. (idiom) (let something ~) to not do anything about something
Note: slide – slid – slid.
contexts: The children were sliding on the ice.
He slid into his seat at the back.
Prices continued to slide.
The kids love the slide in the park.
Let's look at the next slide.
He showed us slides of his holiday.
There was a slide in the value of the pound.
I'll let it slide this time, but don't be late again.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) very small in size, amount or degree
2. (adjective) (of a person) thin and light
3. (idiom) (not in the ~est) not at all
4. (noun) an action or remark that insults someone
contexts: There's been a slight improvement.
She was small and slight.
I'm not in the slightest bit tired.
He took her comment as a slight.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to slide by accident and fall or nearly fall
2. (verb) to slide out of position or out of your hand
3. (verb) to go somewhere quietly and quickly, so nobody notices
4. (verb) to put something somewhere quickly and quietly
5. (verb) to become lower or worse
6. (noun) a small mistake
7. (noun) a small piece of paper
8. (idiom) (~ your mind) to be forgotten
9. (idiom) (a ~ of the tongue) a small mistake when you say something you did not mean to
Note: slip – slipped – slipped.
contexts: She slipped on the ice and broke her arm.
The glass slipped from my hand.
He slipped out of the room.
She slipped the note into his pocket.
Standards have slipped.
It was just a slip.
Write your name on a slip of paper.
Sorry, it completely slipped my mind.
Calling him by the wrong name was just a slip of the tongue.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a short phrase that is easy to remember, used in advertising or politics
contexts: The party's slogan was “Time for change”.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a surface that goes up or down
2. (verb) to go up or down
3. (verb) to lean to one side, not be straight
contexts: The house is on a steep slope.
The garden slopes down to the river.
His handwriting slopes to the left.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) moving slowly
2. (adjective) (of a film, book or story) with little action, so it is not very exciting
contexts: We were stuck in slow-moving traffic.
The film was too slow-moving for me.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to laugh quietly in an unkind way
2. (noun) a quiet, unkind laugh
Note: British English also: snigger.
contexts: The boys snickered when the teacher tripped.
I heard a snicker from the back of the room.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a button on an alarm clock or phone that stops the alarm for a few minutes so you can sleep a little longer
contexts: I pressed the snooze button three times this morning.

words.definition:
1. (idiom) having too much work to deal with
Note: Informal.
contexts: I'm completely snowed under at work this week.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) used to show that you think a word or name is not correct
2. (adjective) used to show that something is usually called by a particular name
contexts: Her so-called friends didn't help her.
They study so-called black holes.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to cry noisily, taking in short breaths
2. (noun) the sound of someone crying noisily
Note: sob – sobbed – sobbed.
contexts: She sobbed when she heard the news.
We could hear her sobs from the next room.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) friendly and enjoying spending time with other people
contexts: She's very sociable and has lots of friends.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a person who loves meeting and talking to lots of different people
Note: Informal.
contexts: My sister is a real social butterfly – she knows everyone.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a person whose job is to design and write computer programs
contexts: She works as a software developer for a bank.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) connected with the sun
2. (adjective) using the power of the sun's light to produce electricity or heat
contexts: Solar energy is clean.
We put solar panels on our roof.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a large area of land covered with panels that turn sunlight into electricity
contexts: A new solar farm was built outside the town.

words.definition:
1. (adverb) in a way that you do not know or understand
2. (adverb) for a reason that you do not know
contexts: Somehow, she managed to finish on time.
Somehow, I don't trust him.

words.definition:
1. (adverb) at a time in the future or past that you do not know exactly
Note: Don't confuse it with "sometimes" (= now and then).
contexts: Let's meet sometime next week.

words.definition:
1. (adverb) a little, or to some degree
Note: Formal.
contexts: I was somewhat surprised by his answer.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) (of a machine or system) clever and complicated
2. (adjective) (of a person) having a lot of experience of the world and knowing about fashion and culture
3. (adjective) (of a person or idea) able to understand difficult things
contexts: The car has a sophisticated computer system.
She's a sophisticated young woman.
He has a sophisticated understanding of politics.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the part of a person that is not the body, which some people believe lives on after death
2. (noun) a person's deepest thoughts and feelings
3. (noun) a person
4. (noun) a type of music with strong feeling, made popular by African American singers
5. (noun) deep feeling and energy, especially in art or music
contexts: They prayed for the souls of the dead.
She put her heart and soul into the work.
There wasn't a soul in the street.
She loves soul music.
The performance had no soul.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the music used in a film
2. (noun) a recording of the music from a film, sold separately
contexts: The soundtrack of the film was amazing.
I bought the soundtrack online.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) having a sharp taste like a lemon
2. (adjective) (of milk) having a bad taste and smell because it is old
3. (adjective) unfriendly or in a bad mood
4. (idiom) (go/turn ~) to become bad or unpleasant
5. (verb) to make a relationship or situation unfriendly or bad
contexts: These apples are sour.
The milk has gone sour.
She gave me a sour look.
Their relationship turned sour.
The argument soured their friendship.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) extra, and kept in case it is needed
2. (adjective) (of time) free, when you are not working
3. (adjective) not being used and available for anyone to use
4. (noun) an extra thing kept to use if another one is lost or broken
5. (verb) to give time, money or help to someone, although you do not have much
6. (verb) to stop someone from having to experience something unpleasant
7. (verb) to not kill or hurt someone
8. (idiom) (to ~) left over, more than you need
contexts: Do you have a spare key?
What do you do in your spare time?
Is this seat spare?
I've lost my key, but I have a spare.
Can you spare a few minutes?
Spare me the details!
Please spare my life!
We got there with ten minutes to spare.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to speak more loudly
2. (phrasal verb) to say publicly what you think, especially to support someone or something
contexts: Could you speak up, please? I can't hear you.
If you think it's wrong, you should speak up.

words.definition: 1. (noun) unusual pictures or sounds in a film that are made by computers or special equipment
contexts: The film has amazing special effects.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a person who knows a lot about a particular subject or is very skilled in one area
2. (noun) a doctor who has a lot of knowledge about one type of illness or part of the body
3. (adjective) having a lot of knowledge or skill in one area
contexts: She's a specialist in computer security.
My doctor sent me to a heart specialist.
You need specialist advice.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to give most of your attention to one subject, product or activity
Note: British spelling also: specialise.
contexts: She specializes in children's books.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a group of animals or plants that are the same type and can produce young together
Note: Plural: species.
contexts: There are over 10,000 species of birds.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to say or describe something clearly and exactly
Note: specify – specified – specified.
contexts: Please specify your size when ordering.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) very exciting to look at
2. (adjective) very great, impressive or surprising
contexts: We had a spectacular view of the mountains.
The team had a spectacular win.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a person who watches an event, especially a sports event
contexts: The stadium holds 50,000 spectators.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to guess the reasons for something or what might happen, without knowing all the facts
2. (verb) to buy land, shares or other things hoping to sell them later at a profit
contexts: Newspapers speculated about the reasons for her resignation.
He made a fortune speculating on the stock market.

words.definition:
1. (noun) ideas or guesses about something that you do not know all the facts about
2. (noun) the activity of buying things hoping to sell them later at a profit
contexts: There is a lot of speculation about who will be the next president.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a raised strip across a road that makes cars go slower
Note: British English also: sleeping policeman (informal).
contexts: Slow down – there's a speed bump ahead.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a dried part of a plant, such as a seed or root, used to give a hot or special taste to food
2. (noun) interest or excitement
3. (verb) to add these dried plant parts to food
4. (phrasal verb) (~ up) to make something more exciting
contexts: Cinnamon and pepper are common spices.

The soup was spiced with ginger.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to make liquid flow over the edge of a container by accident

3. (noun) an amount of liquid that has come out of a container
4. (idiom) (~ the beans) to tell a secret
Note: spill – spilled or spilt – spilled or spilt. "Spilt" is British.
contexts: I spilled coffee on my shirt.
Fans spilled onto the street after the game.
Wipe up that spill.
Come on, spill the beans – who is he?

words.definition:
1. (adjective) connected with a person's soul and deep feelings, not with the body or physical things
2. (adjective) connected with religion
3. (idiom) (~ home) the place where you feel you belong
contexts: Money cannot meet our spiritual needs.

Paris is her spiritual home.

words.definition:
1. (idiom) (in ~ of) although something is true

3. (verb) to do something to hurt or upset someone
contexts: In spite of the rain, we went for a walk.

words.definition:
1. (verb) (of a liquid) to fall on something or move about in drops

3. (verb) to move noisily in water
4. (noun) the sound of something hitting water
5. (noun) a small amount of liquid
6. (noun) a small area of colour
7. (idiom) (make a ~) to become very famous or noticed
contexts: Water splashed on the floor.
The car splashed water all over me.
The children were splashing in the pool.
She jumped into the water with a big splash.
Add a splash of milk.
The room needs a splash of colour.
Her first book made a big splash.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a small, thin, sharp piece of wood, glass or metal that has broken off a larger piece
2. (verb) to break into small, thin, sharp pieces
3. (noun) (~ group) a small group that has separated from a larger one
contexts: I've got a splinter in my finger.
The glass splintered when it hit the floor.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to divide something into two or more parts, or to become divided
2. (verb) to share something between people
3. (verb) to break or tear along a line
4. (verb) (~ up) to end a relationship
5. (noun) a disagreement that divides a group
6. (noun) a long, thin tear or crack
7. (noun) the act of dividing something into parts
8. (idiom) (a ~ second) a very short moment
Note: split – split – split.
contexts: Split the class into two groups.
Let's split the bill.

There was a split in the party.
There's a split in the seat.
A 50–50 split seems fair.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to make something less good, enjoyable or attractive
2. (verb) to give a child too much of what they want, so that they behave badly
3. (verb) to treat someone in a very kind way to make them happy
4. (verb) (of food) to become bad
5. (idiom) (be ~t for choice) to have more choices than you need
Note: spoil – spoiled or spoilt – spoiled or spoilt. "Spoilt" is British.
contexts: The rain spoiled our picnic.
They spoil their grandchildren.
Let me spoil you with a nice dinner.
The meat will spoil if you don't put it in the fridge.
We were spoilt for choice in the restaurant.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a person who speaks officially for a group or organization
Note: Plural: spokespeople. Also: spokesman, spokeswoman.
contexts: A spokesperson for the company said they would investigate.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to pay for an event, programme or team, often in return for advertising
2. (verb) to promise to give money to a charity if someone does something difficult
3. (noun) a company or person that pays for an event or team in return for advertising
4. (noun) a person who promises money to a charity if someone does something difficult
5. (verb) to officially support a new law or plan
contexts: The race is sponsored by a car company.
Will you sponsor me? I'm running a marathon for charity.
The team has a new sponsor.
I've got ten sponsors for my walk.
She sponsored a bill on climate change.

words.definition: 1. (noun) money that a company gives to pay for an event or team, often in return for advertising
contexts: The club gets a lot of money from sponsorship.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) happening naturally, without being planned
2. (adjective) (of a person) doing things without planning them first
contexts: The crowd broke into spontaneous applause.
She's very spontaneous and fun.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a funny film, TV show or piece of writing that copies a serious one to make fun of it
2. (verb) to copy something serious in a funny way
Note: Informal.
contexts: The film is a spoof of old horror movies.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) connected with sports such as football and tennis
2. (adjective) fair and generous to the other team or player
contexts: The Olympics is the biggest sporting event in the world.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) completely clean
2. (adjective) (of a reputation or record) with nothing bad
contexts: Her kitchen is always spotless.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) with a pattern of small round marks
2. (verb) (the past form of "spot")
contexts: She wore a red and white spotted dress.

words.definition:

2. (noun) an injury caused by twisting a joint suddenly
contexts: I sprained my ankle playing football.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) firmly fixed and not likely to move or fall
2. (adjective) not likely to change suddenly
3. (adjective) (of a person) calm and reasonable
4. (noun) a building where horses are kept
contexts: Make sure the ladder is stable.

He's a very stable person.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) (of food) no longer fresh, especially dry and hard
2. (adjective) (of air) not fresh and unpleasant
3. (adjective) no longer interesting or new
contexts: The bread is stale.
The room smelled of stale smoke.
Their jokes are getting stale.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a table or small shop with an open front where things are sold, for example in a market
2. (verb) (of an engine) to stop suddenly, or to make it stop by mistake
3. (verb) to stop making progress
4. (verb) to try to get more time by delaying something
5. (noun) a small space for one animal in a farm building
contexts: She runs a fruit stall at the market.
