The talks have stalled.
Stop stalling and answer the question!
The cow was in its stall.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a public opinion or attitude about something
2. (noun) the way someone stands
contexts: What's your stance on the death penalty?
The batter took his stance.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to support someone in a difficult situation
2. (phrasal verb) to be ready to act if needed
3. (phrasal verb) to do nothing while something bad happens
4. (phrasal verb) to keep a promise or decision
contexts: Her husband stood by her through the trial.
The army is standing by.
We can't just stand by and watch.
I stand by what I said.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to give up an important job or position so someone else can have it
2. (phrasal verb) (of soldiers or police) to stop being ready for action
Note: Mainly British.
contexts: The chairman will stand down next month.
The troops were ordered to stand down.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to not come to a date or meeting that you arranged with someone
Note: Informal.
contexts: I waited for an hour – I think she stood me up.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to look at someone or something for a long time, often because you are surprised
2. (noun) a long, fixed look
contexts: Don't stare at people – it's rude.
He gave me a cold stare.

words.definition: 1. (verb) to surprise someone suddenly and make them a little afraid
contexts: Sorry, I didn't mean to startle you.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a new small company, especially one in technology
Note: Also written: start-up.
contexts: She works for a tech startup.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to suffer or die because you do not have enough food
2. (verb) to give a person or animal too little food
3. (idiom) (be ~ing) to be very hungry
4. (verb) (be ~d of) to not have enough of something you need
contexts: Thousands of people starved during the war.
They starved the prisoners.
When's dinner? I'm starving!
The schools are starved of money.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a person's social or professional position compared with others
2. (noun) the situation of something at a particular time
3. (noun) a person's legal position
4. (noun) a short message you put on a social media page about what you are doing or thinking
contexts: Doctors have high status in society.
What's the status of my order?
What is your marital status?
She updated her status on Facebook.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a holiday that you spend at home or in your own country, not abroad
Note: Informal.
contexts: We couldn't afford to fly, so we had a staycation.

words.definition:
1. (adverb) slowly and regularly, without stopping
2. (adverb) in a calm and firm way
contexts: Prices have risen steadily.
She looked at him steadily.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) firmly fixed and not shaking or moving
2. (adjective) happening at a regular, even speed or rate
3. (adjective) not changing, and continuing for a long time
4. (verb) to stop something from moving or shaking
5. (verb) to make someone calm
contexts: Hold the camera steady.
There has been a steady increase in sales.
She has a steady job.
He put out a hand to steady himself.
She took a deep breath to steady her nerves.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the hot gas that water becomes when it boils
2. (verb) to cook food in this hot gas
3. (verb) to send out this hot gas
4. (idiom) (let off ~) to do something to get rid of strong feelings or energy
5. (idiom) (run out of ~) to lose energy or interest
6. (phrasal verb) (~ up) (of glass) to become covered with tiny drops of water
contexts: Steam rose from the hot soup.
Steam the vegetables for five minutes.
The kettle was steaming.
The kids need to let off steam after school.
The project ran out of steam.
My glasses steamed up.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a very strong metal made from iron and carbon, used to make knives, cars and buildings
2. (verb) (~ yourself) to prepare yourself for something unpleasant
contexts: The bridge is made of steel.
She steeled herself to hear the bad news.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) (of a hill, road or stairs) rising or falling sharply
2. (adjective) (of a rise or fall) sudden and large
3. (adjective) (of a price) too expensive
4. (verb) to leave food in a liquid so that it becomes soft or takes on a taste
Note: The meaning "too expensive" is informal.
contexts: The road up the hill is very steep.
There's been a steep rise in prices.
Fifty dollars for a ticket seems a bit steep.
Steep the tea for three minutes.

words.definition: 1. (phrasal verb) to leave an important job or position
contexts: She stepped down as manager after ten years.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to come out beyond the edge or surface of something
2. (phrasal verb) to push a part of your body forward
3. (phrasal verb) to be very easy to notice
4. (idiom) (~ it out) to continue doing something difficult until the end
5. (idiom) (~ like a sore thumb) to look very different from everything around you
contexts: His ears stick out.
The child stuck out his tongue at me.
She really sticks out in that bright dress.
The job is hard, but I'll stick it out.
In his suit, he stuck out like a sore thumb.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to continue doing or using something and not change it
2. (phrasal verb) to keep a promise or decision
3. (phrasal verb) to talk only about a particular subject
contexts: Let's stick to the plan.
She always sticks to her word.
Please stick to the point.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) covered with a substance, such as glue or honey, that holds on to things it touches
2. (adjective) (of weather) hot and wet in an unpleasant way
3. (adjective) difficult or embarrassing
4. (noun) (~ note) a small piece of paper that you can stick on something
contexts: My hands are sticky from the jam.
It was a hot, sticky day.
We were in a sticky situation.
She left me a sticky note on the fridge.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) hard and not easy to bend or move
2. (adjective) (of muscles or joints) painful and difficult to move
3. (adjective) more difficult or severe than usual
4. (adjective) not friendly or relaxed
5. (adjective) (of a mixture) thick and almost solid
6. (adverb) (bored/scared ~) very bored or very frightened
contexts: The new shoes are stiff.
I've got a stiff neck.
There's stiff competition for the job.
He gave a stiff smile.
Beat the eggs until they are stiff.
I was bored stiff in the meeting.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to make something grow or become more active
2. (verb) to make someone interested and excited
3. (verb) to make a part of the body work
contexts: The government wants to stimulate the economy.
Good teachers stimulate their students.
Coffee stimulates the heart.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) not liking to spend or give money
2. (adjective) (of an amount) very small
Note: Informal.
contexts: He's too stingy to buy anyone a drink.
The portions were a bit stingy.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the goods that a shop has available to sell
2. (noun) an amount of something kept to use later
3. (noun) a share in a company, or the value of a company's shares
4. (noun) a liquid made by boiling meat, fish or vegetables, used to make soups and sauces
5. (verb) to have goods available to sell
6. (verb) to fill a place with goods or food
7. (phrasal verb) (~ up) to buy a lot of something to use later
8. (idiom) (take ~) to stop and think carefully about a situation
contexts: The shoes are out of stock in your size.
We have a good stock of food for the winter.
She bought stocks in a tech company.
Add the chicken stock to the pan.
Do you stock printer paper?
The fridge was stocked with beer.
We stocked up on water before the storm.
It's time to take stock of our lives.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a short illness that makes you sick and gives you pain in your stomach
Note: Informal.
contexts: Half the class is off school with a stomach bug.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a small, narrow river
2. (noun) a continuous flow of liquid, air or gas
3. (noun) a continuous series of people, things or events
4. (verb) to flow or move continuously in large numbers
5. (verb) to play video or sound directly from the internet
6. (noun) a group of students of the same ability
Note: The meaning about groups of students is British.
contexts: The children played in the stream.
A stream of water came out of the pipe.
There was a steady stream of customers.
Tears streamed down her face.
You can stream the film online.
She's in the top stream for maths.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to make something or someone stronger, or to become stronger
2. (verb) to make a relationship, idea or position more powerful or certain
contexts: Exercise strengthens your muscles.
The visit strengthened ties between the two countries.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to make something longer or wider by pulling it
2. (verb) to make your arms, legs or body as long as possible
3. (verb) (of material) to become longer or looser
4. (verb) to spread over a large area or long time
5. (verb) to make money or supplies last longer
6. (noun) an area of land or water
7. (noun) a continuous period of time
8. (noun) a movement in which you make your body as long as possible
9. (idiom) (~ your legs) to go for a short walk after sitting for a long time
contexts: She stretched the rubber band.
He woke up and stretched.
My sweater stretched in the wash.
The forest stretches for miles.
We need to stretch our budget.
This stretch of road is dangerous.
She worked for ten hours at a stretch.
Do some stretches before exercise.
Let's stop the car and stretch our legs.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) making sure that people obey rules and behave well
2. (adjective) (of a rule) that must be obeyed
3. (adjective) exact and correct
4. (adjective) following the rules of a religion or belief carefully
contexts: My parents were very strict with me.
There are strict rules about smoking.
It's not true in the strict sense of the word.
She's a strict vegetarian.

words.definition:
1. (adverb) in a firm way, so that rules must be obeyed
2. (adverb) exactly or completely
3. (idiom) (~ speaking) if you are being very exact
contexts: Smoking is strictly forbidden.
That's not strictly true.
Strictly speaking, a tomato is a fruit.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to hit someone or something hard
2. (verb) to stop working for a time to show you disagree with your employer about pay or conditions
3. (verb) (of something bad) to happen suddenly
4. (verb) (of an idea or thought) to come suddenly into your mind
5. (verb) to have a particular effect on someone
6. (verb) (of a clock) to ring to show the time
7. (verb) to light a match
8. (noun) a period when workers stop working to show they disagree with their employer
9. (noun) a sudden military attack
10. (idiom) (~ a deal) to make an agreement
Note: strike – struck – struck.
contexts: The car struck a tree.
The nurses are striking for better pay.
The earthquake struck at midnight.
It struck me that he was lying.
She strikes me as a very honest person.
The clock struck twelve.
He struck a match.
The workers are on strike.
The army launched an air strike.
They struck a deal with the bank.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a sudden serious illness when a blood vessel in the brain bursts or is blocked
2. (noun) a hit with a hand, stick or ball
3. (noun) a line made with a pen or brush
4. (noun) a style of swimming, or one movement of the arms in swimming
5. (verb) to move your hand gently over something, again and again
6. (idiom) (a ~ of luck) something lucky that happens unexpectedly
7. (idiom) (on the ~ of) exactly at a particular time
contexts: He had a stroke and couldn't speak.
He hit the ball with a single stroke.
She painted with quick strokes.
She swims with long, smooth strokes.
She stroked the cat.
By a stroke of luck, the bus was late too.
He arrived on the stroke of midnight.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to walk slowly and in a relaxed way
2. (noun) a slow, relaxed walk
contexts: We strolled along the beach.
Let's go for a stroll in the park.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a small seat on wheels for pushing a young child around
2. (noun) a person who is walking slowly
Note: The first meaning is American. In British English: pushchair or buggy.
contexts: She pushed the baby in a stroller.
The park was full of evening strollers.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to try very hard to do something that is difficult
2. (verb) to fight against someone or try to get free
3. (verb) to have problems, for example with money or a task
4. (noun) a great effort to achieve something difficult
5. (noun) a fight
contexts: She struggled to find a job.
He struggled to get free.
Many families are struggling to pay their bills.
Learning English was a struggle for him.
There were signs of a struggle.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) refusing to change your opinion or what you are doing, even when you should
2. (adjective) difficult to remove or deal with
contexts: He's too stubborn to say sorry.
This soap removes stubborn stains.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) so shocked or surprised that you cannot speak or act
2. (adjective) made unconscious or confused by a hit on the head
contexts: She was stunned by the news.
The bird lay stunned on the ground.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) very beautiful or attractive
2. (adjective) very surprising or impressive
contexts: You look stunning!
The team had a stunning victory.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to repeat the first sound of words when you speak, because of a speech problem or nervousness
2. (noun) a speech problem that makes someone repeat sounds
contexts: He stutters when he's nervous.
She has a slight stutter.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to give a document, plan or piece of work to someone officially so they can check or decide about it
2. (verb) (~ to) to accept that someone has power over you, or to agree to something you do not want
Note: submit – submitted – submitted. Formal.
contexts: Please submit your application by Friday.
He refused to submit to their demands.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) happening after something else
2. (idiom) (~ to) after
Note: Formal.
contexts: The problems are explained in subsequent chapters.
Subsequent to the meeting, we made a decision.

words.definition:
1. (adverb) after something else happened
Note: Formal.
contexts: He was arrested and subsequently released.

words.definition:
1. (noun) words at the bottom of a film or TV screen that translate or show what people are saying
Note: Singular: subtitle.
contexts: I watched a French film with English subtitles.

words.definition:
1. (noun) an area where people live, outside the centre of a city
2. (noun) (the ~s) the areas where people live outside a city centre
contexts: They live in a quiet suburb of London.
They moved to the suburbs when they had kids.

words.definition:
1. (noun) physical or mental pain
2. (noun) (~s) feelings of pain and unhappiness
contexts: The drug helps to reduce suffering.
The war caused great sufferings.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) as much as is needed for a particular purpose
Note: Formal.
contexts: We have sufficient food for a week.

words.definition:
1. (adverb) to the degree that is needed
Note: Formal.
contexts: She has recovered sufficiently to go home.

words.definition:
1. (noun) an amount of money
2. (noun) the total you get when you add numbers together
3. (noun) a simple maths problem
4. (idiom) (in ~) used to give the main point briefly
contexts: They spent a large sum on the house.
The sum of 5 and 3 is 8.
The children are doing sums.
In sum, the plan is too expensive.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to give the main points of something in a few words
2. (phrasal verb) to describe or show the most typical qualities of something
3. (phrasal verb) to form an opinion about someone or something quickly
contexts: To sum up, the project was a success.
That picture sums up the feeling of the time.
She summed up the situation immediately.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) very good
2. (adverb) very
Note: Informal.
contexts: We had a super time.
The test was super easy.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the actors in a film or play who are not the main stars
contexts: The supporting cast is excellent.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a doctor who cuts open people's bodies to repair or remove parts
contexts: The surgeon operated on her heart.

words.definition:
1. (noun) medical treatment in which a doctor cuts open your body to repair or remove a part
2. (noun) a place where people go to see a doctor or dentist
3. (noun) the time when a doctor sees patients
Note: The last two meanings are British. In American English: office and office hours.
contexts: He needs surgery on his knee.
The doctor's surgery opens at 8.
Morning surgery is from 9 to 12.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to be all around someone or something
2. (verb) to move into position all around someone or something, so they cannot escape
3. (verb) to be closely connected with a situation
contexts: The house is surrounded by trees.
Police surrounded the building.
There is a lot of mystery surrounding his death.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) all around a place
2. (noun) (~s) the place where someone or something is and the things in it
contexts: The castle and the surrounding area are beautiful.
The hotel is in beautiful surroundings.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the fact of continuing to live or exist, especially in a difficult situation
contexts: The animals fight for survival in the desert.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a person who continues to live after an accident, war or illness
2. (noun) a person who is good at dealing with difficult situations
contexts: There were no survivors of the plane crash.
Don't worry about her – she's a survivor.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to think that something is probably true, especially something bad
2. (verb) to think that someone has probably done something wrong
3. (noun) a person who the police think may have done a crime
4. (adjective) possibly false, dangerous or not to be trusted
Note: The verb is stressed on "spect"; the noun and adjective on "sus".
contexts: I suspect that he's lying.
The police suspect him of murder.
The police have arrested two suspects.
The bag looked suspect.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to stop something for a period of time
2. (verb) to stop someone from working or going to school for a time, as a punishment
3. (verb) to hang something from somewhere
contexts: The game was suspended because of rain.
He was suspended from school for fighting.
A lamp was suspended from the ceiling.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) able to continue without harming the environment or using up natural resources
2. (adjective) able to continue for a long time
contexts: We need more sustainable sources of energy.
The company's growth is not sustainable.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to make food, drink or a pill go down your throat into your stomach
2. (verb) to believe something that is not true
3. (verb) (~ your pride) to do something that is embarrassing for you, such as saying sorry
4. (noun) a small bird with a tail with two points, that flies very fast
contexts: Chew your food before you swallow it.
I can't believe you swallowed that story!
He swallowed his pride and asked for help.
Swallows fly south in winter.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to give something to someone and get something else from them
2. (verb) to replace one thing with another
3. (noun) an exchange of one thing for another
Note: swap – swapped – swapped. Also written: swop.
contexts: Can I swap seats with you?
Swap the sugar for honey.
Let's do a swap.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to use rude or offensive words
2. (verb) to promise seriously that something is true or that you will do something
3. (phrasal verb) (~ by) to be sure that something is very good or useful
Note: swear – swore – sworn.
contexts: Don't swear in front of the children.
I swear I didn't take your money.
She swears by this cream.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to clean a floor or surface by using a brush
2. (verb) to move or push something quickly and with force
3. (verb) to spread quickly through an area
4. (verb) to move quickly and proudly
5. (noun) a long, curved movement
6. (idiom) (~ someone off their feet) to make someone fall in love with you quickly
7. (idiom) (~ something under the carpet) to hide a problem
Note: sweep – swept – swept.
contexts: Can you sweep the kitchen floor?
The wave swept him into the sea.
A new fashion is sweeping the country.
She swept out of the room.
He showed us the room with a sweep of his arm.
He swept her off her feet.
They tried to sweep the scandal under the carpet.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to move your finger quickly across a touch screen
2. (verb) to pass a card through a machine that reads it
3. (verb) to hit or try to hit someone with your arm
4. (verb) to steal something
5. (noun) a quick movement of your finger across a touch screen
6. (noun) (take a ~ at) a criticism of someone
Note: The meaning "steal" is informal.
contexts: Swipe left to see the next photo.
Swipe your card to open the door.
He swiped at the fly.
Someone swiped my phone.
Unlock the phone with a swipe.
He took a swipe at his rivals in the speech.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a list of the subjects and books that are studied in a course
Note: Plural: syllabuses or syllabi.
contexts: Shakespeare is on the syllabus this year.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) kind to someone who is in a bad situation, and showing that you understand how they feel
2. (adjective) (~ to/towards) agreeing with or supporting an idea or plan
3. (adjective) (of a person in a book or film) easy to like
Note: It does not mean "nice" or "pleasant" in English.
contexts: She was very sympathetic when my father died.
He is sympathetic to our cause.
The main character isn't very sympathetic.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the feeling of being sorry for someone who is sad or in a bad situation
2. (noun) agreement with or support for an idea or plan
contexts: I have no sympathy for him – it's his own fault.
I have some sympathy with their views.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to make the information on two or more devices the same
2. (idiom) (in ~) happening at the same time or working well together
3. (idiom) (out of ~) not happening at the same time, or not working well together
Note: Short for synchronize. Also written: synch.
contexts: Sync your phone with your laptop.
The sound and the picture are not in sync.
My body clock is out of sync after the flight.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a newspaper with small pages, many photos and short stories, often about famous people and shocking events
contexts: The tabloids are full of stories about the singer's divorce.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to make a serious effort to deal with a difficult problem
2. (verb) (in football and other sports) to try to take the ball from another player
3. (verb) to take hold of someone and make them fall, for example to stop them escaping
4. (verb) to speak to someone about something difficult
5. (noun) an attempt to take the ball from another player
6. (noun) the equipment used for fishing
contexts: The government must tackle unemployment.
He tackled the striker and won the ball.
The police officer tackled the thief.
I'll tackle him about the money tomorrow.
He was injured in a bad tackle.
He packed his fishing tackle.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a very young frog that lives in water and has a long tail and no legs yet
contexts: The children collected tadpoles from the pond.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a small piece of paper, plastic or material attached to something, giving information about it
2. (noun) a word or phrase added to a post online to show what it is about
3. (noun) a children's game in which one child chases and tries to touch the others
4. (verb) to fix a label to something
5. (verb) to add someone's name to a photo or post on social media
6. (phrasal verb) (~ along) to go somewhere with someone, often when they did not invite you
Note: "Tag along" is informal.
contexts: Look at the price tag.
Use the tag #travel.
The kids were playing tag in the park.
All the bags were tagged with names.
She tagged me in a photo.
Do you mind if I tag along?

words.definition: 1. (phrasal verb) to look or behave like an older member of your family
contexts: She takes after her mother – they're both very funny.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to separate something into its different parts
2. (phrasal verb) to show that an idea or argument is completely wrong
3. (phrasal verb) to beat a team or player very easily
Note: The last two meanings are informal.
contexts: He took the clock apart to see how it worked.
The critics took her new film apart.
They took the other team apart, winning 6–0.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to remove something or someone from a place
2. (phrasal verb) to make a feeling or pain go away
3. (phrasal verb) to remove a number from another number
4. (phrasal verb) to buy cooked food from a restaurant and eat it somewhere else
Note: The last meaning is British. In American English: to go.
contexts: The waiter took away our plates.
The tablets took the pain away.
If you take 3 away from 10, you get 7.
Two pizzas to take away, please.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to return something to the place you got it from
2. (phrasal verb) to admit that something you said was wrong
3. (phrasal verb) to make you remember a time in the past
4. (phrasal verb) to agree to have someone back, such as a partner or worker
contexts: I took the shoes back because they were too small.
I take back what I said – you were right.
This song takes me back to my school days.
She forgave him and took him back.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to understand and remember information
2. (phrasal verb) to let someone stay in your home
3. (phrasal verb) to trick someone into believing something that is not true
4. (phrasal verb) to make clothes tighter
5. (phrasal verb) to include something
6. (phrasal verb) to look at something carefully
contexts: There was too much information to take in.
They took in a homeless cat.
Don't be taken in by his charm.
Can you take in this dress?
The tour takes in all the main sights.
We stopped to take in the view.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a story about imaginary events, especially an exciting one
2. (noun) a report of something that happened, which may not be completely true
3. (idiom) (tell ~s) to tell someone in authority about something bad that another person has done
contexts: She told us a tale about a magic forest.
He came back with tales of his adventures.
Don't tell tales on your brother.

words.definition: 1. (phrasal verb) to persuade someone to do something
contexts: She talked me into going to the party.

words.definition: 1. (phrasal verb) to discuss something with someone, especially before making a decision
contexts: Let's talk it over before we decide.

words.definition: 1. (idiom) to talk about your work when you are with people socially
contexts: Let's not talk shop at dinner.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a TV or radio programme in which famous people are asked questions about their lives
Note: In British English: chat show.
contexts: She was a guest on a late-night talk show.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to train a wild animal to be calm and not afraid of people
2. (verb) to control something that is difficult or dangerous
3. (adjective) (of an animal) not wild or afraid of people
4. (adjective) not exciting or interesting
contexts: They tamed a wild horse.
The government is trying to tame inflation.
The birds are so tame they eat from your hand.
The party was pretty tame.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a large container for holding liquid or gas
2. (noun) a heavy military vehicle with a large gun that moves on metal belts
3. (noun) a glass container for fish
4. (verb) to fail badly
Note: The verb is informal.
contexts: The car has a petrol tank.
Tanks rolled into the city.
We keep tropical fish in a tank.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to hit someone or something lightly, often several times

7. (idiom) (on ~) (of beer) served from a barrel

contexts: Someone tapped me on the shoulder.
Tap the icon to open the app.
The police tapped his phone.
We need to tap into new markets.
Turn off the tap.
I heard a tap at the window.
They have three beers on tap.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to pull paper or cloth apart, or make a hole in it

3. (verb) to move very quickly

contexts: She tore the letter in half.
This material tears easily.
He tore down the street.
There's a tear in your shirt.
Tears ran down her face.
She burst into tears when she heard the news.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to destroy a building, wall or other structure
2. (phrasal verb) to pull something off a wall
contexts: They tore down the old factory to build flats.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to pull something such as paper into small pieces
2. (phrasal verb) to say that an agreement is no longer valid
3. (phrasal verb) to start to have tears in your eyes
Note: In the last meaning, "tear" rhymes with "fear" and the past is "teared".
contexts: She tore up the letter and threw it away.
The government tore up the treaty.
He teared up during his speech.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a person who knows a lot about computers and technology
Note: Informal.
contexts: Ask Sam – he's a real techie.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) connected with the use of science and machines in industry and everyday life
contexts: We live in an age of rapid technological change.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the years of your life between the ages of 13 and 19
2. (noun) young people aged between 13 and 19
Note: Informal.
contexts: She started writing in her teens.
The show is popular with teens.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a building where people go to pray in some religions, such as Buddhism and Hinduism
2. (noun) the flat part on each side of your head, between your eye and your ear
contexts: We visited an ancient temple in Thailand.
He had grey hair at his temples.

words.definition: 1. (adverb) for a short time only
contexts: The shop is temporarily closed.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) lasting or used for only a short time
contexts: She has a temporary job for the summer.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a person who pays rent to live in a house or flat or to use an office
contexts: The landlord asked the tenants to leave.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a habit of behaving in a particular way, or a quality that is likely to happen
2. (noun) a new way of thinking or behaving that is starting to develop
contexts: He has a tendency to talk too much.
There is a growing tendency to work from home.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) nervous and worried, and not able to relax
2. (adjective) (of a situation) making people nervous because something bad might happen
3. (adjective) (of a muscle) tight and not relaxed

contexts: She was very tense before the exam.
The atmosphere at the meeting was tense.
My shoulders are tense.
“Went” is the past tense of “go”.
He tensed his arm.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a feeling of worry or nervousness that makes it impossible to relax
2. (noun) a situation in which people or countries do not trust each other and may fight
3. (noun) tightness in a muscle, rope or wire
contexts: You could feel the tension in the room.
There is growing tension between the two countries.
Massage helps to reduce tension in the back.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a building at an airport where passengers arrive and leave
2. (noun) a building at the end of a bus, train or ship route
3. (noun) a keyboard and screen connected to a main computer

contexts: Our flight leaves from Terminal 2.
The bus terminal is downtown.
Each desk has a computer terminal.
He has terminal cancer.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the conditions of an agreement or contract

3. (idiom) (on good/bad ~) having a good or bad relationship with someone
4. (idiom) (come to ~ with) to slowly accept something sad or difficult

In terms of money, the job is great.
She's on good terms with her ex-husband.
He's still coming to terms with his wife's death.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a house that is one of a row of houses joined together by their side walls
Note: British. In American English: row house.
contexts: They live in a small terraced house in London.

words.definition:
1. (adverb) very, or extremely

words.definition: 1. (adjective) very, very frightened

words.definition:
1. (verb) to make someone extremely frightened
Note: terrify – terrified – terrified.
contexts: Flying terrifies me.

words.definition:
1. (noun) land that is controlled by a particular country or ruler

3. (noun) an area of knowledge or experience
contexts: The plane flew over enemy territory.
Dogs mark their territory.
We're moving into new territory with this project.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a feeling of extreme fear
2. (noun) violence used to make people afraid, for political reasons

Note: The last meaning is informal.
contexts: She screamed in terror.
The country suffered years of terror.
Their son is a little terror.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the use of violence, such as bombs and killings, to frighten people and achieve political aims
contexts: The government is fighting terrorism.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a person who uses violence, such as bombs and killings, to frighten people and achieve political aims
2. (adjective) connected with such violence
contexts: The terrorists planted a bomb in the station.
There was a terrorist attack in the city.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the process of checking something to see if it works or is safe, or someone to see what they know
2. (adjective) difficult and needing a lot of effort
contexts: The new drug is still in testing.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a book that teaches a particular subject, used by students

contexts: Open your textbooks at page 20.

words.definition:
1. (verb) (of ice or snow) to turn into water as it gets warmer

words.definition:
1. (noun) the crime of stealing something

words.definition: 1. (noun) a person whose job is to treat people with mental or physical problems, often by talking with them or by exercise
contexts: She sees a therapist every week.

words.definition:
1. (noun) treatment for a mental or physical problem, usually without drugs or operations
Note: Plural: therapies.
contexts: She's in therapy for depression.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a long piece of writing on a subject that you write for a university degree
2. (noun) an idea or argument that someone tries to show is true
Note: Plural: theses.

The book's main thesis is that we need less money to be happy.

words.definition: 1. (phrasal verb) to consider something carefully before you decide

words.definition:

words.definition:
1. (adjective) done carefully and completely, with attention to every detail

words.definition:
1. (adverb) completely, or very much

words.definition:
1. (adjective) kind and thinking about what other people need or want

contexts: It was very thoughtful of you to bring flowers.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a statement that someone will hurt you or cause you problems if you do not do what they want

words.definition:

words.definition: 1. (adjective) very pleased and excited

words.definition: 1. (idiom) in good times and bad times, without stopping to support someone

words.definition:
1. (noun) the low, dull sound of something heavy falling or hitting something

words.definition:
1. (noun) the short, thick finger at the side of your hand

words.definition:
1. (verb) to hit someone or something hard, often with your closed hand

words.definition:

words.definition:
1. (noun) a school or college that trains people in a special skill
2. (noun) an organization of people who work to develop art, science or literature
contexts: He studied at a military academy.
She's a member of the Royal Academy of Arts.

words.definition:
1. (verb) (of a vehicle or person) to go faster
2. (verb) to make something happen sooner or faster
contexts: The car accelerated down the hill.
The government wants to accelerate economic growth.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the act of agreeing to take something that is offered
2. (noun) the act of agreeing that something is true or right
3. (noun) the process of allowing someone to become part of a group
4. (noun) the act of agreeing to a difficult situation that you cannot change
contexts: Her acceptance of the job surprised us.
There is growing acceptance that climate change is real.
He wanted acceptance from his classmates.
She showed calm acceptance of her illness.

words.definition:
1. (noun) how easy it is to reach, enter or use something, especially for people with disabilities
2. (noun) how easy something is to understand
contexts: The new station improves accessibility for wheelchair users.
The book is known for its accessibility.

words.definition:
1. (noun) something difficult or impressive that you have succeeded in doing
2. (noun) a skill that you have learned
contexts: Winning the prize was a great accomplishment.
Speaking three languages is one of her accomplishments.

words.definition:
1. (adverb) in a way that is suitable for the situation
2. (adverb) for that reason, therefore
Note: Formal.
contexts: You're adults, so please behave accordingly.
Prices went up. Accordingly, sales fell.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to give the reason for something or explain it
2. (phrasal verb) to form a particular part of a total
3. (phrasal verb) to know where someone or something is
contexts: How do you account for the missing money?
Students account for 20% of the town's population.
All passengers have been accounted for.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the fact of being responsible for your decisions and actions, and being expected to explain them
contexts: There must be more accountability in government.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) responsible for your decisions and actions, and expected to explain them
contexts: Politicians should be held accountable for their actions.

words.definition: 1. (verb) to slowly get more and more of something over a period of time
contexts: He accumulated a lot of money.

words.definition:
1. (noun) an amount of something that has slowly grown over time
2. (noun) the process of slowly getting more of something
contexts: There was an accumulation of snow on the roof.
The accumulation of wealth was his only goal.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a statement saying that someone has done something wrong or illegal
contexts: She made false accusations against him.

words.definition:
1. (noun) (the ~) the person or people in a court who are said to have done a crime
2. (adjective) said to have done something wrong or illegal
Note: Plural (noun): the accused.
contexts: The accused was found not guilty.
The accused man stood up.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) (~ to) familiar with something so that it seems normal
2. (adjective) usual
Note: Formal.
contexts: My eyes slowly became accustomed to the dark.
He sat in his accustomed seat.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a person you know, but not well
2. (noun) knowledge of something
3. (idiom) (make someone's ~) to meet someone for the first time
contexts: She's an acquaintance from work, not a close friend.
I have some acquaintance with French law.
I'm pleased to make your acquaintance.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the process of getting or learning something
2. (noun) something that someone has recently bought or got
3. (noun) the act of one company buying another company
contexts: Children's language acquisition is fast.
The painting is the museum's latest acquisition.
The bank announced the acquisition of a smaller rival.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a unit for measuring land, equal to about 4,047 square metres
contexts: The farm covers 200 acres.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) (of a machine or part of the body) to not work as it should
2. (phrasal verb) (of a child) to behave badly
Note: Informal.
contexts: My computer is acting up again.
The kids always act up when we have guests.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the act of making something start working
contexts: Account activation takes 24 hours.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a person who works hard to bring political or social change
contexts: Environmental activists protested outside the factory.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) very serious or severe
2. (adjective) (of an illness) coming suddenly and serious for a short time
3. (adjective) (of the senses) very good and sensitive
4. (adjective) quick to notice and understand things
5. (adjective) (of an angle) less than 90 degrees
contexts: There is an acute shortage of nurses.
He has acute appendicitis.
Dogs have an acute sense of smell.
She's an acute observer of human behaviour.
Draw an acute angle.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a film, TV show or play that is based on a book
2. (noun) a change that makes something suitable for a new situation or use
3. (noun) the process of changing to fit a new situation
contexts: The film is an adaptation of a famous novel.
Wings are an adaptation that lets birds fly.
Adaptation to life in a new country takes time.

words.definition:
1. (verb) (~ to) to follow a rule, law or belief exactly
2. (verb) to stick firmly to a surface
Note: Formal.
contexts: All members must adhere to the rules.
The paint did not adhere to the wall.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) next to or very near something
Note: Formal.
contexts: They live in the house adjacent to ours.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a small change made to something to improve it
2. (noun) the process of getting used to a new situation
contexts: I made a few adjustments to the plan.
Moving to the city required a big adjustment.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to manage or organize something, such as a company or system
2. (verb) to give someone medicine or a drug
3. (verb) to give a punishment or test to someone
Note: Formal.
contexts: The fund is administered by a charity.
The nurse administered the injection.
The test was administered to all students.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) connected with managing and organizing the work of a company or institution
contexts: She has an administrative job at the hospital.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a person whose job is to manage and organize the work of a company or institution
2. (noun) a person who manages a computer system or website
contexts: She works as a school administrator.
Contact the system administrator if you forget your password.

words.definition:
1. (noun) permission to enter a place or join a school or organization
2. (noun) the money you pay to enter a place
3. (noun) a statement saying that you did something wrong or that something is true
4. (noun) the act of taking someone into hospital
contexts: He applied for admission to the university.
Admission is free for children.
His silence was an admission of guilt.
Hospital admissions rise in winter.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the period of life when a child develops into an adult, between about 13 and 18
contexts: Adolescence can be a difficult time.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a young person who is developing from a child into an adult
2. (adjective) connected with young people who are developing into adults
contexts: The book is written for adolescents.
She studies adolescent behaviour.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the legal process of taking another person's child into your family and becoming its parent
2. (noun) the act of starting to use a plan, method or idea
contexts: They're thinking about adoption.
The adoption of new technology has been slow.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) negative, harmful or not good for something
Note: Formal.
contexts: The drug has no adverse effects.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a very difficult or unlucky situation
Note: Formal.
contexts: She showed great courage in the face of adversity.

words.definition:
1. (noun) public support for an idea, plan or group of people
Note: Formal.
contexts: She is known for her advocacy of women's rights.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to publicly support or recommend an idea or plan
2. (noun) a person who publicly supports an idea, plan or group
3. (noun) a lawyer who speaks for someone in court
Note: The verb ends like "late"; the noun ends like "it".
contexts: He advocates a ban on smoking in parks.
She's a strong advocate of free education.
He hired an advocate to defend him.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) connected with beauty and art, and how things look
2. (noun) the way something looks, or a set of ideas about what is beautiful
Note: American spelling also: esthetic.
contexts: The building has great aesthetic value.
I love the clean aesthetic of Japanese design.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a feeling of liking or loving someone or something
contexts: He has great affection for his grandmother.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) having a lot of money and a good standard of living
Note: Formal.
contexts: They live in an affluent area of the city.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the fact of being cheap enough for people to buy
contexts: Housing affordability is a big problem for young people.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the period after a bad event such as a war, storm or accident, and the effects it causes
contexts: Many people lost their jobs in the aftermath of the crisis.

words.definition: 1. (idiom) in a hurry because there is not much time to finish something
contexts: We were working against the clock to finish the report.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to make a bad situation, illness or injury worse
2. (verb) to annoy someone
Note: The meaning "annoy" is informal.
contexts: Running will only aggravate your knee injury.
Stop aggravating your sister!

words.definition:
1. (noun) a total made by adding several amounts or things together
2. (adjective) made by adding several amounts or things together
Note: Formal.
contexts: They won 4–2 on aggregate over two games.
The aggregate cost of the project was $5 million.

words.definition:
1. (noun) angry or violent behaviour or feelings towards another person
2. (noun) an attack by one country on another without a good reason
contexts: Some dogs show aggression towards strangers.
The invasion was an act of aggression.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) able to move quickly and easily
2. (adjective) able to think quickly and clearly
3. (adjective) (of a company or way of working) able to change quickly
contexts: Monkeys are very agile climbers.
She has an agile mind.
Small companies are often more agile.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) connected with farming
contexts: Most of the land here is agricultural.

words.definition: 1. (idiom) earlier than planned or expected
contexts: Book your tickets ahead of time.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a person who helps an important person, such as a politician, in their work
contexts: The president's aides were in the room.

words.definition:
1. (conjunction) although
Note: Formal.
contexts: He agreed, albeit unwillingly.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) watching and ready to notice and deal with anything that happens
2. (adjective) (~ to) knowing about a possible danger
3. (verb) to warn someone about a danger or problem
4. (noun) a warning about a possible danger
5. (noun) a message on a phone or computer that tells you about something
6. (idiom) (on the ~) ready to deal with possible danger
contexts: Stay alert while driving.
Doctors should be alert to the signs of the illness.
A neighbour alerted the police.
The police issued a flood alert.
I got an alert about a new email.
The army is on high alert.

words.definition:
1. (noun) proof that someone was in another place when a crime happened
2. (noun) an excuse
contexts: He has a strong alibi – he was at work all day.
Being busy is his alibi for everything.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to arrange things in a straight line or in the correct position
2. (verb) (~ yourself with) to publicly agree with or support a person or group
3. (verb) to make plans or ideas match each other
Note: The "g" is not pronounced.
contexts: Align the text to the left.
The party aligned itself with the unions.
Our goals are closely aligned.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the arrangement of things in a straight line or in the correct position
2. (noun) agreement or support between people, groups or countries
contexts: The car's wheels are out of alignment.
The two parties are in alignment on this issue.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) very similar
2. (adverb) in the same or a similar way
3. (adverb) used to say that two groups are both included
contexts: The two sisters look alike.
They dress alike.
The show is popular with adults and children alike.

words.definition:
1. (idiom) everywhere, in many different places
2. (idiom) not organized, or in a confused state
Note: Informal.
contexts: There were toys all over the place.
Since she left, I've been all over the place.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a statement saying that someone has done something wrong or illegal, without proof
contexts: He denies all the allegations against him.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to say that someone has done something wrong or illegal, without giving proof
Note: Formal.
contexts: She alleges that her boss stole money.

words.definition: 1. (adverb) according to what people say, although it has not been proved
contexts: He allegedly stole a car.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to make pain or a problem less serious
Note: Formal.
contexts: The drug helps to alleviate the pain.

words.definition:
1. (noun) an agreement between countries, groups or people to work together
2. (noun) a group of countries or organizations that have agreed to work together
contexts: The two countries formed an alliance.
NATO is a military alliance.

words.definition: 1. (verb) to officially give something, such as money or time, to someone or for a particular purpose
contexts: The government allocated $1 million to the project.

words.definition:
1. (noun) an amount of money, time or space that is given for a particular purpose
2. (noun) the process of giving something to people for a particular purpose
contexts: Each school receives an allocation of funds.
The allocation of tickets will be done by lottery.

words.definition:
1. (noun) money that someone is given regularly for a particular purpose
2. (noun) money that parents give to a child regularly
3. (noun) an amount of something that is allowed
4. (idiom) (make ~s for) to accept someone's bad behaviour because of a special situation
Note: The meaning "money for a child" is American. In British English: pocket money.
contexts: He gets a travel allowance from his company.
Her parents give her a weekly allowance.
What's the baggage allowance on this flight?
We should make allowances for her because she's ill.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a country that agrees to help or support another country, especially in a war
2. (noun) a person who helps and supports you
3. (verb) (~ yourself with) to join with another person or group to support them
Note: Plural: allies.
contexts: The US and Britain are close allies.
She has been a loyal ally.
The party allied itself with the greens.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a light, silver-grey metal used for making cans, foil and planes
Note: British spelling: aluminium.
contexts: Drinks cans are made of aluminum.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) doing something for fun and not as a job
2. (noun) a person who does an activity for fun and not as a job
3. (noun) a person who is not skilled at something
contexts: He's an amateur photographer.
The tournament is open to amateurs.
Compared to her, I'm just an amateur.

words.definition:
1. (noun) an important official who represents their country in another country
2. (noun) a person who represents or supports a group or idea
contexts: She is the French ambassador to Japan.
He's a goodwill ambassador for the UN.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the state of having more than one possible meaning, so that it is not clear
contexts: There is some ambiguity in the contract.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) having more than one possible meaning, so that it is not clear
contexts: Her answer was ambiguous.

words.definition: 1. (verb) to walk slowly and calmly, without hurrying
contexts: We ambled along the river bank.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to attack someone suddenly from a hidden place
2. (noun) a sudden attack from a hidden place
contexts: The soldiers were ambushed on the road.
Three soldiers were killed in the ambush.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to make small changes to a law, document or statement, to improve it or make it more correct
Note: Formal.
contexts: The law was amended in 2010.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a small change to a law, document or statement
2. (noun) (with a capital A) one of the official changes added to the US Constitution
contexts: They made several amendments to the contract.
The First Amendment protects free speech.

words.definition:
1. (noun) something that makes a place pleasant, comfortable or easy to live in, such as a park, pool or shop
Note: Usually used in the plural: amenities.
contexts: The hotel has excellent amenities.

words.definition:
1. (preposition) in the middle of, or among
2. (preposition) during a time of something, especially something bad
Note: Formal. Also: amidst.
contexts: The house stood amid the trees.
The minister resigned amid rumours of a scandal.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) enough, or more than enough
2. (adjective) large
contexts: There is ample time to finish.
She has an ample figure.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a comparison between two things that shows how they are similar, used to explain something
contexts: The teacher made an analogy between the heart and a pump.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a heavy metal object on a long chain that is dropped into the water to stop a ship from moving
2. (noun) a person who reads the news on TV and introduces reports
3. (noun) a person or thing that gives support and makes you feel safe
4. (verb) to stop a ship from moving with a heavy object on a chain
5. (verb) to fix something firmly in position
Note: The "ch" sounds like "k".
contexts: The ship dropped anchor in the bay.
She's a news anchor on CNN.
My family is my anchor.
We anchored near the island.
The tent was anchored to the ground.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a short, interesting or funny story about a real person or event
contexts: He told us an amusing anecdote about his first job.

words.definition:
1. (noun) (in some religions) a spirit who serves God, often shown as a person with wings
2. (noun) a very kind and good person
contexts: There's an angel on top of the Christmas tree.
Thanks for your help – you're an angel!

words.definition: 1. (noun) the illegal buying and selling of wild creatures or parts of their bodies
contexts: Animal trafficking threatens many species with extinction.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) (of a person) with a name that is not known or not made public
2. (adjective) done or written by someone whose name is not known
3. (adjective) without interesting features
contexts: The money was given by an anonymous donor.
She received an anonymous letter.
It was a large, anonymous office building.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the equipment or tools used for a particular activity or purpose
2. (noun) the structure of an organization or system
Note: Plural: apparatus or apparatuses.
contexts: The firefighters wore breathing apparatus.
The apparatus of government was very slow.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) attractive or interesting
contexts: The idea of a holiday is very appealing.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a section with extra information at the end of a book or report
2. (noun) a small tube-shaped organ inside the body near the stomach
Note: Plural: appendixes or appendices.
contexts: The tables are in the appendix.
He had his appendix removed.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to clap your hands to show that you liked a performance or speech
2. (verb) to praise someone or something
contexts: The audience applauded loudly.
We applaud her courage.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) suitable for or connected with a particular person or situation
contexts: The rules are applicable to everyone.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to officially choose someone for a job or position
2. (verb) to decide on a time or place for something
contexts: She was appointed head of the department.
We met at the appointed time.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the feeling of being thankful for something
2. (noun) an understanding of the value or importance of something
3. (noun) an understanding of a situation or problem
4. (noun) an increase in value over time
contexts: She gave him a gift to show her appreciation.
He has a deep appreciation of music.
They have no appreciation of the risks.
The house has had a large appreciation in value.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) worried or a little afraid that something bad might happen
contexts: She was apprehensive about her first day at work.

words.definition: 1. (noun) an extreme fear of spiders
contexts: My brother suffers from arachnophobia.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) based on chance or a personal decision, not on reason or a system
2. (adjective) (of power) used without considering what other people want or need
contexts: The choice of colour was completely arbitrary.
The arbitrary arrest of protesters caused anger.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) connected with the design of buildings
contexts: The city has many architectural treasures.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a collection of historical documents or records, or the place where they are kept
2. (noun) a place on a computer where old files or messages are stored
3. (verb) to store documents or files in a safe place to keep them
Note: The noun is often plural: archives. The "ch" sounds like "k".
contexts: The film was found in the national archive.
Check the email archive.
Old emails are archived after a year.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a large building with seats around a central area, used for sports or entertainment
2. (noun) an area of activity, especially one where people compete
contexts: The concert is at the city arena.
She entered the political arena in 2010.

words.definition: 1. (adverb) used to say that something could be true, and there are good reasons to think it
contexts: She is arguably the best singer of her time.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) (of land or weather) very dry, with very little rain
2. (adjective) boring and without new ideas
contexts: Few plants grow in this arid region.
It was an arid discussion.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to make someone have a particular feeling or reaction, such as interest or suspicion
2. (verb) to make someone feel sexually excited
3. (verb) to wake someone up
Note: Formal.
contexts: His strange behaviour aroused suspicion.
He was aroused by her voice.
She was aroused from a deep sleep.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a large group or range of things of the same type
2. (verb) to arrange things in an attractive or ordered way
Note: Formal.
contexts: The shop sells a wide array of cheeses.
The dishes were arrayed on the table.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the crime of setting fire to a building or other property on purpose
contexts: The police believe the fire was arson.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a person who sets fire to buildings or other property on purpose
contexts: The arsonist was caught on camera.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to express ideas or feelings clearly in words
2. (verb) to pronounce words clearly
3. (adjective) able to express ideas clearly in words
Note: The verb ends like "late"; the adjective ends like "it".
contexts: She found it hard to articulate her feelings.
He articulated every word carefully.
She's a very articulate young woman.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the grey or black powder that is left after something burns
2. (noun) (~es) what is left of a person's body after it has been burned
3. (noun) a tall tree with grey bark
contexts: He dropped cigarette ash on the carpet.
They scattered her ashes in the sea.
An old ash tree stood in the garden.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a strong hope or wish to achieve something
contexts: She has aspirations to become a lawyer.

words.definition: 1. (verb) (~ to) to have a strong wish to achieve something or become someone
contexts: He aspires to be a doctor.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) hoping to become successful in a particular job or activity
contexts: The workshop is for aspiring writers.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a person who attacks someone, especially physically
Note: Formal.
contexts: She did not recognize her assailant.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the murder of an important or famous person, especially for political reasons
contexts: The assassination of President Kennedy shocked the world.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a violent physical attack on a person
2. (noun) a military attack
3. (noun) a strong criticism or attempt to stop something
4. (verb) to attack someone violently
contexts: He was charged with assault.
The army launched an assault on the city.
The new law is an assault on free speech.
He assaulted a police officer.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to come together in a group, or to bring people or things together
2. (verb) to fit the parts of something together
contexts: A crowd assembled outside the building.
The furniture is easy to assemble.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a group of people who meet to make laws or decisions
2. (noun) a meeting of all the students and teachers in a school
3. (noun) the process of putting together the parts of something
4. (noun) the act of people coming together in a group
contexts: The national assembly voted on the new law.
We have assembly every morning at nine.
The furniture comes with assembly instructions.
Everyone has the right of free assembly.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to say firmly that something is true
2. (verb) to make people accept your rights or authority
3. (verb) (~ yourself) to behave in a confident way so that people notice you
contexts: He asserted that he was innocent.
She needs to assert her rights.
You must learn to assert yourself at work.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a statement that you firmly believe is true
contexts: I don't agree with his assertion that money brings happiness.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a promise that something will happen or is true, so that you do not worry
2. (noun) a feeling of confidence in yourself
3. (noun) a type of insurance, especially for life
Note: The meaning about insurance is British.
contexts: He gave me his assurance that he would pay.
She spoke with calm assurance.
He has a life assurance policy.

words.definition:
1. (noun) protection that a government gives to people who have left their own country because they were in danger
2. (noun) a hospital for people with mental illness, in the past
Note: The second meaning is old-fashioned.
contexts: They asked for political asylum.
She spent years in an asylum.

words.definition: 1. (noun) an extremely cruel and violent act, especially in a war
contexts: Both sides committed atrocities during the war.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to succeed in getting or reaching something, usually after a lot of effort
Note: Formal.
contexts: She attained her goal of becoming a doctor.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the act of going to or being at an event, school or meeting
2. (noun) the number of people who are at an event
3. (idiom) (in ~) present at an event
contexts: Attendance at all lessons is required.
Attendance at the match was 40,000.
Several famous people were in attendance.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a lawyer, especially one who speaks for people in court
Note: Mainly American.
contexts: You should talk to an attorney.

words.definition:
1. (verb) (~ to) to say or believe that something is caused by someone or something
2. (verb) (~ to) to say that someone wrote, said or made something
3. (noun) a quality or feature of someone or something
Note: The verb is stressed on "trib"; the noun on "at".
contexts: She attributes her success to hard work.
The painting is attributed to Rembrandt.
Patience is an important attribute for a teacher.

words.definition:
1. (noun) an official check of the financial records of a company or organization
2. (noun) a careful check of something to see if it is working well
3. (verb) to officially check the financial records of a company
contexts: The company has an audit every year.
We did an energy audit of the house.
The accounts are audited by an outside firm.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a situation in which a government spends much less money to reduce its debts
2. (noun) a simple way of life without comfort or luxury
contexts: The country has been through years of austerity.
The monks live a life of austerity.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) real and not a copy
2. (adjective) made or done in the traditional or original way
3. (adjective) true and based on facts
contexts: Is this an authentic painting by Picasso?
We had authentic Mexican food.
The film gives an authentic picture of life in the war.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to give official permission for something

words.definition:
1. (noun) a car

words.definition: 1. (verb) to make a process work by machines or computers instead of people

words.definition: 1. (noun) the use of machines and computers instead of people to do work

words.definition:

Note: Formal.
contexts: The region wants more autonomy.

words.definition:

words.definition:
1. (verb) to wait for something

Note: Formal.
contexts: We are awaiting news of the election results.
A warm welcome awaits you.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a feeling of great respect mixed with wonder and sometimes fear

words.definition:

2. (phrasal verb) to stop trying to make someone do something or criticizing them
3. (phrasal verb) to decide not to continue with a plan or claim

words.definition:

contexts: The mountains made a beautiful backdrop for the photos.

words.definition:
1. (noun) help or support, often money

words.definition: 1. (noun) a strong negative reaction by many people against something

words.definition:

words.definition:

words.definition:

words.definition:

words.definition:
1. (noun) a number that is not exact but close to the right one

words.definition:
1. (noun) a long piece of cloth with a message on it, often carried between two poles
2. (noun) an advertisement across the top of a web page

Click on the banner to find out more.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) not covered by clothes

words.definition:
1. (noun) a large round container with flat ends, made of wood or metal, for storing liquids

words.definition:

contexts: Turn up the bass – I love this song.
He plays bass in a rock band.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a place where a battle is fought

Education has become a political battlefield.

words.definition:
1. (noun) an area of sea that is partly surrounded by land

contexts: We sailed into the bay.
Park in the loading bay.
She drinks lots of tea to keep colds at bay.
Add a bay leaf to the soup.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a line of light from the sun or a lamp

5. (verb) to send radio or TV signals
contexts: A beam of sunlight came through the window.

The match was beamed around the world.

words.definition: 1. (phrasal verb) to be patient with someone while they do something

words.definition:
1. (noun) a large, wild or dangerous animal

words.definition:

words.definition:
1. (noun) a standard or level that other things are compared with

contexts: The test results are a benchmark for measuring progress.

words.definition:

Note: Formal.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a person who gets money or an advantage from something

words.definition:
1. (verb) to hurt someone who trusts you, by not being loyal to them
2. (verb) to give secret information to an enemy
3. (verb) to show a feeling that you are trying to hide
contexts: He betrayed his best friend.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to tie someone or something firmly with rope or string

words.definition: 1. (noun) the large number and variety of plants and animals that live in a particular place

words.definition: 1. (noun) the story of a person's life, written by another person

words.definition: 1. (adjective) very strange and unusual

words.definition:
1. (noun) the flat, sharp part of a knife, sword or tool that cuts

words.definition:
1. (noun) an explosion

5. (verb) to break something with explosives
6. (verb) to make a very loud noise, especially music

contexts: Five people were hurt in the blast.
A blast of cold air came through the door.
He gave a blast on his whistle.
The party was a blast!

The newspapers blasted the government.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) without hope or good things to expect
2. (adjective) (of a place) cold, empty and not attractive
3. (adjective) (of weather) cold and grey
contexts: The future looks bleak.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to lose blood from your body
2. (verb) (of colour) to spread into something else
Note: bleed – bled – bled.
contexts: My nose is bleeding.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to mix two or more things together

words.definition:

words.definition:

words.definition:

words.definition:

words.definition:

words.definition:

words.definition:
