3. (adjective) (of a person) having a bad habit for a long time
contexts: She suffers from chronic back pain.
There's a chronic shortage of housing.
He's a chronic liar.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) arranged in the order in which events happened
contexts: List the events in chronological order.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) very pleased and proud
Note: British, informal.
contexts: I'm chuffed to bits with my new car.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a thick, solid piece of something
2. (noun) a large part or amount of something
contexts: Cut the meat into chunks.
The rent takes a big chunk of my salary.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to move continuously around a closed system or area
2. (verb) (of information or a story) to pass from person to person
3. (verb) to send something to a group of people
4. (verb) to move around and talk to different people at a party
contexts: Blood circulates around the body.
Rumours are circulating about the company.
The report was circulated to all staff.
She circulated among the guests.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the movement of blood around the body
2. (noun) the number of copies of a newspaper or magazine that are sold
3. (noun) the passing of something from one person or place to another
contexts: Exercise improves your circulation.
The paper has a circulation of 2 million.
There are fake coins in circulation.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the legal right to belong to a particular country
2. (noun) the duties and behaviour expected of a member of a society
contexts: She applied for British citizenship.
Schools should teach good citizenship.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) connected with a town or city, or the people who live in it
contexts: The mayor has many civic duties.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a person who is not a member of the army, navy, air force or police
2. (adjective) not connected with the army, navy or air force
contexts: Many civilians were killed in the attack.
He returned to civilian life after the war.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to suddenly stop talking or refuse to talk, often because you are nervous or shy
Note: Informal.
contexts: Whenever I ask about his past, he clams up.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the quality of being clear and easy to understand
2. (noun) the ability to think clearly
3. (noun) the quality of being easy to see or hear
contexts: The instructions lack clarity.
After a good sleep, I had more clarity.
The photos have amazing clarity.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a short fight between two groups of people
2. (noun) a serious disagreement or argument
3. (noun) a situation in which two events happen at the same time, so you cannot go to both
4. (verb) to fight or argue with someone
5. (verb) (of colours) to look ugly together
6. (verb) (of events) to happen at the same time
contexts: There were clashes between police and protesters.
There was a clash of opinions at the meeting.
There's a clash between my two classes.
Protesters clashed with police.
Your red shirt clashes with your orange trousers.
The concert clashes with my exam.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the process of putting things into groups according to their type
2. (noun) a group that something is put into
contexts: The classification of plants is a complex science.
The film has a 15 classification.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to hold on tightly to someone or something
2. (verb) to stick to something
3. (verb) (~ to) to continue to believe or hope for something, even when it is unlikely
Note: cling – clung – clung.
contexts: The child clung to her mother.
Her wet dress clung to her body.
She clung to the hope that he was alive.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) connected with the treatment of patients, not with theory
2. (adjective) showing no feelings, cold
3. (adjective) (of a room) very clean and plain
contexts: The drug is now in clinical trials.
He spoke in a cool, clinical way.
The office was white and clinical.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the permanent closing of a business, school or hospital
2. (noun) the temporary closing of a road or bridge
3. (noun) a feeling that a difficult experience is finally over
contexts: The factory closure cost 300 jobs.
There are road closures in the city centre.
The trial gave the family some closure.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a group of similar things or people close together
2. (verb) to come together in a small group
contexts: A cluster of houses stood by the river.
People clustered around the fire.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a government formed by two or more political parties working together
2. (noun) a group of people or organizations who join together for a shared purpose
contexts: The two parties formed a coalition government.
A coalition of charities is fighting the plan.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) on or near the land along the sea
contexts: They live in a small coastal town.

words.definition:
1. (noun) an alcoholic drink made by mixing two or more drinks, or juice and alcohol
2. (noun) a mixture of different things, often dangerous
contexts: We had cocktails by the pool.
The drug was a deadly cocktail of chemicals.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) connected with thinking, understanding, learning and remembering
Note: Formal.
contexts: Reading helps children's cognitive development.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the quality of being logical, clear and well organized
contexts: The essay lacks coherence.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) (of ideas or a plan) logical, clear and well organized
2. (adjective) (of a person) able to speak clearly so others can understand
contexts: They need a coherent plan.
He was too upset to be coherent.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to happen at the same time as something else
2. (verb) (of ideas or opinions) to be the same
contexts: Her visit coincided with the festival.
Our views on this coincide.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to work together with someone to produce or achieve something
2. (verb) to secretly help an enemy who is in control of your country
contexts: The two companies collaborated on the project.
He was accused of collaborating with the enemy.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the act of working together with others to produce or achieve something
2. (noun) something produced by people working together
contexts: The book was written in collaboration with a journalist.
The album is a collaboration between two singers.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) shared or done by all the members of a group
2. (noun) a business or farm owned and run by the people who work in it
contexts: It was a collective decision.
She works in an artists' collective.

words.definition:
1. (noun) an accident in which two vehicles or people hit each other
2. (noun) a strong disagreement between people or ideas
contexts: Three people were hurt in a collision between two cars.
There was a collision of interests.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) connected with a time when a country was ruled by a more powerful country
contexts: India was under colonial rule for many years.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a journalist who writes a regular article for a newspaper or magazine
contexts: She's a fashion columnist for a weekly magazine.

words.definition:
1. (noun) fighting, especially during a war
2. (verb) to try to stop something bad from happening or getting worse
contexts: He was killed in combat.
The government is trying to combat crime.

words.definition: 1. (phrasal verb) to happen, especially in a way that was not planned
contexts: How did the accident come about?

words.definition: 1. (phrasal verb) to offer to help or to give information, especially to the police
contexts: Police asked witnesses to come forward.

words.definition: 1. (verb) (of a law or rule) to officially start to apply
contexts: The new law comes into force next month.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) (of news or a result) to arrive
2. (phrasal verb) to get through a difficult or dangerous situation
3. (phrasal verb) (of a feeling) to be clear to other people
4. (phrasal verb) to do what people hope or expect
contexts: My exam results came through today.
She came through the operation well.
His love for his children comes through in his songs.
She came through for us when we needed help.

words.definition: 1. (verb) to remember an important person or event officially, with a ceremony or special object
contexts: A statue was built to commemorate the soldiers who died.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to begin
Note: Formal.
contexts: The meeting will commence at 10 a.m.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a spoken description of an event, such as a sports game, as it happens on TV or radio
2. (noun) a written explanation or discussion of something
contexts: We listened to the match commentary on the radio.
The book is a commentary on modern society.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a person who describes an event, such as a sports game, on TV or radio
2. (noun) a person who writes or speaks about a subject in newspapers or on TV
contexts: He's a football commentator.
Political commentators expect her to win.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the activity of buying and selling goods and services
contexts: The city is a centre of trade and commerce.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a senior official who is in charge of a government department or organization
2. (noun) a member of a group with official responsibility for something
contexts: The police commissioner held a press conference.
She is an EU commissioner.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a product or raw material, such as oil, coffee or metal, that can be bought and sold
2. (noun) something useful or valuable
contexts: Oil is the country's main commodity.
Time is a precious commodity.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) shared by all the members of a group
contexts: The flats have a communal garden.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) based on a political system in which the government owns and controls all property and businesses
2. (noun) a person who supports this political system
contexts: Cuba has a communist government.
He was a member of the party and a committed communist.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a person who spends time with you or travels with you
2. (noun) a person paid to live with and help an old or ill person
contexts: My dog is my best companion.
She works as a companion to an old lady.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) similar to something else, so that they can be compared
contexts: Prices here are comparable to those in London.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a strong feeling of sympathy for people who are suffering, and a wish to help them
contexts: She showed great compassion for the sick.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) (of computers or devices) able to be used together
2. (adjective) (of people) able to live or work together happily
3. (adjective) (of ideas or facts) able to exist together
contexts: Is this software compatible with my computer?
They're very compatible.
His plans are not compatible with our goals.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to force someone to do something
2. (verb) (feel ~led) to feel that you must do something
Note: compel – compelled – compelled. Formal.
contexts: The law compels parents to send their children to school.
I felt compelled to tell her the truth.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) so interesting or exciting that you have to pay attention
2. (adjective) so strong or convincing that you have to believe or accept it
contexts: It's a compelling story.
There is compelling evidence that he is guilty.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to pay someone money because they have lost something or been hurt
2. (verb) (~ for) to make a bad situation better by having or doing something good
contexts: The company will compensate workers for their injuries.
His enthusiasm compensates for his lack of experience.

words.definition:
1. (noun) money that is paid to someone because they have lost something or been hurt
2. (noun) something good that makes a bad situation better
contexts: She received compensation for her injuries.
The beautiful view was some compensation for the long walk.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the ability to do something well or well enough
contexts: Nobody doubts her competence as a teacher.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) having enough skill or knowledge to do something well
2. (adjective) good enough, but not excellent
contexts: He's a competent driver.
She gave a competent performance.

words.definition: 1. (verb) to collect information from different places and put it together in a list, book or report
contexts: We're compiling a list of the best restaurants.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to go well with something and make it better or more attractive
2. (noun) a thing that goes well with something else and makes it better
3. (noun) the total number needed to make something complete
Note: Don't confuse it with "compliment" (= praise).
contexts: The wine complements the food perfectly.
The sauce is the perfect complement to the fish.
The ship had its full complement of sailors.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the state of having many parts that are connected in a way that makes it difficult to understand
2. (noun) (~ies) the difficult details of something
contexts: I didn't realize the complexity of the problem.
Few people understand the complexities of the tax system.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the act of obeying a rule, law or request
Note: Formal.
contexts: The company is in compliance with safety rules.

words.definition:
1. (noun) something that makes a situation more difficult
2. (noun) a new medical problem that makes an illness or operation worse
contexts: There's a further complication – he's lost his passport.
She died from complications after surgery.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to obey a rule, law or request
Note: comply – complied – complied. Formal.
contexts: All buildings must comply with fire safety rules.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the different parts or people that something is made of
2. (noun) a piece of music or art
3. (noun) a short piece of writing done at school
4. (noun) the act or skill of writing music
5. (noun) the way things are arranged in a picture or photo
contexts: Scientists studied the composition of the soil.
This is one of Mozart's early compositions.
We had to write a composition about our summer.
She studied composition at music school.
The photo has a lovely composition.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to understand something completely
Note: Formal.
contexts: I couldn't comprehend why she was so angry.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the ability to understand something
2. (noun) an exercise that tests how well students understand a piece of writing or speech
contexts: The problem is beyond my comprehension.
We did a reading comprehension in class.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to press something so that it fits into a smaller space
2. (verb) to make a computer file smaller
3. (verb) to make something shorter in time
contexts: The machine compresses the rubbish into blocks.
Compress the files before you email them.
The course compresses two years of study into one.

words.definition:
1. (noun) an agreement in which both sides accept less than they wanted
2. (verb) to reach an agreement by both sides accepting less than they wanted
3. (verb) to do something that harms your beliefs, principles or reputation
4. (verb) to put something in danger
contexts: After hours of talks, they reached a compromise.
We both had to compromise.
I won't compromise my principles.
The leak could compromise national security.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to calculate an amount or number
Note: Formal.
contexts: The program computes the total cost.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to hide something or someone carefully
2. (verb) to not let people know about a feeling or fact
Note: Formal.
contexts: He concealed the gun under his coat.
She couldn't conceal her disappointment.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to admit, often unwillingly, that something is true
2. (verb) to admit that you have lost a game, election or argument
3. (verb) to give something to someone, often unwillingly
4. (verb) (in sports) to let the other team score
contexts: He conceded that he had made a mistake.
The president conceded defeat.
The government conceded the right to strike.
The team conceded two goals in the first half.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to think of a new idea or plan
2. (verb) to imagine something
3. (verb) to become pregnant
contexts: She conceived the idea for the book while travelling.
I can't conceive of a world without music.
They tried for years to conceive.

words.definition:
1. (noun) an idea or understanding of what something is like
2. (noun) the process of forming an idea or plan
3. (noun) the moment when a woman becomes pregnant
contexts: He has no conception of how hard this is.
The project was a success from conception to completion.
The baby was born nine months after conception.

words.definition:
1. (noun) something that you allow or give up to end a disagreement
2. (noun) a lower price for students, children or old people
3. (noun) a right to sell something or to do business in a particular place
contexts: Both sides made concessions.
There are ticket concessions for students.
The company has a mining concession.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) giving information clearly and in a few words
contexts: Write a concise summary of the article.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to say very strongly that you think something is wrong
2. (verb) to give someone a severe punishment
3. (verb) to force someone to live in a bad situation
4. (verb) to say officially that a building is not safe to use
Note: The "n" at the end is not pronounced.
contexts: World leaders condemned the attack.
He was condemned to death.
Poverty condemns many children to a life without hope.
The old school was condemned.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to discuss something with other people before making a decision
2. (verb) to officially give someone a title, degree or honour
Note: confer – conferred – conferred. Formal.
contexts: The judges conferred before announcing the winner.
The university conferred an honorary degree on her.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a statement in which you admit that you have done something wrong or illegal
2. (noun) a statement of something that you feel embarrassed about
3. (noun) the act of telling a priest about the bad things you have done
contexts: He made a full confession to the police.
I have a confession to make – I ate your cake.
She goes to confession every week.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) meant to be kept secret and not shared with other people
contexts: This information is strictly confidential.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the way the parts of something are arranged
2. (noun) the settings of a computer program or system
contexts: The seats can be put in different configurations.
Check the network configuration.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to keep something within the limits of a particular area, subject or group
2. (verb) to keep someone in a closed space that they cannot leave
3. (idiom) (be ~d to bed) to have to stay in bed because of illness
contexts: Please confine your comments to the topic.
He was confined to a small room.
She was confined to bed for a week.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a statement or document that shows that something is true or definite
2. (noun) a ceremony in which a person becomes a full member of a Christian church
contexts: You will receive a confirmation of your booking by email.
She had her confirmation at 13.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to behave in the same way as most other people
2. (verb) (~ to) to obey a rule or meet a standard
contexts: Teenagers feel pressure to conform.
The building does not conform to safety rules.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to deal with a difficult situation or problem directly
2. (verb) to face someone in an angry or threatening way
3. (verb) (of a problem) to appear and need to be dealt with
contexts: You need to confront your fears.
She confronted him about his lies.
The problems confronting the government are huge.

words.definition: 1. (noun) an angry disagreement or fight between people or groups
contexts: There was a confrontation between police and fans.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the people who are at a religious service in a church
contexts: The priest spoke to the congregation.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) connected with the US Congress, the group of people who make laws in the US
contexts: He's running in the congressional elections.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to take control of a country or city by force
2. (verb) to succeed in dealing with a fear or problem
3. (verb) to become very successful or popular in a place
contexts: The Romans conquered much of Europe.
She finally conquered her fear of flying.
The band went on to conquer America.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the part of your mind that tells you whether what you are doing is right or wrong
2. (idiom) (have a guilty ~) to feel bad about something you have done
Note: Pronounced like KON-shuns.
contexts: My conscience told me to tell the truth.
I have a guilty conscience about not calling her.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the state of being awake and able to see, hear and think
2. (noun) the state of knowing that something exists or is important
contexts: He lost consciousness after the fall.
There is a growing consciousness of environmental problems.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) following one after another without a break
contexts: It rained for five consecutive days.

words.definition: 1. (noun) general agreement among a group of people
contexts: There is a consensus that the plan needs changing.

words.definition:
1. (noun) permission to do something, especially from someone in authority
2. (noun) agreement about something
3. (verb) to agree to something or give permission for it
Note: Formal.
contexts: You can't use the photo without her consent.
He was chosen as leader by common consent.
Her father consented to the marriage.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to use as little of something as possible so it lasts longer
2. (verb) to protect something from damage or change
contexts: Turn off the lights to conserve energy.
We must conserve our forests.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the quality of always behaving or doing something in the same way
2. (noun) how thick, smooth or firm a liquid or mixture is
contexts: The team lacks consistency.
Mix until the sauce has a smooth consistency.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to make your position or power stronger and more certain
2. (verb) to join things together into one
contexts: The team consolidated their lead with a second goal.
The two companies were consolidated into one.

words.definition:
1. (noun) an area of a country that elects a representative to parliament
2. (noun) the people who live in such an area and vote
Note: Mainly British.
contexts: He was elected MP for a constituency in London.
She has the support of her constituency.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to form or be part of a whole
2. (verb) to be considered as something
Note: Formal.
contexts: Women constitute 60% of the workforce.
This decision constitutes a big change.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the set of basic laws and principles that a country or organization is governed by
2. (noun) the general health and strength of a person's body
contexts: The US Constitution was written in 1787.
She has a strong constitution and is rarely ill.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) connected with or allowed by the set of basic laws of a country
contexts: Free speech is a constitutional right.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to limit what someone or something can do
Note: Formal.
contexts: Our research was constrained by a lack of money.

words.definition: 1. (noun) something that limits what you can do
contexts: Time constraints meant we couldn't visit everything.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a meeting with an expert, such as a doctor or lawyer, to get advice
2. (noun) the process of discussing something with people before making a decision
contexts: She had a consultation with a specialist.
The plan was made in consultation with local people.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the idea that buying more and more things is good for people and the economy
contexts: The film criticizes modern consumerism.

words.definition: 1. (verb) to make something dirty, harmful or poisonous by adding a dangerous substance
contexts: Chemicals from the factory contaminated the river.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) made dirty, harmful or poisonous by chemicals, bacteria or other substances
contexts: Don't drink contaminated water.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to think carefully about doing something
2. (verb) to think about something deeply for a long time
3. (verb) to look at something carefully for a long time
contexts: She's contemplating a career change.
He sat quietly, contemplating the meaning of life.
She stood contemplating the painting.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a strong feeling that someone or something does not deserve any respect
2. (noun) (~ of court) the crime of not obeying a court or judge
contexts: She looked at him with contempt.
He was jailed for contempt of court.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to say that something is true
2. (verb) to compete against others to win something
3. (verb) (~ with) to have to deal with a difficult problem
Note: Formal.
contexts: The lawyers contend that he is innocent.
Five teams are contending for the title.
Farmers have to contend with bad weather.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a person or team that has a good chance of winning a competition
contexts: She's a strong contender for the gold medal.

words.definition:
1. (noun) an opinion that someone states in an argument
2. (noun) disagreement between people
3. (idiom) (in ~) having a chance of winning
Note: Formal.
contexts: It is my contention that the plan will fail.
The new tax is a point of contention.
The team is still in contention for the title.

words.definition:
1. (adverb) again and again, often in an annoying way
2. (adverb) all the time, without stopping
contexts: She's continually complaining.
The software is continually updated.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a person or company that is paid to do work for another company, especially building work
contexts: We hired a contractor to build the new kitchen.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to say that what someone else has said is wrong and that the opposite is true
2. (verb) (of statements or facts) to be so different that they cannot both be true
contexts: Don't contradict your mother!
The two reports contradict each other.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a difference between two statements or facts that means they cannot both be true
2. (idiom) (a ~ in terms) a statement that has two parts that cannot both be true
contexts: There's a contradiction between what he says and what he does.
A friendly argument sounds like a contradiction in terms.

words.definition:
1. (idiom) (on the ~) used to say that the opposite of what was said is true
2. (adjective) completely different or opposite
3. (noun) (the ~) the opposite
4. (adjective) (of a person) deliberately doing the opposite of what people want
Note: In the last meaning, it is stressed on "tra".
contexts: “Was the film boring?” “On the contrary, it was great.”
Contrary to popular belief, bats are not blind.
I thought he'd fail, but he proved the contrary.
She's being contrary just to annoy me.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a person or thing that gives money, help or ideas to something
2. (noun) a person who writes articles for a newspaper or magazine
3. (noun) one of the causes of something
contexts: She's a big contributor to the charity.
He's a regular contributor to the magazine.
Smoking is a major contributor to heart disease.

words.definition:
1. (adverb) used to introduce an idea that is the opposite of what was just said
Note: Formal.
contexts: Some people like spicy food; conversely, others hate it.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the process of changing something from one form, use or system to another
2. (noun) a change from one religion or belief to another
3. (noun) (in rugby) extra points scored by kicking the ball after a try
contexts: The conversion of the barn into a house took a year.
His conversion to Islam surprised his family.
He scored the conversion.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to officially decide in a court that someone is guilty of a crime
2. (noun) a person who has been found guilty of a crime and sent to prison
Note: The verb is stressed on "vict"; the noun on "con".
contexts: He was convicted of murder.
Two convicts escaped from the prison.

words.definition:
1. (noun) an official decision in a court that someone is guilty of a crime
2. (noun) a strong belief or opinion
3. (noun) the feeling of being sure about something
contexts: He has two previous convictions for theft.
She has strong religious convictions.
He spoke with great conviction.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to work together with someone to achieve something
2. (verb) to be helpful by doing what someone asks
Note: British spelling also: co-operate.
contexts: The two countries cooperated on the project.
The suspect refused to cooperate with the police.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) willing to help or do what people ask
2. (adjective) done by people working together
3. (noun) a business or farm owned and run by the people who work in it
Note: British spelling also: co-operative.
contexts: The staff were very cooperative.
It was a cooperative effort.
The farmers formed a cooperative to sell their milk.

words.definition:

words.definition:
1. (noun) the machines and electronic parts of a computer, not the programs
2. (noun) tools and equipment used in the house and garden
3. (noun) the weapons and equipment used by an army
contexts: We need to upgrade our computer hardware.
He bought some nails at the hardware store.
They have the latest military hardware.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a state of peaceful agreement and friendship
2. (noun) a pleasant combination of different musical notes played or sung together
3. (noun) a pleasant combination of different parts
contexts: People of different religions live together in harmony.
They sang in perfect harmony.
The colours are in harmony with each other.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) cruel, severe or unkind
2. (adjective) (of conditions) very difficult to live in
3. (adjective) too strong or bright and unpleasant
contexts: The punishment was too harsh.
They survived a harsh winter.
The harsh light hurt my eyes.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the time when crops are cut and collected from the fields
2. (noun) the amount of crops collected
3. (verb) to cut and collect crops
contexts: Farmers are busy during the harvest.
We had a good harvest this year.
They harvest the grapes in September.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a very strong feeling of dislike
contexts: He has a deep hatred of injustice.

words.definition:
1. (verb) (of a ghost) to appear in a place again and again
2. (verb) (of a memory or problem) to make someone worried or upset for a long time
3. (noun) a place that someone visits often
contexts: People say the castle is haunted.
The memory of the accident still haunts him.
The café is a favourite haunt of artists.

words.definition:
1. (idiom) to dislike someone and try to cause problems for them
Note: Informal.
contexts: My boss really has it in for me.

words.definition: 1. (idiom) to be old and in bad condition
contexts: This old sofa has seen better days.

words.definition:
1. (noun) something that could be dangerous or cause harm
2. (verb) (~ a guess) to try to guess something
contexts: Smoking is a health hazard.
Could you hazard a guess at his age?

words.definition: 1. (adjective) dangerous, especially to people's health or safety
contexts: The factory produces hazardous waste.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) (of a meal) large and filling
2. (adjective) loud, cheerful and friendly
3. (adjective) (of feelings) strong and sincere
contexts: We had a hearty breakfast.
He gave a hearty laugh.
Hearty congratulations on your success!

words.definition: 1. (verb) to make a feeling or effect stronger, or to become stronger
contexts: The music heightened the tension in the film.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the history, traditions, buildings and culture of a country or group that are important to keep
contexts: The city is proud of its cultural heritage.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a system in which people or things are arranged in levels of importance
contexts: She's at the top of the company hierarchy.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) getting a lot of attention from the public and the media
contexts: It was a high-profile murder case.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to make it difficult for something to happen or for someone to make progress
Note: Formal.
contexts: The snow hindered the rescue.

words.definition:
1. (noun) something you say or do that suggests what you think, without saying it directly
2. (noun) a useful piece of advice
3. (noun) a very small amount of something
4. (verb) to suggest something without saying it directly
5. (idiom) (take the ~) to understand what someone is suggesting and do it
contexts: She gave me a hint about my birthday present.
Here are some helpful hints for saving money.
There was a hint of sadness in her voice.
He hinted that he might leave.
I yawned, but he didn't take the hint and go home.

words.definition: 1. (verb) to walk with difficulty because your legs or feet hurt
contexts: He hobbled to the door on crutches.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to wait before doing something
2. (phrasal verb) (of rain or bad weather) to not start
3. (phrasal verb) to stop an attacker or competitor from beating you
contexts: We'll hold off buying a car until next year.
I hope the rain holds off for the picnic.
She held off a strong challenge to win the race.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the country where you or your family were born
contexts: After the war, they returned to their homeland.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to jump on one foot
2. (verb) (of an animal or bird) to move by jumping
3. (verb) to get onto or off a vehicle quickly
4. (noun) a short jump
5. (noun) a short journey, especially by plane
Note: hop – hopped – hopped.
contexts: She hopped around the room.
A rabbit hopped across the field.
Hop in – I'll give you a lift.
The frog made a little hop.
It's a short hop from London to Paris.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) believing that something you want will happen
2. (adjective) making you believe that something good will happen
3. (noun) a person who wants to be successful, especially in a competition
contexts: I'm hopeful that we'll win.
There are hopeful signs of improvement.
Hundreds of young hopefuls came to the audition.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the line far away where the land or sea seems to meet the sky
2. (noun) (~s) the limit of your knowledge, experience or interests
3. (idiom) (on the ~) likely to happen soon
contexts: The sun disappeared below the horizon.
Travel broadens your horizons.
There are changes on the horizon.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a person who is kept as a prisoner by someone until they get what they want
contexts: The gunmen took ten hostages.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) unfriendly and aggressive
2. (adjective) (~ to) strongly against something
3. (adjective) connected with an enemy
4. (adjective) (of conditions) difficult to live in
contexts: The crowd was very hostile.
They are hostile to the idea of change.
The plane flew into hostile territory.
The desert is a hostile environment.

words.definition:
1. (noun) unfriendly or aggressive behaviour or feelings towards someone
2. (noun) strong opposition to an idea or plan
3. (noun) (~ies) fighting in a war
contexts: There was a lot of hostility between the two groups.
The plan met with hostility from local people.
Hostilities ended in 1945.

words.definition:
1. (noun) all people as a group
2. (noun) kindness and sympathy towards others
3. (noun) the state of being human
4. (noun) (the ~ies) subjects such as history, languages and literature
contexts: The war was a crime against humanity.
The nurses treated everyone with great humanity.
The film makes us think about our shared humanity.
She studied the humanities at university.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) not proud, and not thinking that you are better than others
2. (adjective) of low social rank or position
3. (adjective) simple and not expensive or important
4. (verb) to make someone realize that they are not as important or good as they thought
contexts: Despite his success, he remained humble.
She comes from a humble background.
They live in a humble little house.
The champions were humbled by a small team.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a gas that has no colour or smell, is lighter than air and burns easily
contexts: Water is made of hydrogen and oxygen.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) based on a situation that is imagined and not real
contexts: Let me ask you a hypothetical question.

words.definition:
1. (noun) an official document, such as a passport, that shows who you are
2. (noun) the process of finding out who or what someone or something is
3. (noun) a feeling of sharing someone's experiences or feelings
Note: Short form: ID.
contexts: Please bring some identification with you.
The identification of the victims took days.
Readers feel a strong identification with the main character.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) based on a particular set of political or social beliefs
contexts: The two parties have deep ideological differences.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a set of political, social or religious beliefs that a group of people has
contexts: The party has a left-wing ideology.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a very stupid person
Note: Informal and rude.
contexts: I felt like an idiot when I fell over.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to admire or love someone so much that you think they are perfect
Note: British spelling also: idolise.
contexts: He idolizes his older brother.

words.definition: 1. (noun) lack of knowledge or information about something
contexts: His ignorance of the law is no excuse.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) rude and not polite
Note: Formal.
contexts: He's an ill-mannered young man.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the act of entering or living in a country without official permission
contexts: The government is trying to reduce illegal immigration.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the state of not being able to read or write
contexts: Illiteracy is still a big problem in some countries.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the use of words to create pictures in the reader's mind
2. (noun) pictures or photos
contexts: The poem is full of beautiful imagery.
The satellite imagery shows the damage clearly.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) extremely large or great
contexts: The project needs an immense amount of work.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) going to happen very soon
contexts: The storm is imminent.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the process of making a plan, decision or system start to work
contexts: The implementation of the new rules will take time.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) suggested but not said directly
2. (adjective) (of trust or belief) complete, without any doubt
contexts: There was an implicit threat in his words.
She had implicit trust in her doctor.

words.definition: 1. (verb) to put someone in prison or keep them in a place they cannot leave
contexts: He was imprisoned for five years.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the state of being kept in prison
contexts: She was sentenced to life imprisonment.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a sudden strong wish to do something without thinking about it first
2. (noun) a short signal of electricity sent along a wire or nerve
contexts: I bought the dress on impulse.
The brain sends nerve impulses to the muscles.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) doing things suddenly without thinking carefully about the results
contexts: He's very impulsive and often regrets his decisions.

words.definition:
1. (idiom) following or obeying a rule, law or someone's wishes
Note: Formal.
contexts: The money was given in accordance with her will.

words.definition:
1. (idiom) more than a particular number or amount
Note: Formal.
contexts: The car can reach speeds in excess of 200 km/h.

words.word: in the blink of an eye
words.definition: 1. (idiom) so quickly that you almost do not notice it
contexts: It was all over in the blink of an eye.

words.definition: 1. (idiom) over a long period of time in the future
contexts: Buying a good car will save you money in the long run.

words.definition:
1. (idiom) in a place that is far from any town or other people
Note: Informal.
contexts: Our car broke down in the middle of nowhere.

words.definition: 1. (idiom) at the last possible moment, just before it is too late
contexts: The ambulance arrived in the nick of time.

words.definition: 1. (idiom) about, or close to a particular number or amount
contexts: The house cost in the region of $300,000.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the fact of not being able to do something
contexts: His inability to speak French was a problem in Paris.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) not good enough, or not enough in amount
2. (adjective) (of a person) not confident or not able to deal with a situation
contexts: The hospital has inadequate equipment.
She made me feel inadequate.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) not suitable or right for a particular situation
contexts: His comments were completely inappropriate.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) not paying attention
contexts: The student was inattentive in class.

words.definition:
1. (noun) how often something happens, especially something bad
Note: Formal.
contexts: There is a high incidence of heart disease in the area.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) (~ to) wanting to do something
2. (adjective) (~ to) likely to do something or behave in a particular way
3. (adjective) having a natural ability for something
contexts: I'm inclined to agree with you.
He's inclined to get angry easily.
She's very musically inclined.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the act of making someone or something part of a group, list or team
2. (noun) the practice of making sure that all people, including those with disabilities, can take part
contexts: She was surprised by her inclusion in the team.
The school is committed to inclusion.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) changing too often, so that it is not reliable
2. (adjective) (~ with) not matching other facts or ideas
contexts: The team's performance has been inconsistent.
His story is inconsistent with the evidence.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to experience something bad, such as a cost or punishment, because of something you have done
Note: incur – incurred – incurred. Formal.
contexts: You will incur a fine if you return the book late.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a sign that shows what something is like or how it is changing
2. (noun) a flashing light on a car that shows which way it is going to turn
3. (noun) a needle or light on a machine that shows a level or amount
Note: The car meaning is British. In American English: turn signal.
contexts: Unemployment is an important indicator of the economy.
He forgot to use his indicator.
The fuel indicator shows the tank is low.

words.definition:
1. (noun) an official statement saying that someone is accused of a serious crime
2. (noun) (an ~ of) a sign that something is very bad and should be criticized
Note: The "c" is not pronounced.
contexts: He faces an indictment for fraud.
The report is an indictment of the school system.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) (of people, plants or animals) belonging to a place and living there from the earliest times
Note: Formal.
contexts: The indigenous people of Australia have a rich culture.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) so important or useful that you cannot do without it
contexts: A good dictionary is indispensable for language learners.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to cause something to happen
2. (verb) to persuade someone to do something
3. (verb) to make a pregnant woman start giving birth by giving her a drug
Note: Formal.
contexts: Some drugs can induce sleep.
Nothing would induce me to go back there.
The doctors decided to induce labour.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to allow yourself to have or do something enjoyable
2. (verb) to let someone have or do whatever they want
contexts: I indulged myself with a box of chocolates.
They indulge their children too much.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the process of developing many factories and businesses in a country or region
Note: British spelling also: industrialisation.
contexts: The 19th century saw rapid industrialization in Europe.

words.definition: 1. (noun) an unfair situation in which some people have more money, rights or chances than others
contexts: There is growing inequality between the rich and the poor.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) famous for something bad
Note: Stressed on "in".
contexts: He was an infamous criminal.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a baby or very young child
2. (adjective) for babies or very young children
Note: Formal.
contexts: The mother held her infant in her arms.
The shop sells infant clothing.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to give someone a disease
2. (verb) (of bacteria) to get into a cut or part of the body and make it ill
3. (verb) (of a virus) to damage a computer
4. (verb) to make other people have the same feeling
contexts: The virus has infected thousands of people.
The wound became infected.
A virus infected my laptop.
Her laughter infected everyone.

words.definition: 1. (verb) to make someone suffer something unpleasant, such as pain or damage
contexts: The storm inflicted serious damage on the town.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) having a lot of power to change what people think or do
contexts: She is one of the most influential women in the world.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to live in a place
Note: Formal.
contexts: The island is inhabited by about 500 people.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) existing as a natural and basic part of something
Note: Formal.
contexts: There are risks inherent in any business.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to stop something from happening or make it slower
2. (verb) to make someone too nervous or embarrassed to do something
Note: Formal.
contexts: The drug inhibits the growth of cancer cells.
Shyness inhibited her from speaking.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to make something begin
2. (verb) to make someone a member of a group, often with a special ceremony
3. (verb) (~ into) to teach someone about something for the first time
Note: Formal.
contexts: The government initiated a new health programme.
New members are initiated at a secret ceremony.
He initiated me into the world of jazz.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to put a drug or medicine into someone's body using a needle
2. (verb) to add a quality to something
3. (verb) to put money into a business or plan
contexts: The nurse injected the drug into my arm.
She injected some humour into the speech.
The government injected $1 billion into the economy.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the act of putting a drug into someone's body using a needle
2. (noun) a large amount of money put into a business or plan
contexts: The doctor gave me an injection.
The company needs a cash injection.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a situation in which people are treated unfairly
contexts: They fought against injustice.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a person who is kept in a prison or a hospital for mental illness
contexts: The prison has 500 inmates.

words.definition: 1. (verb) to introduce new ideas, methods or products
contexts: Companies must innovate to survive.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to ask someone for information
2. (phrasal verb) (~ into) to officially try to find out the facts about something
Note: Formal. British English also: enquire.
contexts: I'm calling to inquire about the job.
The police are inquiring into his death.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the act of putting something into something else
2. (noun) something added to a piece of writing
contexts: The insertion of the needle didn't hurt.
The editor made several insertions.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a person who is part of a group or organization and so has special knowledge about it
contexts: According to an insider, the company is in trouble.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to look at something carefully to check it
2. (verb) to officially visit a place to check that rules are being obeyed
contexts: He inspected the car for damage.
Restaurants are inspected regularly.

words.definition:
1. (noun) an official visit to check that something is correct or that rules are being obeyed
2. (noun) the act of looking at something carefully
contexts: The school has an inspection next week.
On closer inspection, the painting was a fake.

words.definition:
1. (noun) something that gives you new ideas or the wish to do something
2. (noun) a person or thing that makes you want to do better
3. (noun) a sudden good idea
contexts: The trip gave me the inspiration for my book.
She's an inspiration to us all.
I had an inspiration!

words.definition:
1. (noun) a natural way of behaving that you do not need to learn
2. (noun) a feeling that makes you do something without thinking
contexts: Birds build nests by instinct.
My instinct told me not to trust him.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) connected with large organizations such as banks, schools or hospitals
2. (adjective) existing as part of the system of an organization or society
contexts: Institutional investors own most of the shares.
There is institutional racism in the police.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to tell someone officially to do something
2. (verb) to teach someone how to do something
Note: Formal.
contexts: The police instructed people to stay indoors.
She instructs students in first aid.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) (~ in) very important in making something happen
2. (adjective) (of music) played on musical instruments, without singing
contexts: She was instrumental in getting the law changed.
The album has three instrumental tracks.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) not enough for a particular purpose
Note: Formal.
contexts: There is insufficient evidence to arrest him.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to cover something with a material that stops heat, cold, sound or electricity from passing through
2. (verb) to protect someone from unpleasant experiences
contexts: We insulated the roof to save energy.
Their money insulated them from the crisis.

words.definition: 1. (noun) material that stops heat, cold, sound or electricity from passing through
contexts: Good insulation keeps the house warm.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to say or do something rude that upsets someone
2. (noun) a rude remark or action that upsets someone
3. (idiom) (add ~ to injury) to make a bad situation even worse for someone
Note: The verb is stressed on "sult"; the noun on "in".
contexts: He insulted my mother.
The fans shouted insults at the referee.
To add insult to injury, it started to rain.

words.definition: 1. (noun) an attempt by a group of people with weapons to take control of a country by fighting the government
contexts: The army is fighting an insurgency in the north.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) not damaged or broken, and complete
contexts: The old church is still intact.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the amount of food, drink or other substance that you take into your body
2. (noun) the number of people who start at a school, college or job at a particular time
3. (idiom) (an ~ of breath) a sudden breath in, often because you are surprised
contexts: Try to reduce your salt intake.
The school has an intake of 200 students a year.
There was a sharp intake of breath.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) necessary and important as a part of a whole
contexts: Music is an integral part of the school day.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) with different parts joined together in a way that works well
2. (adjective) including people of different races, religions or groups
contexts: We need an integrated transport system.
It's a racially integrated school.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the process of joining different things together so they work as a whole
2. (noun) the process of people from different groups becoming part of a society
contexts: The integration of the two systems took a year.
The government supports the integration of immigrants.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the quality of being honest and having strong moral principles
2. (noun) the state of being whole and not damaged
Note: Formal.
contexts: She's a woman of great integrity.
The earthquake damaged the integrity of the building.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to become stronger or more extreme, or to make something do this
Note: intensify – intensified – intensified.
contexts: The storm intensified overnight.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the quality of being very strong or extreme
2. (noun) the strength of something that can be measured, such as light or sound
contexts: The intensity of the heat made us stay inside.
The light changes in intensity during the day.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) involving a lot of work or activity in a short time
2. (adjective) (~ care) special treatment in a hospital for people who are very ill
3. (adjective) (of farming) producing as much as possible from the land
contexts: She did an intensive English course.
He's in intensive care after the accident.
Intensive farming can harm the environment.

words.definition:
1. (noun) what you plan or want to do
2. (adjective) (~ on) determined to do something
3. (adjective) giving all your attention to something
4. (idiom) (to all ~s and purposes) in every way that is important
Note: Formal.
contexts: He was charged with intent to kill.
She was intent on winning.
He had an intent look on his face.
To all intents and purposes, the war was over.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) (of a computer program or device) reacting to the things the user does
2. (adjective) involving people talking and working together
contexts: The museum has interactive displays.
The lessons are very interactive.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the way a computer program shows information and lets the user give instructions
2. (noun) a point where two systems, subjects or groups meet and affect each other
contexts: The app has a simple user interface.
She works at the interface between science and art.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to get involved in a situation when you are not wanted
2. (phrasal verb) (~ with) to stop something from happening or working in the normal way
contexts: Please don't interfere in my life.
Noise interferes with my sleep.

words.definition:
1. (noun) involvement in a situation when you are not wanted
2. (noun) noise or other problems that spoil a radio or TV signal
contexts: I don't want any interference from my parents.
There was a lot of interference on the line.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) used for a short time until something permanent is found
2. (idiom) (in the ~) in the time between two events
Note: Formal.
contexts: He was named interim manager.
The new office opens in June; in the interim, we'll work from home.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the inside part of something
2. (adjective) inside, or connected with the inside of something
3. (noun) the central part of a country, far from the coast
4. (noun) (~ design) the art of decorating the inside of a building
contexts: The interior of the car was very clean.
We painted the interior walls.
They explored the interior of Africa.
She studied interior design.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) between beginner and advanced level
2. (adjective) between two other stages or things
contexts: She's in an intermediate English class.
There's an intermediate step in the process.

words.definition: 1. (verb) to ask someone a lot of questions for a long time, often in an aggressive way
contexts: The police interrogated him for hours.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to become involved in a situation in order to change it or stop it
2. (verb) to happen between two times or events
contexts: The police had to intervene to stop the fight.
Ten years intervened before we met again.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the act of becoming involved in a situation in order to change it or stop it
contexts: Military intervention may be needed.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) very close and personal
2. (adjective) (of a place) small, quiet and pleasant
3. (adjective) private and personal
4. (adjective) having a sexual relationship
5. (adjective) (of knowledge) very detailed
contexts: They're intimate friends.
It's an intimate little restaurant.
She told me intimate details about her life.
They were intimate for a short time.
He has an intimate knowledge of the city.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to frighten or threaten someone, so that they do what you want
2. (verb) to make someone feel nervous and less confident
contexts: The gang tried to intimidate the witnesses.
Don't be intimidated by the size of the task.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) very interesting because it is unusual or mysterious
contexts: It's an intriguing idea.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) belonging to the basic nature of something
Note: Formal.
contexts: The painting has little intrinsic value.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) based on feelings rather than facts or reasons
2. (adjective) (of a person) able to understand things quickly by feeling
3. (adjective) (of a computer program or device) easy to use without instructions
contexts: She had an intuitive sense that he was lying.
He's a very intuitive teacher.
The app is very intuitive.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) extremely useful
Note: It does not mean "not valuable".
contexts: Your help has been invaluable.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a person whose job is to find out the facts about a crime, accident or problem
contexts: Investigators are looking for the cause of the crash.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) impossible to see
2. (adjective) not noticed or not given attention
contexts: Germs are invisible to the human eye.
Old people often feel invisible.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to use a law or rule to support your actions
2. (verb) to mention a person, idea or principle to support an argument
3. (verb) to make someone have a feeling or memory
Note: Formal.
contexts: The government invoked emergency powers.
He invoked the name of Gandhi in his speech.
The smell invoked memories of my childhood.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the act of taking part in something
2. (noun) a romantic or emotional relationship
contexts: His involvement in the crime was never proved.
She had a brief involvement with a married man.

words.definition: 1. (phrasal verb) to solve small problems or difficulties
contexts: We still need to iron out a few details.

words.definition:

words.definition: 1. (adjective) not based on reason or clear thinking

words.definition: 1. (idiom) to stop someone or something unpleasant from coming too close or causing problems

words.definition:

words.definition:

words.definition:

words.definition:

words.definition: 1. (noun) a device that produces a very strong, narrow beam of light, used for cutting, medical operations and reading information

words.definition:

words.definition:

words.definition:

words.definition:

words.definition:

words.definition:

words.definition:

words.definition:

words.definition:
