words.definition:
1. (adjective) using strong or violent methods to achieve political or social change
2. (noun) a person who uses strong or violent methods to achieve political or social change
contexts: Militant groups attacked the town.
The police arrested several militants.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a group of ordinary people who are trained as soldiers but are not part of a regular army
contexts: Local militias are fighting in the north.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a building with a machine for making grain into flour
2. (noun) a factory that makes paper, cloth or steel
3. (noun) a small machine for crushing coffee or pepper
4. (phrasal verb) (~ around/about) to move around in a crowd without going anywhere
contexts: The old mill is now a museum.
He worked in a cotton mill.
Pass me the pepper mill.
People were milling around outside the cinema.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) very small in amount or degree
contexts: The damage was minimal.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to reduce something bad to the smallest possible amount
2. (verb) to make something seem less important than it really is
3. (verb) to make a window on a computer screen very small
Note: British spelling also: minimise.
contexts: We must minimize the risks.
She minimized her part in the success.
Minimize all the windows.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the process or industry of digging coal, gold and other substances out of the ground
contexts: The town grew because of coal mining.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a government department that is responsible for a particular area
2. (noun) the work of a religious leader
contexts: She works for the Ministry of Health.
He spent 30 years in the ministry.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a very surprising and lucky event that seems impossible
2. (noun) an act that seems impossible and is believed to be done by God
3. (adjective) very effective or helpful in a way that is surprising
contexts: It's a miracle that nobody was hurt.
The Bible tells of Jesus's miracles.
It's a miracle cure.

words.definition:
1. (noun) great unhappiness or suffering
2. (noun) a situation that causes great unhappiness
3. (idiom) (put someone out of their ~) to stop someone worrying by telling them something they want to know
contexts: The war brought misery to millions.
Life was a misery after the accident.
Put me out of my misery – did I pass?

words.definition: 1. (adjective) giving the wrong idea or making you believe something that is not true
contexts: The advert is very misleading.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a weapon that flies through the air and explodes when it hits something
2. (noun) an object that is thrown at someone
contexts: They launched a missile attack.
Fans threw missiles onto the pitch.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to make something bad less serious or harmful
Note: Formal.
contexts: Trees help to mitigate the effects of pollution.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a large crowd of people who are angry and may become violent
2. (noun) (the ~) a group of criminals who are organized
3. (verb) (of a crowd) to gather around someone in an excited or angry way
contexts: An angry mob attacked the police station.
He worked for the mob.
The singer was mobbed by fans.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the ability to move easily from one place to another
2. (noun) the ability to change jobs, social class or where you live
contexts: The disease affects her mobility.
Education increases social mobility.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to organize a group of people to support something or take action
2. (verb) to prepare an army for war
Note: British spelling also: mobilise.
contexts: They mobilized thousands of volunteers.
The country mobilized its army.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) not too much and not too little, average in size or amount
2. (adjective) having political or religious opinions that are not extreme
3. (verb) to make something less extreme or strong
4. (verb) to control a discussion so that it is fair
Note: The adjective ends like "it"; the verb ends like "late".
contexts: Cook over a moderate heat.
He's a moderate politician.
He moderated his language.
She moderated the debate.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a small change made to something to improve it
contexts: We made a few modifications to the design.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the force that keeps an object moving after it has started
2. (noun) the ability to keep growing or developing
contexts: The car gained momentum as it went down the hill.
The campaign is gaining momentum.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a member of a group of religious men who live together apart from other people
contexts: The monks pray five times a day.

words.definition:
1. (noun) complete control of a business or industry by one company, so that others cannot compete
2. (noun) complete control or possession of something that others cannot share
contexts: The company has a monopoly on train travel.
Men don't have a monopoly on power.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the amount of confidence and enthusiasm that a person or group feels at a particular time
Note: Stressed on "rale".
contexts: Morale in the team is very low after the defeat.

words.definition:
1. (noun) principles about what is right and wrong behaviour
2. (noun) the degree to which something is right or wrong
contexts: Religion has a strong influence on morality.
People question the morality of testing on animals.

words.definition: 1. (idiom) almost, nearly, or approximately
contexts: The work is more or less finished.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the number of deaths in a particular group or period
2. (noun) the fact that all people must die
contexts: Infant mortality has fallen.
His illness made him think about his own mortality.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) extremely embarrassed or ashamed
contexts: I was mortified when I realized my mistake.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a reason for doing something, especially something bad
contexts: The police don't know the motive for the murder.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a person who drives a car
contexts: Motorists are warned to drive carefully in the fog.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to feel and show great sadness because someone has died
2. (verb) to feel sad because something has ended or been lost
contexts: The whole nation mourned her death.
They mourned the loss of the old school.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) ordinary, boring and not interesting
contexts: She hates mundane jobs like cleaning.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) connected with the government of a town or city
contexts: The municipal library is open on Sundays.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) felt or done by two or more people towards each other
2. (adjective) shared by two or more people
contexts: They have mutual respect for each other.
We met through a mutual friend.

words.definition: 1. (adverb) used to give more exact details about something you have just said
contexts: Two people were absent, namely Tom and Sarah.

words.definition: 1. (phrasal verb) to reduce the number of possibilities or choices
contexts: We've narrowed down the list to three candidates.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) happening or existing in all parts of a country
2. (adverb) in all parts of a country
contexts: There was a nationwide strike.
The shop has 50 branches nationwide.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the feeling that you are going to be sick
contexts: The medicine can cause nausea.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) connected with a country's navy or ships used in war
contexts: There's a big naval base on the island.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to not give enough care or attention to someone or something
2. (verb) (~ to) to forget or fail to do something
3. (noun) the state of not being looked after
contexts: He neglected his children.
She neglected to tell me about the meeting.
The house was in a state of neglect.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) next to or near a place
Note: British spelling: neighbouring.
contexts: They moved to a neighboring town.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a structure that a bird makes to lay its eggs in
2. (noun) a home that some insects or animals make
3. (verb) (of a bird) to build a structure for its eggs
4. (idiom) (fly the ~) to leave your parents' home to live on your own
5. (idiom) (~ egg) money that you save for the future
contexts: There's a bird's nest in the tree.
We found a wasps' nest in the roof.
Swallows nest under the roof.
Their youngest son has just flown the nest.
They have a nice nest egg for their retirement.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a short report with news that is sent regularly to members of a group or organization
contexts: Sign up for our monthly newsletter.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to eat something by taking very small bites
2. (noun) a small bite of something
3. (noun) (~s) small snacks
Note: "Nibbles" is informal and British.
contexts: She nibbled a biscuit.
He took a nibble of the cheese.
We'll have some nibbles before dinner.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a job or activity that is perfect for someone
2. (noun) a small part of a market with special needs
3. (adjective) interesting to only a small number of people
4. (noun) a small hollow space in a wall
contexts: She found her niche in teaching.
The company sells to a small niche of customers.
They sell niche products.
There's a statue in a niche.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) morally good and generous
2. (adjective) belonging to a family of high social rank
3. (adjective) impressive in size or quality
4. (noun) a person from a family of high social rank
contexts: Helping the poor is a noble cause.
She comes from a noble family.
It's a noble building.
The king called the nobles together.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to move your head up and down to show that you agree or understand
2. (verb) to move your head down once to say hello or show something
3. (noun) a movement of the head up and down
Note: nod – nodded – nodded.
contexts: She nodded in agreement.
He nodded towards the door.
He gave me a nod.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to fall asleep by accident, especially when you are sitting
Note: Informal.
contexts: Grandpa nodded off in front of the TV.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to officially suggest someone for a job, position or prize
2. (verb) to officially choose someone for a job
contexts: She was nominated for an Oscar.
He was nominated as the new chairman.

words.definition: 1. (noun) an official suggestion that someone should get a job, position or prize
contexts: The film received five nominations.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a person who has been officially suggested for a job, position or prize
contexts: The nominees for best actor are announced today.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) (of an organization) not trying to make money, but using any money it makes to help others
2. (noun) an organization that is not trying to make money
Note: Also written: nonprofit.
contexts: She works for a non-profit organization.
He started a non-profit to help homeless people.

words.definition:
1. (adverb) even so, despite what has just been said
Note: Formal.
contexts: The test was hard; nonetheless, everyone passed.

words.definition:
1. (noun) ideas or statements that are silly or not true
2. (noun) silly or unacceptable behaviour
3. (noun) words that have no meaning
contexts: That's complete nonsense!
Stop this nonsense at once!
The poem is full of nonsense words.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a happy but slightly sad feeling when you think about good times in the past
contexts: She felt a wave of nostalgia for her childhood.

words.definition: 1. (idiom) used to add another point that makes what you are saying stronger
contexts: The hotel was dirty, not to mention expensive.

words.word: not to put too fine a point on it
words.definition: 1. (idiom) used to show that you are going to say something very directly
contexts: Not to put too fine a point on it, your work is bad.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) important or interesting enough to be noticed
2. (noun) an important or famous person
contexts: The town is notable for its old buildings.
Several local notables attended.

words.definition:
1. (adverb) especially, used to give an important example
2. (adverb) in a way that is easy to notice
contexts: Several people, notably the president, were absent.
She was notably absent.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to officially tell someone about something
Note: notify – notified – notified. Formal.
contexts: Please notify us of any change of address.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) well known for something bad
contexts: The road is notorious for accidents.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the quality of being new, different and interesting
2. (noun) something new and unusual
3. (noun) a cheap small toy or decoration
contexts: The novelty of living in a big city soon wore off.
Cars were still a novelty in 1900.
The shop sells party novelties.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to look after and help someone or something grow and develop
2. (noun) the care and help given to a child as it grows
Note: Formal.
contexts: She nurtured her children with love.
Is intelligence a matter of nature or nurture?

words.definition:
1. (noun) a statement that shows you disagree with or do not like something
2. (noun) a reason for not liking or agreeing with something
contexts: Does anyone have any objections to the plan?
My only objection is the cost.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to force someone to do something, by law or because it is a duty
2. (verb) to help someone by doing what they ask
3. (idiom) (be ~d to) to be grateful to someone
Note: Formal.
contexts: Drivers are obliged to wear seat belts.
I asked for help, and he was happy to oblige.
I'm much obliged to you for your help.

words.definition: 1. (verb) to think about something or someone all the time, in a way that is not normal
contexts: She obsesses about her weight.

words.definition:
1. (noun) something or someone that you think about all the time, in a way that is not normal
2. (noun) the state of thinking about something all the time
contexts: Football is his obsession.
Her obsession with cleanliness is getting worse.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) no longer used because something newer and better exists
contexts: Typewriters are now obsolete.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) happening sometimes, but not often or regularly
contexts: I have the occasional glass of wine.

words.definition:
1. (noun) something that happens
2. (noun) the fact of something happening
Note: Formal.
contexts: Power cuts are a common occurrence here.
The occurrence of the disease is rising.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the chance that something will happen
2. (noun) (in betting) the numbers that show how likely something is and how much money you will win
3. (idiom) (against all ~) although it seemed impossible
4. (idiom) (at ~ with) disagreeing with someone or something
contexts: The odds are that he'll be late again.
The odds on that horse are ten to one.
Against all odds, they won the game.
He is at odds with his boss.

words.definition:
1. (noun) something that is given, especially as a gift or to God
2. (noun) something that is made available to buy or watch, such as a new product or film
contexts: They left offerings of fruit at the temple.
The band's latest offering is their best album yet.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to balance one effect with an opposite one, so that there is no change
Note: offset – offset – offset.
contexts: The rise in prices was offset by higher wages.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a person's children, or an animal's young
Note: Plural: offspring. Formal.
contexts: Parents want the best for their offspring.

words.definition: 1. (preposition) for someone, as their representative or instead of them
contexts: I'm writing on behalf of my mother.

words.definition: 1. (idiom) nervous and not able to relax
contexts: She's been on edge since the phone call.

words.definition:
1. (preposition) about, roughly (used with numbers)
Note: Formal, mainly American. British English: of the order of.
contexts: The project will cost on the order of $5 million.

words.definition:
1. (idiom) immediately, without any delay
2. (idiom) at the exact place where something is happening
3. (idiom) (put someone ~) to ask someone a difficult question that they must answer immediately
contexts: He was offered the job on the spot.
Police were on the spot within minutes.
The interviewer really put me on the spot.

words.definition:
1. (idiom) very rarely
Note: Informal.
contexts: My brother visits once in a blue moon.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the beginning of something, especially something unpleasant
contexts: The onset of the disease is often sudden.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) working and ready for use
2. (adjective) connected with the way an organization or system works
contexts: The new airport will be operational next year.
We had some operational problems.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to treat a group of people cruelly and unfairly, especially by limiting their freedom
2. (verb) to make someone feel worried and unhappy
contexts: The government oppressed minorities for years.
The heat oppressed him.

words.definition: 1. (verb) (~ for/to) to make a choice
contexts: Many students opt to study abroad.

words.definition: 1. (phrasal verb) to choose not to take part in something
contexts: You can opt out of the pension scheme.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) connected with sight or light
2. (adjective) connected with lenses and glasses
contexts: It's an optical illusion.
She works in an optical shop.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) the best or most effective possible
Note: Formal. Also: optimum.
contexts: The optimal temperature for the plants is 25 degrees.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the feeling that good things will happen and that the future will be good
contexts: There is growing optimism about the economy.

words.definition: 1. (idiom) used after a number or amount to show that it is not exact
contexts: It takes an hour or so.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) spoken, not written
2. (adjective) connected with the mouth
3. (noun) a spoken exam, especially in a foreign language
contexts: We have an oral exam tomorrow.
Brush your teeth for good oral health.
I passed my French oral.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) connected with the way a company or group is arranged and managed
2. (adjective) connected with the ability to plan and arrange things
Note: British spelling also: organisational.
contexts: The company made some organizational changes.
She has excellent organizational skills.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the direction that something faces
2. (noun) training and information for people who are new to a school, job or place
3. (noun) a person's beliefs, interests or the kind of people they are attracted to
contexts: The orientation of the house means it gets lots of sun.
New students attend an orientation week.
People should not be judged on their sexual orientation.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to begin or come from a particular place or situation
Note: Formal.
contexts: The tradition originated in China.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) generally accepted and traditional
2. (adjective) following the traditional beliefs of a religion very closely
3. (adjective) (with a capital O) connected with the Christian Church in Eastern Europe and Greece
contexts: The doctor used orthodox medicine.
They are orthodox Jews.
She belongs to the Greek Orthodox Church.

words.definition:
1. (idiom) no longer secret, and known by everyone
2. (idiom) outside, in a place that can be easily seen
contexts: Now the truth is out in the open.
They camped out in the open.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) not suitable for a particular situation, or not belonging there
2. (adjective) not in the usual or correct position
contexts: I felt out of place at the party.
Nothing in the room was out of place.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the sudden start of something bad, such as a disease or war
contexts: There's been an outbreak of flu.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a short trip for pleasure, often with a group
2. (noun) the act of telling people that someone is gay when they want it to be secret
contexts: We went on a family outing to the zoo.
The outing of the politician caused a scandal.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a shop that sells a company's goods cheaply
2. (noun) a place in a wall where you connect electrical equipment
3. (noun) a way of expressing or getting rid of strong feelings or energy
4. (noun) a shop or business that sells a particular product
5. (noun) an organization that publishes news, such as a newspaper or website
Note: The meaning of a place in a wall is American. In British English: socket.
contexts: We bought shoes at the factory outlet.
Plug the lamp into the outlet.
Sport is a good outlet for stress.
The company has 200 retail outlets.
The story was reported by several news outlets.

words.definition:
1. (noun) your general way of thinking about life or the world
2. (noun) what is likely to happen in the future
3. (noun) the weather expected for the next few days
contexts: She has a positive outlook on life.
The economic outlook is good.
The outlook for the weekend is sunny.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a strong feeling of anger and shock
2. (noun) an act or event that is very wrong and shocking
3. (verb) to make someone very angry and shocked
contexts: The decision caused public outrage.
The attack was an outrage.
The news outraged the public.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) very shocking and unacceptable
2. (adjective) very unusual and slightly shocking, often in a funny way
contexts: The prices in this restaurant are outrageous.
She wears outrageous clothes.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a person who does not belong to a particular group or place
2. (noun) a person or team that is not expected to win
contexts: I always felt like an outsider at school.
The horse was a complete outsider.

words.definition:
1. (idiom) extremely happy and pleased
Note: Informal, mainly British.
contexts: She was over the moon about her new job.

words.definition: 1. (idiom) to work too hard or do too much of something, so that it harms you
contexts: Don't overdo it – you've only just recovered.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to change a system completely to make it better
2. (verb) to look at every part of a machine and repair it
3. (noun) a complete change or repair of something
contexts: The government plans to overhaul the tax system.
The engine needs to be overhauled.
The health service needs an overhaul.

words.definition:
1. (verb) (of two things) to cover part of the same area, subject or time
2. (noun) a part that two things share
Note: overlap – overlapped – overlapped.
contexts: Our holidays overlap by a week.
There's some overlap between the two jobs.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to not notice something
2. (verb) to forgive or not punish something wrong
3. (verb) (of a building or room) to have a view of a place from above
contexts: It's easy to overlook small mistakes.
I'll overlook your mistake this time.
The hotel overlooks the sea.

words.definition: 1. (adverb) too, or more than is good
contexts: I'm not overly worried.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the situation of having too many people living in an area
contexts: Overpopulation puts pressure on resources.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to watch and manage work or people to make sure it is done correctly
Note: oversee – oversaw – overseen.
contexts: She oversees the whole project.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to turn over, or to make something turn over, so that the top is at the bottom
2. (verb) to change a legal decision officially
contexts: The car hit a wall and overturned.
The court overturned his conviction.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to make someone feel a very strong emotion that they cannot control
2. (verb) to give someone too much work or too many problems
3. (verb) to defeat someone completely
contexts: She was overwhelmed by grief.
The hospitals are overwhelmed with patients.
The army overwhelmed the enemy.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) very great or strong, so that it is difficult to deal with
2. (adjective) (of an amount) very large
contexts: I had an overwhelming desire to cry.
The overwhelming majority voted yes.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a formal agreement between people, groups or countries
contexts: The two countries signed a peace pact.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a number of pieces of paper fixed together at one edge
2. (noun) a thick piece of soft material used to protect something or make it more comfortable
3. (noun) the soft part under the foot of a cat or dog
4. (noun) a flat area where helicopters land or rockets are launched
5. (noun) a person's flat or house
6. (verb) to walk quietly with soft steps
7. (phrasal verb) (~ out) to make a speech or piece of writing longer by adding things that are not necessary
Note: The meaning "flat or house" is old-fashioned and informal.
contexts: She wrote the number on a pad of paper.
Football players wear shin pads.
The dog cut its paw pad.
The helicopter landed on the pad.
Come back to my pad.
She padded across the room in her slippers.
He padded out his essay.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to walk in shallow water without shoes
2. (verb) to move a small boat through water using a short pole with a flat end
3. (noun) a short pole with a flat end, used to move a small boat through water
Note: The meaning "walk in shallow water" is British. In American English: wade.
contexts: The children paddled in the sea.
We paddled the canoe down the river.
He lost his paddle in the river.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) feeling sudden strong fear and not able to think clearly
Note: Informal.
contexts: I started to feel panicky in the lift.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a limit or set of rules that controls how something is done
Note: Usually used in the plural: parameters.
contexts: We must work within the parameters of the budget.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) connected with being a mother or father, or with looking after children
contexts: Children under 12 need parental permission.

words.definition:
1. (noun) an area with its own church and priest
2. (noun) a small area of local government in Britain
contexts: He's the priest of a small parish.
The parish council meets every month.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) connected with the group of elected people who make the laws of a country
contexts: The parliamentary elections will be held in May.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) not complete
2. (adjective) (~ to) liking something very much
3. (adjective) supporting one side unfairly
contexts: The plan was only a partial success.
I'm quite partial to chocolate.
The referee was accused of being partial.

words.definition: 1. (adverb) not completely, or only to some degree
contexts: The road is partially closed.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the act of going past or of time going by
2. (noun) a person's death (a polite way of saying it)
3. (adjective) lasting only a short time
4. (idiom) (in ~) while talking about something else
contexts: The building has changed with the passing of time.
We were sad to hear of his passing.
It was just a passing interest.
She mentioned in passing that she was getting married.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) accepting what happens without trying to change it or react
2. (noun) (the ~) the form of a verb in which the subject receives the action, as in "The house was built"
3. (adjective) (~ smoking) breathing in smoke from other people's cigarettes
contexts: He's very passive and never complains.
Change these sentences into the passive.
Passive smoking can harm children.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a Christian priest who is in charge of a church
contexts: The pastor welcomed us to the service.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a small area that is different from the area around it
2. (noun) a small piece of material used to cover a hole or a damaged area
3. (noun) a small area of land for growing food
4. (noun) a piece of material worn over an injured eye
5. (noun) a small piece of computer code that fixes a problem in a program
6. (verb) to cover a hole with a small piece of material
7. (phrasal verb) (~ up) to end a disagreement and become friends again
8. (idiom) (a bad/rough ~) a difficult period
contexts: There were patches of ice on the road.
She sewed a patch on her jeans.
We have a vegetable patch.
He wore a patch over one eye.
Install the latest security patch.
He patched the hole in the roof.
They've patched up their differences.
They're going through a rough patch.

words.definition:
1. (noun) an official right to be the only person or company that can make and sell an invention
2. (verb) to get an official right to be the only one who can make and sell an invention
3. (adjective) clear and easy to see
contexts: She took out a patent on her design.
He patented the new machine.
That's a patent lie.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a path for walking
2. (noun) a way of reaching or achieving something
contexts: A narrow pathway led to the beach.
Education is a pathway to success.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to go around an area regularly to check that there is no trouble
2. (noun) a group of soldiers, police or vehicles that watch an area
3. (idiom) (on ~) going around an area to watch and check it
Note: patrol – patrolled – patrolled.
contexts: Police patrol the streets at night.
A police patrol stopped the car.
Two officers were on patrol.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a person who gives money and support to an artist or organization
2. (noun) a famous person who supports a charity and helps it get attention
3. (noun) a customer of a shop, restaurant or hotel
4. (adjective) (~ saint) a saint who is believed to protect a particular place or group
Note: Formal.
contexts: She's a patron of the arts.
The prince is a patron of several charities.
The restaurant is for patrons only.
St Patrick is the patron saint of Ireland.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the work of an international military force that keeps peace in an area where there has been fighting
2. (adjective) connected with keeping peace in an area where there has been fighting
contexts: The UN is involved in peacekeeping in the region.
Peacekeeping troops were sent to the border.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the pointed top of a mountain
2. (noun) the highest or most successful point or level
3. (adjective) busiest or highest
4. (verb) to reach the highest point or level
5. (noun) the front part of a cap that sticks out
contexts: Snow covered the mountain peaks.
Traffic is at its peak at 8 a.m.
Train fares are higher at peak times.
Sales peaked in December.
He pulled the peak of his cap down.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a poor person who owns or rents a small piece of land and grows food on it, especially in the past
contexts: The peasants worked on the land all day.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) strange or unusual, sometimes in a worrying way
2. (adjective) (~ to) belonging only to a particular person, place or thing
contexts: There's a peculiar smell in the kitchen.
This custom is peculiar to the region.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) (of food) likely to go bad quickly
contexts: Keep perishable food in the fridge.

words.definition:
1. (noun) something extra that you get from your job as well as your pay, such as a car or free meals
2. (noun) an advantage of a situation
3. (phrasal verb) (~ up) to become or make someone happier and more energetic
Note: Informal.
contexts: A free car is one of the perks of the job.
One perk of living here is the view.
She perked up when she heard the news.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a person who commits a crime or does something harmful
Note: Formal.
contexts: The police are still looking for the perpetrators.

words.definition: 1. (noun) cruel and unfair treatment of people, especially because of their race, religion or political beliefs
contexts: They fled their country to escape religious persecution.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to continue to exist or happen for longer than expected
2. (verb) to continue doing something, although it is difficult or other people do not want you to
contexts: If the pain persists, see a doctor.
She persisted with her studies.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) continuing for a long time, or happening again and again
2. (adjective) (of a person) continuing to try to do something, although it is difficult
contexts: She has a persistent cough.
He's very persistent – he never gives up.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the people who work for an organization or the army
2. (noun) the department of a company that deals with employing and training workers
Note: Stressed on "nel". The department is also called human resources.
contexts: All personnel must wear ID badges.
Speak to personnel about your holiday.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the feeling that bad things will happen
contexts: There is a lot of pessimism about the economy.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a written request, signed by many people, asking someone in authority to do something
2. (noun) an official request to a court of law
3. (verb) to make a formal request to someone in authority
contexts: Over 10,000 people signed the petition.
She filed a petition for divorce.
Residents petitioned the council to close the road.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a person who studies or writes about ideas such as the meaning of life, truth and knowledge
2. (noun) a person who thinks deeply about life
contexts: Plato was a famous Greek philosopher.
My grandfather was a bit of a philosopher.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) connected with the study of ideas about life, truth and knowledge
2. (adjective) staying calm when something bad happens
contexts: They had a philosophical discussion about free will.
She was philosophical about losing her job.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a doctor, especially one who treats illnesses without operations
Note: Formal, mainly American.
contexts: Consult your physician before taking this drug.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to eat only small amounts of food because you are not hungry or do not like it
2. (phrasal verb) to pull or touch something again and again with your fingers
contexts: She just picked at her dinner.
Stop picking at that scab!

words.definition:
1. (noun) a journey to a holy place for religious reasons
2. (noun) a visit to a place that is important to you
contexts: Every year, millions of Muslims make a pilgrimage to Mecca.
Fans make a pilgrimage to Elvis's home.

words.definition:
1. (noun) one of the first people to do something or develop a new area of knowledge
2. (noun) one of the first people to go and live in a new area
3. (verb) to be the first person to develop or use a new idea or method
contexts: She was a pioneer of modern medicine.
The pioneers travelled west in wagons.
He pioneered the use of solar energy.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a long line of pipes that carries oil or gas over a long distance
2. (idiom) (in the ~) being planned or developed and likely to happen soon
contexts: The pipeline runs across the desert.
There are big changes in the pipeline.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a person who attacks ships at sea to steal from them
2. (noun) a person who illegally copies and sells films, music or software
3. (verb) to illegally copy and sell films, music or software
4. (adjective) copied or broadcast illegally
contexts: Pirates attacked the ship.
Software pirates cost the industry millions.
The film was pirated before it came out.
He was selling pirate DVDs.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a large deep hole in the ground
2. (noun) a coal mine
3. (noun) (the ~s) the place beside a race track where cars stop for fuel and repairs
4. (noun) the hard seed in the middle of some fruits
5. (idiom) (the ~ of your stomach) the place where you feel fear or worry
6. (verb) (~ against) to make people or things compete against each other
Note: The meaning "hard seed" is American. In British English: stone.
contexts: They dug a pit for the rubbish.
He worked down the pit for 30 years.
He came into the pits to change tyres.
Remove the pits from the cherries.
I had a sick feeling in the pit of my stomach.
The final pits the two best teams against each other.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) reasonable and likely to be true
contexts: Her excuse sounded plausible.

words.definition: 1. (phrasal verb) to make something seem less important or serious than it really is
contexts: The government tried to play down the crisis.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a strong and emotional request for something
2. (noun) a statement in a court of law saying whether you are guilty or not
contexts: She made a plea for help.
He entered a plea of not guilty.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to ask for something in a strong and emotional way
2. (verb) to say in a court of law whether you are guilty or not
3. (verb) to give a reason or excuse for something
Note: plead – pleaded (US also: pled) – pleaded (US also: pled).
contexts: She pleaded with him to stay.
He pleaded guilty to theft.
She pleaded ignorance of the rules.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to make a formal or public promise to do or give something
2. (noun) a formal or public promise
contexts: The government pledged $10 million to help the victims.
She made a pledge to stop smoking.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a difficult, sad or dangerous situation that someone is in
Note: Formal.
contexts: The film shows the plight of refugees.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to walk slowly with heavy steps, because you are tired
2. (phrasal verb) (~ on/along) to continue working slowly at something boring
Note: plod – plodded – plodded.
contexts: We plodded up the hill.
He plodded on with his work.

words.definition:
1. (noun) an object with metal pins that connects a piece of equipment to the electricity supply
2. (noun) a round piece of rubber or plastic that you put in a hole to stop water flowing out
3. (noun) praise for a product or event, to advertise it
4. (verb) to fill a hole so that nothing can pass through
5. (phrasal verb) (~ in) to connect a piece of equipment to the electricity supply
6. (idiom) (pull the ~ on) to stop something from continuing
Note: plug – plugged – plugged.
contexts: The plug on the kettle is broken.
Pull out the plug and let the water drain.
She gave her new book a plug on TV.
He plugged the hole with paper.
Plug in the TV.
The bank pulled the plug on the project.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to fall or move down suddenly from a high position
2. (verb) (of prices or values) to fall suddenly by a large amount
3. (verb) to push something firmly and deeply into something
4. (noun) a sudden fall in value or amount
5. (idiom) (take the ~) to decide to do something important or risky
contexts: The car plunged into the river.
Share prices plunged.
She plunged her hand into the cold water.
There was a plunge in sales.
They finally took the plunge and got married.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the illegal hunting or catching of animals, birds or fish
2. (noun) the act of taking workers or players from another company or team
contexts: Elephant poaching is a serious problem.
The company was accused of poaching staff from its rivals.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a long, thin stick of wood or metal, often used to hold something up
2. (noun) one of the two points at the most northern or southern ends of the earth
3. (noun) one of two opposite ideas or positions
4. (idiom) (~s apart) completely different
contexts: The flag was on a tall pole.
They travelled to the South Pole.
Their views are at opposite poles.
The two brothers are poles apart.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to eat or drink all of something quickly
2. (phrasal verb) to finish a piece of work quickly
Note: Informal.
contexts: He polished off a whole pizza.
I polished off the report in an hour.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a study in which many people are asked the same questions to find out what most people think
2. (noun) (the ~s) an election, or the place where people vote
3. (verb) to ask many people the same questions to find out what they think
contexts: A recent poll shows the president is losing support.
The country goes to the polls next month.
We polled 1,000 voters.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a collection of examples of someone's work, used to show their skills
2. (noun) the shares and investments that a person or company owns
3. (noun) the area of responsibility of a government minister
Note: Plural: portfolios.
contexts: The artist showed her portfolio to the gallery.
He has a large share portfolio.
She holds the foreign affairs portfolio.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to show or describe someone or something in a particular way
2. (verb) to play a character in a film or play
contexts: The film portrays him as a hero.
She portrayed the queen in the film.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) existing or happening after the end of a period of fighting between countries, especially after 1945
Note: Also written: postwar.
contexts: The post-war years were a time of great change.

words.definition: 1. (verb) to arrange for an event to happen at a later time than planned
contexts: The match was postponed because of rain.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a meal to which every guest brings some food to share
2. (idiom) (take ~) to accept whatever is available without knowing what it will be
Note: The meal meaning is mainly American.
contexts: We're having a potluck at the office on Friday.
We didn't book, so we'll just take potluck.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a person who works in a profession, especially medicine or law
2. (noun) a person who regularly does a particular activity
Note: Formal.
contexts: She's a medical practitioner.
He's a practitioner of yoga.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) dealing with problems in a practical and sensible way, not based on theory
contexts: We need a pragmatic solution to the problem.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to give a religious talk, especially in a church
2. (verb) to give advice about how to behave, in a way that is annoying
3. (verb) to try to persuade people to accept a belief or way of life
contexts: The priest preached about forgiveness.
Stop preaching at me!
He preaches the importance of hard work.

words.definition:
1. (noun) an action or decision from the past that is used as an example or rule for the future
Note: Formal.
contexts: The court's decision set a precedent for similar cases.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the quality of being exact and accurate
contexts: The work was done with great precision.

words.definition:
1. (noun) an animal that kills and eats other animals
2. (noun) a person who uses other people, especially sexually, for their own advantage
contexts: Lions are predators.
Parents must protect children from online predators.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a person who had a job or position before someone else
2. (noun) something that came before something else
contexts: The new manager is very different from her predecessor.
The new phone is faster than its predecessor.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) most common, most noticeable or most powerful
Note: Formal.
contexts: Red is the predominant colour in the painting.

words.definition:
1. (adverb) mostly or mainly
Note: Formal.
contexts: The town is predominantly Catholic.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the time when a woman or female animal has a baby growing inside her body
contexts: Don't drink alcohol during pregnancy.

words.definition:
1. (noun) an unfair opinion or dislike of a person or group that is not based on reason or experience
2. (verb) to make someone have an unfair opinion about someone or something
3. (verb) to harm someone's chances of something
contexts: Racial prejudice is still a problem.
The news reports may prejudice the jury.
This could prejudice your chances of getting the job.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) coming before the main part of something, to prepare for it
2. (noun) something done first, to prepare for the main event
Note: Formal.
contexts: The preliminary results look good.
After the preliminaries, the meeting began.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) happening too early or before the right time
2. (adjective) (of a baby) born before the normal time
contexts: It's premature to say who will win.
The baby was six weeks premature.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the leader of a government, a prime minister
2. (adjective) best or most important
contexts: The Chinese premier visited Europe.
It's the country's premier university.

words.definition:
1. (noun) an idea or statement that an argument or theory is based on
2. (noun) (~s) the building and land that a business uses
contexts: The film is based on a simple premise.
Smoking is not allowed on the premises.

words.definition:
1. (noun) an extra amount of money that you pay in addition to the normal price
2. (noun) an amount of money you pay regularly for insurance
3. (adjective) of very high quality and more expensive
4. (idiom) (at a ~) difficult to get because many people want it
contexts: You pay a premium for a room with a sea view.
Insurance premiums have gone up.
They sell premium coffee.
Space is at a premium in the city.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a piece of paper on which a doctor writes the medicine that a patient needs
2. (noun) medicine that a doctor has ordered for you
3. (noun) a suggestion or plan for making something better
contexts: The doctor gave me a prescription for antibiotics.
You can collect your prescription at the chemist.
The report offers a prescription for economic growth.

words.definition:
1. (adverb) at this time, now
2. (adverb) soon, or after a short time
Note: Formal.
contexts: She is presently working in London.
The doctor will see you presently.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the act of keeping something in its original state or in good condition
2. (noun) the act of keeping something safe from harm
contexts: They work for the preservation of old buildings.
Our main aim is the preservation of peace.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) (~ over) to be in charge of a meeting, ceremony or court
2. (phrasal verb) (~ over) to be in control of a situation, especially a bad one
Note: Formal.
contexts: The judge presided over the trial.
He presided over the company's collapse.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the job of being president, or the period of time someone is president
contexts: During his presidency, the economy grew.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) connected with a president or the job of president
contexts: The presidential election is in November.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the respect and admiration that someone or something gets because of success or high quality
Note: Pronounced like pre-STEEZH.
contexts: The job brings a lot of prestige.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) very respected and admired, usually because of high quality
contexts: She went to a prestigious university.

words.definition: 1. (adverb) used to say that you think something is probably true
contexts: Presumably, he forgot about the meeting.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to think that something is probably true, without being certain
2. (verb) (~ to) to do something that you have no right to do
Note: Formal.
contexts: I presume you're hungry after your journey.
I wouldn't presume to tell you how to do your job.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to win a fight or argument, or to be successful in the end
2. (verb) to exist or be common in a particular place or time
3. (phrasal verb) (~ on/upon) to persuade someone to do something
Note: Formal.
contexts: Justice will prevail.
This belief still prevails in some areas.
She prevailed on him to stay.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the fact of being very common in a particular place or time
Note: Formal.
contexts: The prevalence of obesity is rising.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) very common in a particular place or at a particular time
Note: Formal.
contexts: The disease is prevalent in hot countries.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the act of stopping something bad from happening
contexts: Crime prevention is the job of the police.

words.definition:
1. (noun) an animal that is hunted and killed by another animal for food
2. (noun) a person who is easy to cheat or harm
3. (phrasal verb) (~ on) to hunt and kill another animal for food
4. (phrasal verb) (~ on) to harm or cheat people who are weak
5. (idiom) (~ on your mind) to make you worry all the time
contexts: The lion caught its prey.
Old people are easy prey for criminals.
Owls prey on mice.
The gang preyed on tourists.
The problem has been preying on my mind.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the act of selling a business or industry owned by the government to private companies
Note: British spelling also: privatisation.
contexts: The privatization of the railways was unpopular.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a special right or advantage that only some people have
2. (noun) the advantages that rich and powerful people have
3. (noun) something that you are lucky and honoured to do
contexts: Education should be a right, not a privilege.
She grew up in a life of privilege.
It was a privilege to work with her.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) acting early to prevent problems or make things happen, rather than waiting
contexts: We need to be more proactive about safety.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a careful investigation into something
2. (noun) a spacecraft without people, sent to get information
3. (verb) to try to find out the facts about something
4. (verb) to examine something with a long, thin tool
Note: The noun meaning "investigation" is used mainly in newspapers.
contexts: The police started a probe into the deaths.
A space probe was sent to Mars.
Journalists probed into her past.
The doctor probed the wound.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) causing difficulties or full of difficulties
contexts: The new system is proving problematic.

words.definition:
1. (noun) legal action taken against someone in a court
2. (noun) a series of events that happen in a particular place
3. (noun) an official written record of a meeting
Note: Formal.
contexts: They started legal proceedings against the company.
The proceedings began with a speech.
The proceedings of the conference were published.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the money that you get from selling something or from an event
contexts: All proceeds from the sale will go to charity.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the act of dealing with documents or information in an official way
2. (noun) the act of treating food or materials in a factory to change them
3. (noun) the use of a computer to work with information
contexts: Visa processing takes two weeks.
Food processing is a big industry here.
The computer has fast processing power.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the main part of a computer that deals with data and instructions
2. (noun) a machine or company that treats food or materials
contexts: This laptop has a fast processor.
She bought a food processor to chop vegetables.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to announce something officially and publicly
2. (verb) to say something strongly or show it clearly
Note: Formal.
contexts: The country proclaimed its independence in 1960.
He proclaimed his innocence.

words.definition: 1. (verb) to keep delaying something that you should do, usually because you do not want to do it
contexts: Stop procrastinating and start your homework!

words.definition:
1. (adjective) producing or achieving a lot
2. (adjective) (of land) good for growing a lot of crops
contexts: We had a very productive meeting.
The land here is very productive.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the amount of goods or work that a person, factory or country produces compared with the time or money used
contexts: New machines have increased productivity.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) able to do something well because of training and practice
contexts: She's proficient in three languages.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) making money
2. (adjective) useful or helpful
contexts: The business is very profitable.
It was a profitable discussion.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) very great or strong
2. (adjective) showing deep understanding or serious thought
contexts: The book had a profound effect on me.
She made some profound comments.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a guess about a future amount or situation, based on information you have now
2. (noun) the act of showing a film or picture on a screen
3. (noun) something that sticks out from a surface
contexts: Sales projections for next year look good.
The room is used for film projection.
There was a small projection on the rock.

words.definition: 1. (verb) to make something last longer
contexts: The drugs prolonged his life.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) continuing for a long time, often longer than expected
contexts: There was a prolonged silence.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) important and well known
2. (adjective) easy to see or notice
3. (adjective) sticking out from something
contexts: She's a prominent politician.
The church is a prominent feature of the village.
He has a prominent nose.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) very easy to notice
contexts: She has a pronounced French accent.

words.definition:
1. (noun) an object used by actors in a play or film
2. (noun) an object used to support something and keep it in position
3. (verb) to support something by leaning it against something else
4. (phrasal verb) (~ up) to help something that is weak to continue
Note: prop – propped – propped.
contexts: The gun was just a stage prop.
They used wooden props to hold up the roof.
He propped his bike against the wall.
The government propped up the bank.

words.definition: 1. (noun) information, often false or one-sided, that a government or group uses to make people think in a particular way
contexts: The war films were pure propaganda.

words.definition:
1. (noun) an idea, plan or offer, especially in business
2. (noun) a statement that expresses an opinion or idea
3. (verb) to suggest to someone that they have sex with you
contexts: Opening a café here is an attractive proposition.
I don't accept the proposition that all people are selfish.
He propositioned her at the party.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to officially accuse someone of a crime in a court of law
2. (verb) (of a lawyer) to try to show in court that someone is guilty
contexts: Shoplifters will be prosecuted.
She prosecuted the case.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the process of officially accusing someone of a crime in a court of law
2. (noun) (the ~) the lawyers in a court who try to show that someone is guilty
contexts: He faces prosecution for fraud.
The prosecution called its first witness.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a lawyer who tries to show in a court of law that someone is guilty of a crime
contexts: The prosecutor asked for a ten-year sentence.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) likely to become something in the future
contexts: We showed the house to prospective buyers.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the state of being successful and having a lot of money
contexts: The country enjoyed years of peace and prosperity.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) used or meant to keep someone or something safe
2. (adjective) wanting to keep someone safe from harm
contexts: Workers must wear protective clothing.
She's very protective of her children.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a set of rules about the correct way to behave in official situations
2. (noun) an official set of rules or steps for doing something
3. (noun) an international agreement
4. (noun) a set of rules that computers use to send information to each other
contexts: According to protocol, the president arrives last.
Doctors followed the safety protocol.
The countries signed the Kyoto Protocol.
The website uses a secure protocol.

words.definition:
1. (noun) one of the areas that some countries are divided into, with its own local government
2. (noun) (the ~s) all the parts of a country except the capital city
3. (noun) an area of knowledge or responsibility
contexts: Canada has ten provinces.

Finance is not my province.

words.definition:

3. (adjective) (of people or ideas) old-fashioned and not interested in new things

His views are very provincial.

words.definition:

words.definition:

contexts: His comments provoked anger.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) connected with mental illness and its treatment

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to get better after a serious illness or injury
2. (phrasal verb) to succeed in dealing with a difficult situation
contexts: The doctors think she'll pull through.

words.definition:

2. (noun) a short regular sound, light or electrical signal
3. (noun) (~s) the seeds of some plants, such as beans and lentils, eaten as food

contexts: The nurse took my pulse.

Pulses are a good source of protein.
Music pulsed through the room.

words.definition: 1. (phrasal verb) to explain your ideas or feelings clearly so that people understand them

words.definition:

words.definition:
1. (adjective) connected with how good something is, rather than how much of it there is

words.definition:

contexts: The study used quantitative data.

words.definition:

Note: Formal.

She queried the bill.

words.definition:

words.definition:
1. (noun) a fixed amount or number of something that is officially allowed

words.definition:
1. (noun) a system that uses radio waves to find the position of planes, ships and other objects

words.definition:
1. (adjective) (of a change) very great and complete

contexts: The company needs radical changes.

words.definition:

words.definition:

The kids raided the fridge.

words.definition:

The team rallied in the second half.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a position on a list that shows how good or important someone or something is
2. (adjective) having a high position in an organization
contexts: She's number one in the world rankings.
He's the ranking officer here.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the crime of forcing someone to have sex

contexts: He was found guilty of rape.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the relationship between two amounts, shown by two numbers

contexts: The ratio of boys to girls in the class is 2 to 1.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) based on reason and clear thinking, not on feelings

words.definition:
1. (noun) a narrow line of light or heat

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to stretch out your arm to touch or hold something

contexts: She reached out and took my hand.

words.definition:
1. (adverb) quickly and easily

words.definition:
1. (noun) the moment when you understand or become aware of something
2. (noun) the act of achieving something you planned or hoped for
Note: British spelling also: realisation.
contexts: She came to the realization that she was in love.
The new house was the realization of a dream.

words.definition:
1. (noun) an area of activity, interest or knowledge
2. (noun) a country ruled by a king or queen
Note: Formal.
contexts: It's within the realm of possibility.
The king defended his realm.

words.definition:
1. (noun) (the ~) the back part of something
2. (adjective) at the back
3. (verb) to look after children or young animals until they are fully grown
4. (verb) (of a horse) to stand on its back legs

contexts: There's a garden at the rear of the house.
The rear window was broken.
She reared five children on her own.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the process of thinking about something in a logical way to form an opinion
contexts: I don't follow your reasoning.

words.definition: 1. (verb) to say or do something to make someone feel less worried
contexts: The doctor reassured her that the baby was fine.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a person who fights against the government of their country

contexts: The rebels took control of the city.

Teenagers often rebel against their parents.

words.definition:
1. (noun) an organized fight against the government by a group of people using violence
2. (noun) opposition to authority or normal rules
contexts: The army crushed the rebellion.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to bounce back after hitting something

She married him on the rebound.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a person who receives something

contexts: She was the recipient of the Nobel Prize.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the process of building or making something again after it has been damaged or destroyed
2. (noun) an attempt to show how a past event happened, for example by acting it out

The police did a reconstruction of the crime.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to tell someone a story or describe events that happened

contexts: She recounted her adventures in Africa.

The losing side asked for a recount.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) without a job because your employer no longer needs you
2. (adjective) no longer needed or useful
Note: The first meaning is British.
contexts: 200 workers were made redundant.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a vote in which all the people in a country can decide on one important question

words.definition:
1. (verb) to make a substance such as oil or sugar pure by taking out other substances

words.definition:

words.definition:
1. (noun) a change that improves a system, law or organization

words.definition:
1. (noun) a place or situation that gives protection from danger or trouble

words.definition: 1. (verb) to repair and decorate a building to make it look new again
contexts: The hotel has been completely refurbished.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the act of saying or showing that you will not do or accept something
contexts: His refusal to help surprised everyone.

words.definition: 1. (verb) to get something back that you had before
contexts: She slowly regained her strength.

words.definition:
1. (adverb) (~ of) without being affected by something, or not considering it

words.definition:
1. (noun) a government, especially one that was not elected and is unfair or cruel

Note: Pronounced like ray-ZHEEM.

words.definition:
1. (noun) an official organization that controls an industry and makes sure it follows the rules

The heating has a temperature regulator.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) connected with controlling an activity or industry with official rules

contexts: The company needs regulatory approval for the drug.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the process of helping someone return to a normal life after prison, illness or drug problems
2. (noun) the process of returning a building or area to good condition
Note: Short form: rehab.
contexts: He's in a drug rehabilitation centre.
The rehabilitation of the old docks took ten years.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the period of time when a king or queen rules a country

She's the reigning world champion.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the act of refusing to accept or agree to something

words.definition: 1. (noun) the quality of being able to be trusted to work well or behave as expected

words.definition:

words.definition: 1. (noun) the feeling of not wanting to do something

words.definition:

2. (noun) a very good and kind person
Note: Short form in names: St.
contexts: Saint Peter was one of Jesus's followers.
You're a saint for helping me!

words.definition:
1. (idiom) (for the ~ of / for someone's ~) in order to help or please someone or something
2. (idiom) (for goodness' ~ / for heaven's ~) used to show you are annoyed
3. (idiom) (for the ~ of it) for no special reason
contexts: He moved to the country for the sake of his health.
For goodness' sake, hurry up!
He argues just for the sake of it.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a place where people are safe from danger or harm
2. (noun) an area where birds and animals are protected
3. (noun) a quiet and peaceful place
contexts: The church gave sanctuary to the refugees.
We visited a bird sanctuary.
My garden is my sanctuary.

words.definition: 1. (verb) to walk in a slow, relaxed and confident way
contexts: He sauntered into the room as if nothing had happened.

words.definition: 1. (verb) to run quickly with small, light steps, like a child or small animal
contexts: The children scampered across the beach.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) spread over a large area, not close together
2. (adjective) (of weather) happening in a few places, not everywhere
contexts: There are a few scattered houses in the valley.
Expect scattered showers this afternoon.

words.definition:
1. (noun) an animal or bird that eats dead animals or food that people have thrown away
2. (noun) a person who searches through rubbish for things to use or sell
contexts: Vultures are scavengers.
Scavengers searched the rubbish tip.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the range of things that a subject, activity or law deals with
2. (noun) the opportunity to do or develop something
contexts: The issue is outside the scope of this report.
There's plenty of scope for improvement.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a thin metal pin with a spiral shape, which you turn to fix things together
2. (verb) to fix something with a thin metal pin with a spiral shape
3. (verb) to turn something to fasten it or open it

5. (phrasal verb) (~ up your eyes/face) to close your eyes a little or twist your face

contexts: The shelf is held up by four screws.
Screw the shelf to the wall.
Screw the lid on tightly.
I really screwed up the interview.
She screwed up her eyes in the bright sun.

words.definition:
1. (noun) careful and detailed examination
Note: Formal.
contexts: The government's plans are under close scrutiny.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to run with short quick steps, especially to get away

contexts: The crab scuttled across the sand.
The argument scuttled the deal.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to close an envelope, container or opening tightly

4. (noun) an official mark on a document

6. (phrasal verb) (~ off) to stop people from entering an area
contexts: She sealed the envelope.
They sealed the deal with a handshake.
We watched the seals on the rocks.
The letter had the king's seal.
The seal on the jar is broken.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) not religious, or not connected with religion
contexts: Turkey is a secular state.

words.definition:

words.definition:

words.definition: 1. (noun) the policy of keeping people of different races, religions or sexes apart

words.definition:
1. (verb) to take hold of something suddenly and firmly

3. (verb) (of police or officials) to take something away by law
4. (verb) to take a chance quickly

The army seized power.
Police seized drugs worth $1 million.
She seized the opportunity to travel.
The engine seized up.

words.definition:
1. (adverb) not often

contexts: We seldom go out in the evening.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) choosing carefully, so that only the best are included
2. (adjective) affecting or including only some people or things

words.definition: 1. (noun) a member of the upper group of lawmakers in some countries, such as the US

words.definition:
1. (noun) a physical feeling

3. (noun) great excitement and interest, or a person or thing that causes it

I had the strange sensation that someone was watching me.
The new singer is a sensation.
He lost all sensation in his legs.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) presenting news or stories in a shocking way to make people interested
contexts: I hate sensationalist newspapers.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the ability to understand other people's feelings and problems
2. (noun) the quality of reacting quickly or strongly to something, such as heat or criticism
3. (noun) the quality of needing careful treatment because people may be upset
contexts: She showed great sensitivity to his needs.
I have sensitivity to cold.
Be aware of the sensitivity of the subject.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a feeling or opinion about something

Note: Formal.
contexts: Public sentiment is against the war.
There's no room for sentiment in business.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the act of dividing or keeping people or things apart

contexts: The separation of the twins was hard.

words.definition:

He's a serial liar.

words.definition: 1. (idiom) to make a process or series of events start
contexts: The decision set in motion a series of changes.

words.definition:
1. (noun) an official agreement that ends an argument or disagreement

contexts: The two sides reached a settlement.

words.definition:

words.definition:
1. (noun) how serious or bad something is

words.definition:

words.definition:

words.definition:

Note: shed – shed – shed.

I need to shed a few kilos.
Snakes shed their skin.

words.definition:

words.definition:

words.definition: 1. (noun) the amount by which something is less than what is needed or expected

Note: shrink – shrank – shrunk. The noun is informal.

words.definition:

words.definition:

words.definition: 1. (idiom) in my opinion
