words.definition: 1. (idiom) used after giving a few examples, to show that there are many more
contexts: We sell apples, pears and plums, to name but a few.

words.definition: 1. (idiom) used when you say something again using different words to make it clearer
contexts: We spent too much. To put it another way, we're broke.

words.definition: 1. (idiom) used when you say something in a very direct and honest way
contexts: To put it bluntly, your work isn't good enough.

words.definition: 1. (idiom) used to show that the situation is much worse than your words suggest
contexts: The food was disappointing, to put it mildly.

words.definition: 1. (idiom) used to show that you could describe something in a much stronger way
contexts: His behaviour was strange, to say the least.

words.definition:
1. (idiom) used to add a final detail that makes a situation even better or worse
Note: British English also: to top it all.
contexts: I lost my wallet, and to top it all off, I missed my bus.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the dried leaves of a plant that are smoked in cigarettes and pipes
contexts: The government has raised the tax on tobacco.

words.definition:
1. (noun) willingness to accept beliefs or behaviour that are different from your own
2. (noun) the ability to bear pain or difficult conditions
3. (noun) the body's ability to deal with a drug or food without bad effects
contexts: We need more tolerance of other cultures.
He has a high tolerance for pain.
She has a low tolerance to alcohol.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to accept behaviour or opinions that you do not like or agree with
2. (verb) to be able to bear something unpleasant or difficult
contexts: We will not tolerate bad behaviour.
These plants can tolerate cold weather.

words.definition:
1. (noun) money that you pay to use a road or bridge
2. (noun) the number of people killed or hurt in an accident, war or disaster
3. (idiom) (take its ~) to have a bad effect over a period of time
4. (verb) (of a bell) to ring slowly
contexts: We paid a toll to cross the bridge.
The death toll has risen to 50.
Years of stress have taken their toll on his health.
The church bell tolled.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the act of causing someone great pain on purpose, to punish them or get information
2. (noun) a very unpleasant experience
3. (verb) to cause someone great pain on purpose, to punish them or get information
4. (verb) to make someone feel very worried or unhappy
contexts: The prisoners suffered torture.
The long wait was torture.
The soldiers tortured their prisoners.
He was tortured by guilt.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to throw something lightly or carelessly
2. (verb) to throw a coin into the air to decide something, depending on which side it lands on
3. (verb) to move around in an uncontrolled way
4. (verb) to mix food with a sauce or dressing
contexts: She tossed the keys to me.
Let's toss a coin to decide who goes first.
I tossed and turned all night.
Toss the salad with olive oil.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) poisonous and harmful
2. (adjective) (of a person or relationship) very unpleasant and harmful to you
contexts: The factory released toxic chemicals.
She left a toxic relationship.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a name, symbol or design that a company uses for its products and that nobody else can legally use
2. (noun) a quality or way of behaving that someone is known for
contexts: The logo is a registered trademark.
His red hat became his trademark.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a path through the countryside
2. (noun) a series of marks or signs left by someone or something that is moving
3. (verb) to be behind someone in a game or competition
4. (verb) to follow someone secretly
5. (verb) to pull something behind you, often along the ground
contexts: We followed a trail through the forest.
The car left a trail of smoke.
The team trailed 2–0 at half-time.
Detectives trailed him for weeks.
Her dress trailed on the floor.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a short series of scenes from a film, shown to advertise it
2. (noun) a vehicle without an engine that is pulled by a car or truck
3. (noun) a vehicle that people can live in, pulled by a car
Note: The last meaning is American. In British English: caravan.
contexts: Have you seen the trailer for the new film?
We put the bikes on a trailer.
They live in a trailer park.

words.definition:
1. (noun) an act of buying or selling something, or of moving money
Note: Formal.
contexts: All transactions are recorded by the bank.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a written or printed copy of words that were spoken
2. (noun) an official record of a student's courses and grades
Note: The second meaning is American.
contexts: Read the transcript of the interview.
The university asked for my transcript.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a complete change in someone or something
contexts: The town has gone through a huge transformation.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the process of moving people or goods from one place to another
2. (noun) a system of buses and trains for the public
3. (adjective) (of a passenger or area) passing through a place on the way to somewhere else
Note: The meaning about buses and trains is American. In British English: public transport.
contexts: Some items were damaged in transit.
The city has good public transit.
We waited in the transit lounge.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the act of sending out signals by radio or TV, or a programme that is sent
2. (noun) the process of passing a disease from one person to another
3. (noun) the parts of a car that carry power from the engine to the wheels
contexts: The transmission was interrupted by the storm.
Wash your hands to prevent the transmission of the virus.
The car has an automatic transmission.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the quality of being open and honest, so that people can see what is happening
2. (noun) the quality of being clear enough to see through
contexts: The public wants more transparency in government.
The transparency of the water was amazing.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) clear enough to see through
2. (adjective) (of a system or organization) open and honest
3. (adjective) (of a lie or feeling) very easy to notice
contexts: The box is made of transparent plastic.
The voting process must be transparent.
His excuse was transparent.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a very upsetting experience that causes great shock or mental damage for a long time
2. (noun) a serious physical injury
contexts: She never got over the trauma of the war.
He suffered head trauma in the crash.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a formal written agreement between two or more countries
contexts: The two countries signed a trade treaty.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) very great in amount, size or level
2. (adjective) very good
contexts: There was a tremendous noise.
You've done a tremendous job.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) connected with a tribe or tribes
2. (adjective) showing strong loyalty to your own group
contexts: They follow tribal traditions.
Football fans can be very tribal.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a special court or group of people who make official decisions about a particular type of problem
contexts: She took her employer to an employment tribunal.

words.definition:
1. (noun) something that you say, do or give to show respect or admiration for someone, especially after they die
2. (idiom) (be a ~ to) to show how good someone or something is
contexts: Fans paid tribute to the singer.
Her success is a tribute to her hard work.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a group of three people or things
Note: Plural: trios.
contexts: A trio of musicians played at the wedding.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a great success or victory
2. (noun) the feeling of great happiness that you get from a victory
3. (verb) to win or be very successful, especially after a difficult struggle
contexts: The show was a triumph.
She raised her arms in triumph.
Good will triumph over evil.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) not important or serious
contexts: Don't worry about such trivial things.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a cup or other object that is given as a prize for winning a competition
2. (noun) something that you keep to show your success, especially in hunting
contexts: The captain lifted the trophy.
The walls were covered with hunting trophies.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) worried and anxious
2. (adjective) having a lot of problems
contexts: She looked troubled.
He had a troubled childhood.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a person or one of a group of people who manage money or property for someone else or for an organization
contexts: She is a trustee of the charity.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to start eating food with enthusiasm
Note: Informal.
contexts: The kids tucked into their pizza.

words.definition:
1. (noun) teaching, especially to one person or a small group
2. (noun) the money that you pay for being taught at a college or university
contexts: She gives private tuition in maths.
Tuition fees have gone up.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a state of great confusion, worry or lack of order
contexts: The country is in political turmoil.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the number of people who vote in an election or come to an event
contexts: There was a high turnout for the election.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the total amount of money a business makes from sales in a period of time
2. (noun) the rate at which workers leave a company and are replaced
3. (noun) a small pie made by folding pastry over fruit
contexts: The company has an annual turnover of $5 million.
The restaurant has a high staff turnover.
I had an apple turnover.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a thick, rough cloth made of wool, often with different colours
contexts: He wore a tweed jacket.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to be unfaithful to your partner by having a secret relationship with someone else
Note: Informal.
contexts: She found out he was two-timing her.

words.definition:
1. (noun) cruel and unfair use of power by a ruler or government
2. (noun) something that controls your life in an unfair way
contexts: The people lived under tyranny for decades.
She escaped the tyranny of the office.

words.definition:
1. (idiom) kept in a safe place that is locked
2. (idiom) (of a person) kept in prison
contexts: The jewels are kept under lock and key.
The killer is now under lock and key.

words.definition:
1. (idiom) very close to you, but not noticed
2. (idiom) happening openly, but without you noticing
contexts: You'll find your keys right under your nose if you look carefully.
They were stealing money right under your nose.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) real and important but not obvious
2. (adjective) lying under something else
contexts: We need to find the underlying cause of the problem.
The underlying rock is very hard.

words.definition: 1. (verb) to make someone or something slowly become weaker or less effective
contexts: The scandal undermined public trust in the government.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) not having enough workers
contexts: The hospital is badly understaffed.

words.definition: 1. (adverb) used to say that something is certainly true
contexts: She is undoubtedly the best player on the team.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to make separate parts or groups become one
Note: unify – unified – unified.
contexts: The new leader wants to unify the party.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) never having happened or existed before
contexts: The country faces an unprecedented crisis.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to show or announce something publicly for the first time
2. (verb) to remove the cover from a new statue or sign in a ceremony
contexts: The company unveiled its new phone.
The mayor unveiled a statue of the poet.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) planned to happen soon
contexts: Are you ready for the upcoming exams?

words.definition:
1. (verb) to improve a machine or system, or to change it for a newer version
2. (verb) to give someone a better seat or room than the one they paid for
3. (noun) an improvement to a newer or better version
contexts: I upgraded my phone.
We were upgraded to first class.
The upgrade is free.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to support a law, decision or principle and make sure it continues
2. (verb) (of a court) to decide that an earlier decision was correct
Note: uphold – upheld – upheld. Formal.
contexts: The police must uphold the law.
The higher court decided to uphold the ban.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the process of more and more people moving from the countryside to towns and cities
Note: British spelling also: urbanisation.
contexts: Rapid urbanization has caused many problems.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to use something in an effective way
Note: Formal. British spelling also: utilise.
contexts: We need to utilize our resources better.

words.definition: 1. (adverb) completely and totally (used to make a word stronger)
contexts: I was utterly exhausted.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) not clear or detailed
2. (adjective) (of a shape) not clear to see
3. (adjective) (of a person) not clear in what they think or say
contexts: He gave a vague answer.
I saw a vague figure in the fog.
She was very vague about her plans.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to prove that something is true or correct
2. (verb) to make something officially acceptable
3. (verb) to make someone feel that their feelings or opinions are important
Note: Formal.
contexts: The results validate our theory.
Your ticket must be validated before you travel.
Listening to her validated her feelings.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the state of being legally or officially acceptable
2. (noun) the state of being based on good reasons or facts
contexts: Check the validity of your passport.
I question the validity of his argument.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to disappear suddenly in a way that cannot be explained
2. (verb) to stop existing
contexts: The boy vanished on his way home.
Many old customs are vanishing.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) likely to change often
2. (noun) a situation, number or quantity that can change
contexts: The weather here is very variable.
There are too many variables to predict the result.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) of many different types
2. (adjective) changing often, and so interesting
contexts: She has a very varied diet.
His job is very varied.

words.definition:
1. (noun) one of the tubes in the body that carry blood to the heart
2. (noun) a thin line of metal or another substance in rock
3. (idiom) (in the same ~) in the same style or manner
contexts: The nurse put a needle into a vein in my arm.
They found a vein of gold.
He went on in the same vein for an hour.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a soft cloth with a thick, short surface on one side
contexts: She wore a red velvet dress.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a new business or activity that involves risk
2. (verb) to go somewhere that may be dangerous or unpleasant
3. (verb) to say something carefully because people may not like it
contexts: The new restaurant is a joint venture between two chefs.
We didn't venture outside during the storm.
She ventured an opinion.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) spoken rather than written
2. (adjective) connected with words or using words
contexts: We had a verbal agreement.
He suffered verbal abuse.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the official decision of a jury or judge in a court about whether someone is guilty
2. (noun) an opinion or decision about something after thinking about it
contexts: The jury returned a verdict of not guilty.
What's your verdict on the new menu?

words.definition:
1. (verb) to check or prove that something is true or correct
Note: verify – verified – verified.
contexts: Can you verify your address?

words.definition:
1. (adjective) (of a person) able to do many different things well
2. (adjective) (of an object) having many different uses
contexts: She's a versatile actress.
Eggs are a versatile food.

words.definition:
1. (noun) writing in which the lines have a regular rhythm and often rhyme
2. (noun) one part of a poem or song, made of several lines
3. (noun) a short numbered part of a book of the Bible
contexts: The play is written in verse.
Let's sing the first verse again.
The priest read a verse from the Bible.

words.definition:
1. (preposition) used to show that two teams or people are playing or competing against each other
2. (preposition) used to compare two different things or ideas
Note: Short forms: v., vs.
contexts: Tonight's game is England versus France.
It's a question of quality versus price.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a large boat or ship
2. (noun) a container for liquids, such as a bowl or cup
3. (noun) (blood ~) a tube that carries blood through the body
Note: Formal.
contexts: The vessel sank off the coast.
The museum has ancient drinking vessels.
Smoking damages blood vessels.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a person who has been a soldier, sailor or pilot in a war
2. (noun) a person who has done a job or activity for a long time
3. (adjective) having a lot of experience
contexts: He's a Vietnam veteran.
She's a veteran of 20 years in politics.
He's a veteran journalist.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to officially refuse to allow a law or decision, when you have the power to do this
2. (noun) the right to officially refuse to allow a law or decision
Note: Plural (noun): vetoes.
contexts: The president vetoed the bill.
Five countries have a veto at the UN.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) able to work successfully
contexts: Is this plan financially viable?

words.definition:
1. (adjective) full of energy, life and excitement
2. (adjective) (of colours) very bright and strong
contexts: It's a vibrant city with lots of nightlife.
She painted the room a vibrant red.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a bad habit or weakness
2. (noun) criminal activities, such as selling drugs or sex
3. (noun) a tool that holds an object firmly while you work on it
4. (adjective) (~ president/captain) the person next in rank below the leader
Note: The tool is spelled "vise" in American English.
contexts: Chocolate is my only vice.
The police unit fights vice in the city.
Hold the wood in a vice.
She's the vice president of the company.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) violent and cruel
2. (adjective) (of an animal) dangerous and likely to attack
3. (adjective) meant to hurt someone's feelings
4. (idiom) (~ circle) a situation in which one problem causes another, which makes the first problem worse
contexts: It was a vicious attack.
Be careful – the dog is vicious.
She made a vicious remark about him.
Poverty and poor health form a vicious circle.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) strong, active and full of energy
2. (adjective) done with determination and strength
contexts: Do 30 minutes of vigorous exercise a day.
They launched a vigorous campaign against the plan.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a person who lives in a village
contexts: The villagers welcomed us.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to break a law, rule or agreement
2. (verb) to not respect someone's rights or privacy
3. (verb) to damage a holy place
Note: Formal.
contexts: The company violated safety rules.
The photos violated her privacy.
The temple was violated.

words.definition:
1. (noun) an act of breaking a law, rule or agreement
Note: Formal.
contexts: This is a clear violation of the law.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a good quality in someone's character
2. (noun) behaviour that is morally good
3. (noun) an advantage or good feature
4. (idiom) (by ~ of) because of
contexts: Patience is a virtue.
She was a woman of great virtue.
The plan has the virtue of being simple.
He got the job by virtue of his experience.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) connected with the voice
2. (adjective) expressing opinions strongly and publicly
3. (noun) (~s) the part of a song that is sung
contexts: The singer has great vocal range.
She's a vocal critic of the government.
She sings the vocals in the band.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) likely to change suddenly and unexpectedly, often getting worse
2. (adjective) (of a person) likely to become angry suddenly
contexts: The situation in the region is very volatile.
He has a volatile temper.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to make a serious promise to do something
2. (noun) a serious promise, especially a religious one
contexts: He vowed never to drink again.
They exchanged their wedding vows.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the state of being easily hurt, attacked or harmed
contexts: The attack showed the vulnerability of the system.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) easily hurt, attacked or harmed, physically or emotionally
contexts: Old people are vulnerable to the cold.

words.definition: 1. (verb) to walk with short steps, moving your body from side to side like a duck
contexts: The ducks waddled across the road.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a large room in a hospital with beds for patients
2. (noun) an area of a city that elects its own representative
3. (noun) a child who is looked after by a guardian or court
4. (phrasal verb) (~ off) to protect yourself from something bad
contexts: She's in the children's ward.
He represents the north ward on the council.
She was made a ward of the court.
He wears a charm to ward off evil.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a large building for storing goods before they are sold or sent somewhere
contexts: The goods are kept in a warehouse.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the activity of fighting a war, especially using particular weapons or methods
2. (noun) fighting or strong competition between groups
contexts: Chemical warfare is banned.
There's open warfare between the two gangs.

words.definition:
1. (noun) an official document from a court that allows the police to do something, such as search a house or arrest someone
2. (verb) to make something necessary or reasonable
Note: Formal.
contexts: The police have a warrant for his arrest.
The situation warrants immediate action.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a brave and experienced soldier or fighter, especially in the past
contexts: The warriors prepared for battle.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) careful because you think there may be a danger or problem
contexts: Be wary of strangers.

words.definition: 1. (verb) to make someone or something less strong or powerful, or to become less strong
contexts: The illness weakened her heart.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to make cloth by crossing threads over and under each other on a machine or by hand
2. (verb) to move quickly in and out between things
3. (verb) to put different stories or ideas together
Note: weave – wove – woven. In the meaning "move in and out", the past is "weaved" or "wove".
contexts: She weaves beautiful carpets.
The motorbike wove through the traffic.
The writer weaves history and fiction together.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a wild plant that grows where it is not wanted, especially in a garden
2. (noun) the illegal drug cannabis
3. (verb) to remove wild plants that are not wanted from the ground
4. (phrasal verb) (~ out) to remove people or things that are not wanted from a group
Note: The drug meaning is informal.
contexts: The garden is full of weeds.
They were smoking weed.
I spent the afternoon weeding the garden.
The test weeds out weak candidates.

words.definition: 1. (adverb) at all (used after a negative to make it stronger)
contexts: I have no idea whatsoever.

words.definition:
1. (adverb) by which, or as a result of which
Note: Formal.
contexts: They set up a system whereby people can vote online.

words.definition:
1. (conjunction) during the time that something happens
2. (conjunction) although, or used to compare two things
Note: Formal, mainly British. Same meaning as "while".
contexts: Please wait whilst I check.
Whilst I agree with you, I think we should wait.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a long piece of leather or rope fixed to a handle, used for hitting animals or people
2. (verb) to hit a person or animal with a long piece of leather or rope
3. (verb) to mix cream or eggs very quickly until they become thick
4. (verb) to move or take something quickly and suddenly
5. (noun) an official in a political party who makes sure members vote the right way
Note: whip – whipped – whipped.
contexts: The rider used a whip.
He whipped the horse.
Whip the cream until it's stiff.
She whipped out her phone.
The party whip ordered everyone to vote.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) connected with selling goods in large amounts to shops and businesses, not to the public
2. (adjective) affecting a very large number of people or things, often in a bad way
3. (adverb) in large amounts to shops and businesses
contexts: They buy flowers at wholesale prices.
There's been a wholesale destruction of the forest.
We buy everything wholesale.

words.definition:
1. (adverb) completely, totally
Note: Formal.
contexts: I'm not wholly convinced.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to become wider, or to make something wider
2. (verb) to become greater or include more, or to make something do this
contexts: They are widening the road.
The gap between rich and poor has widened.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a woman whose husband has died and who has not married again
Note: A man whose wife has died is a widower.
contexts: She's been a widow for ten years.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the distance from one side of something to the other
contexts: The room is four metres in width.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a large natural area with no people, houses or farms
2. (noun) a place that is not looked after and has become wild
contexts: They spent a week in the Alaskan wilderness.
The garden was a wilderness.

words.definition: 1. (noun) the quality of being happy to do something if it is needed
contexts: She showed a willingness to learn.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to relax after a period of work, excitement or stress
2. (phrasal verb) to slowly reduce the activity of a business before closing it
3. (phrasal verb) to open a car window by turning a handle
Note: wind – wound – wound. Here, "wind" rhymes with "find".
contexts: I like to wind down with a bath.
The company is winding down its operations.
She wound down the window.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to find yourself in a particular place or situation at the end of something
2. (phrasal verb) to bring something to an end
3. (phrasal verb) to annoy someone or make a joke to trick them
4. (phrasal verb) to turn a key or handle to make a clock or toy work
Note: wind – wound – wound. Here, "wind" rhymes with "find". "Annoy or trick" is British and informal.
contexts: We got lost and wound up in a village.
Let's wind up the meeting.
Are you winding me up?
Don't forget to wind up the clock.

words.definition: 1. (idiom) to take someone to good restaurants and give them food and drink, often to persuade them or impress them
contexts: The company wined and dined its clients.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a friend who helps you meet someone you are attracted to
2. (noun) a pilot who flies beside and protects another plane
Note: Plural: wingmen. The first meaning is informal.
contexts: Will you be my wingman at the party?
The wingman stayed close to the leader.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the ability to say things that are clever and funny
2. (noun) (~s) the ability to think quickly and clearly
3. (idiom) (at your ~s' end) so worried that you do not know what to do
contexts: She's known for her sharp wit.
Keep your wits about you in the city.
I'm at my wits' end with this child.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the act of taking money out of a bank account
2. (noun) the act of moving soldiers away from a place
3. (noun) the act of no longer taking part in something
4. (noun) the unpleasant effects you feel when you stop taking a drug
contexts: I made a withdrawal from the cash machine.
The withdrawal of troops began in May.
Her withdrawal from the race surprised everyone.
He suffered withdrawal symptoms.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to be strong enough not to be harmed or damaged by something
Note: withstand – withstood – withstood. Formal.
contexts: The building can withstand earthquakes.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to eat food very quickly, in large amounts
Note: Informal.
contexts: He wolfed down his lunch in five minutes.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) to deal with a problem or difficult feeling slowly and carefully
2. (phrasal verb) to continue working without stopping
contexts: She's still working through her grief.
We worked through the night.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to show respect and love for God or a god, for example by praying
2. (verb) to love and admire someone very much

1. (verb) to make an agreement official by signing it or voting for it
Note: ratify – ratified – ratified. Formal.
contexts: Both countries ratified the treaty.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the reasons for a decision, belief or action
Note: Formal.
contexts: What's the rationale behind the new rule?

words.definition:
1. (verb) to speak angrily to someone because they have done something wrong
2. (noun) angry words spoken to someone because they have done something wrong
Note: Formal.
contexts: The teacher rebuked him for being late.
She received a sharp rebuke from her boss.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) given or done in return by both sides
Note: Formal.
contexts: The two countries have a reciprocal agreement.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to make two people or groups become friends again after an argument
2. (verb) to find a way for two different ideas or facts to exist together
3. (phrasal verb) (~ yourself to) to accept a situation you cannot change
contexts: The brothers were finally reconciled.
It's hard to reconcile work and family life.
She reconciled herself to living alone.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to correct something that is wrong
Note: rectify – rectified – rectified. Formal.
contexts: We will rectify the mistake immediately.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to prove that a statement or idea is wrong
2. (verb) to say that something is not true
Note: Formal.
contexts: Scientists refuted his theory.
She refuted the claims against her.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to say something again, to make it clearer or stronger
Note: Formal.
contexts: Let me reiterate: safety comes first.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to give up power, control or a right, often unwillingly
Note: Formal.
contexts: He refused to relinquish control of the company.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) (~ of) making you think of something similar
contexts: The smell was reminiscent of my grandmother's kitchen.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a small part of something that is still there after the rest has gone
2. (noun) a small piece of cloth left at the end of a roll
contexts: The wall is a remnant of the old city.
She made a bag from fabric remnants.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to say formally that you no longer want something, such as a title or right
2. (verb) to say publicly that you no longer believe in something or will no longer do it
Note: Formal.
contexts: He renounced his claim to the throne.
They renounced violence.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to fill something again by replacing what has been used
Note: Formal.
contexts: We need to replenish our food supplies.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to tell someone officially that they have done something wrong
2. (noun) an official statement that someone has done something wrong
Note: Formal.
contexts: The officer was reprimanded for his behaviour.
He received a written reprimand.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) very determined and not willing to change your purpose
Note: Formal.
contexts: She was resolute in her fight for justice.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the return and growth of an activity or belief after a period when it was less common
Note: Formal.
contexts: There has been a resurgence of interest in vinyl records.

words.definition: 1. (verb) to do something harmful to someone because they have harmed you
contexts: The army retaliated with a missile attack.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to respect and admire someone or something very much
Note: Formal.
contexts: He was revered as a national hero.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) very basic or simple
Note: Formal.
contexts: I have only a rudimentary knowledge of Spanish.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to burst or break apart suddenly
2. (noun) a sudden burst or break in something
3. (noun) a sudden end to a good relationship
contexts: The pipe ruptured and flooded the kitchen.
He had a rupture in his stomach.
The argument caused a rupture between the two countries.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) most important or most noticeable
Note: Formal.
contexts: Here are the salient points of the report.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) having practical knowledge and good judgement about something
2. (noun) practical knowledge and ability
Note: Informal.
contexts: She's a savvy businesswoman.
He has a lot of political savvy.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to look at or examine something very carefully
Note: British spelling also: scrutinise.
contexts: The police scrutinized the documents.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) involving a lot of sitting and not much exercise
2. (adjective) (of people or animals) staying in one place, not moving around
Note: Formal.
contexts: Many people have sedentary jobs.
They became a sedentary farming community.

words.definition: 1. (noun) sand, stones or other material that settles at the bottom of a liquid
contexts: There was a layer of sediment at the bottom of the bottle.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) calm, peaceful and not worried
contexts: She had a serene smile on her face.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) clever at understanding situations and people, and making good decisions
contexts: She's a shrewd businesswoman.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) moving, working or reacting more slowly than normal
contexts: The economy is sluggish.

words.definition:
1. (noun) comfort when you are sad or worried
Note: Formal.
contexts: She found solace in music after his death.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) small in number or amount and spread over a large area
contexts: The population is sparse in the north.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) happening sometimes, but not regularly or often
contexts: There has been sporadic fighting in the area.

words.definition: 1. (verb) to waste money, time or chances in a stupid or careless way
contexts: He squandered all his money on gambling.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) (of water or air) not moving and so smelling bad
2. (adjective) not growing, changing or developing
contexts: Mosquitoes breed in stagnant water.
The economy has been stagnant for years.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) very loyal and strong in your support for someone or something
2. (verb) to stop blood from flowing out of a wound
contexts: He's a staunch supporter of the party.
She used a cloth to staunch the bleeding.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) staying firm and loyal to someone or something, and not changing
Note: Formal.
contexts: She remained steadfast in her beliefs.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a strong feeling in society that something is bad or shameful, which is often unfair
contexts: There's still a stigma attached to mental illness.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) (of rules or conditions) very strict and severe
Note: Formal.
contexts: The country has stringent gun laws.

words.definition:
1. (noun) a person who has a lower position than someone else at work
2. (adjective) less important than something else, or lower in rank
3. (verb) to treat something as less important than something else
Note: The noun and adjective end like "it"; the verb ends like "late".
contexts: She treats her subordinates fairly.
All other issues are subordinate to safety.
He subordinated his own needs to his family's.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to pay part of the cost of something so that it is cheaper for people
Note: British spelling also: subsidise.
contexts: The government subsidizes public transport.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to give evidence that proves that something is true
Note: Formal.
contexts: He couldn't substantiate his claims.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) said or written clearly using only a few words
contexts: She gave a succinct summary of the plan.

words.definition:
1. (phrasal verb) (~ to) to stop trying to resist something, such as a feeling or pressure
2. (phrasal verb) (~ to) to die or become very ill from an illness or injury
Note: Formal. The "b" is not pronounced.
contexts: I finally succumbed to temptation and ate the cake.
He succumbed to cancer.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) more than is needed or wanted
Note: Formal.
contexts: Delete any superfluous words from your essay.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to take the place of something older or less modern
Note: Formal.
contexts: The old system has been superseded by computers.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) (~ to) easily influenced, affected or harmed by something
contexts: Children are susceptible to infections.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the extra energy or success that comes when two or more people or organizations work together
Note: Formal.
contexts: There's great synergy between the two teams.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a person's usual character and the way they feel and behave
contexts: She has a calm temperament.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) very determined and not giving up easily
2. (adjective) holding something very firmly
contexts: He's a tenacious defender.
The baby had a tenacious grip on my finger.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) not certain or final, and may be changed later
2. (adjective) done in a careful way that shows you are not confident
contexts: We made tentative plans to meet next week.
She took a few tentative steps.

words.definition:
1. (noun) the curved path that a moving object follows through the air
2. (noun) the way that something develops over time
Note: Formal.
contexts: They calculated the trajectory of the rocket.
Her career has followed an upward trajectory.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) quiet, calm and peaceful, without noise or worry
contexts: We stayed in a tranquil village by the lake.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to go beyond the usual limits of something
Note: Formal.
contexts: Music transcends language barriers.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) lasting or staying only for a short time
2. (noun) a person who stays in a place for only a short time
Note: Formal.
contexts: The city has a transient population of students.
The hostel is full of transients.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) seeming to be everywhere
Note: Formal.
contexts: Smartphones are now ubiquitous.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) agreed by everyone in a group
contexts: The decision was unanimous.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to be the real cause or basis of something, although it is not obvious
Note: underlie – underlay – underlain. Formal.
contexts: Poverty underlies many health problems.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to support or form the basis of an idea, argument or system
Note: underpin – underpinned – underpinned. Formal.
contexts: Trust underpins every good relationship.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) done by one person, group or country without the agreement of others
Note: Formal.
contexts: The country made a unilateral decision to leave.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) willing to act in a dishonest or unfair way to get what you want
contexts: Unscrupulous landlords charge very high rents.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) not necessary, deserved or reasonable
Note: Formal.
contexts: The criticism was unwarranted.

words.definition: 1. (noun) a big change that causes a lot of confusion, worry or problems
contexts: Moving house is a big upheaval.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) the greatest possible
2. (noun) (the ~) the greatest amount possible
Note: Formal.
contexts: This is a matter of the utmost importance.
She did her utmost to help.

words.definition: 1. (adjective) watching carefully for possible danger or problems
contexts: Police asked people to remain vigilant.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to prove that someone was right, or that they were not guilty
Note: Formal.
contexts: The new evidence vindicated him.

words.definition:
1. (verb) to slowly become weaker or less important
2. (verb) (of the moon) to appear smaller each night
3. (idiom) (on the ~) becoming weaker or less popular
contexts: Interest in the show began to wane.
The moon is waning.
His power is on the wane.

words.definition:
1. (adjective) good for your health
2. (adjective) morally good and suitable for everyone
contexts: They eat simple, wholesome food.
It's a wholesome family film.

words.definition: 1. (noun) great energy and enthusiasm for something you believe in
contexts: She works with missionary zeal.
